name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT_Q08 - Abnormal molar mass and van t Hoff factor calculation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a solute undergoes dissociation in solution, the experimentally measured molar mass is smaller than its normal molar mass, and the van 't Hoff factor (i) is greater than 1.

Statement II: For an electrolyte that dissociates into n ions with a degree of dissociation α, the van 't Hoff factor is related by i = 1 + (n - 1)α.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब कोई विलेय विलयन में वियोजित होता है, तो प्रायोगिक रूप से मापा गया मोलर द्रव्यमान उसके सामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान से कम होता है, और वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (i) का मान 1 से अधिक होता है।

कथन II: एक विद्युत-अपघट्य के लिए जो वियोजन की मात्रा α के साथ n आयनों में वियोजित होता है, वान्ट हॉफ गुणक i = 1 + (n - 1)α द्वारा संबंधित होता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The van 't Hoff factor (\(i\)) accounts for the association or dissociation of solute particles and is defined as: \[ i = \frac{\text{Normal molar mass}}{\text{Abnormal (observed) molar mass}} = \frac{\text{Observed colligative property}}{\text{Calculated colligative property}} \]

Step 2: Dissociation and Observed Molar Mass
When an electrolyte dissociates, the total number of solute particles increases. Because colligative properties are directly proportional to particle count, the observed colligative effect is larger than expected. Since molar mass is inversely proportional to the colligative property: \[ M_{\text{observed}} = \frac{M_{\text{normal}}}{i} \] With particle multiplication, \(i > 1\), which makes \(M_{\text{observed}} < M_{\text{normal}}\). Thus, the first proposition is valid.

Step 3: Derivation of the Mathematical Expression
Consider 1 mole of an electrolyte \(A_x B_y\) that yields \(n\) ions upon dissociation with a degree of dissociation \(\alpha\): \[ A_x B_y \rightleftharpoons n\,\text{ions} \] At equilibrium: - Moles of undissociated electrolyte = \(1 - \alpha\) - Moles of ions produced = \(n\alpha\) - Total moles of particles at equilibrium = \((1 - \alpha) + n\alpha = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha\) By definition, the van 't Hoff factor is: \[ i = \frac{\text{Total particles after dissociation}}{\text{Initial particles}} = \frac{1 + (n - 1)\alpha}{1} = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha \] This algebraic relation is exact, verifying that the second proposition is also correct.

Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (\(i\)) विलेय कणों के संगुणन या वियोजन को ध्यान में रखता है और इसे निम्न रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है: \[ i = \frac{\text{सामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान}}{\text{असामान्य (प्रेक्षित) मोलर द्रव्यमान}} = \frac{\text{प्रेक्षित अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म}}{\text{परिकलित अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म}} \]

चरण 2: वियोजन और प्रेक्षित मोलर द्रव्यमान
जब कोई विद्युत-अपघट्य वियोजित होता है, तो विलेय कणों की कुल संख्या बढ़ जाती है। चूंकि अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म कणों की संख्या के समानुपाती होते हैं, इसलिए प्रेक्षित अणुसंख्य प्रभाव सामान्य से बड़ा होता है। चूंकि मोलर द्रव्यमान अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है: \[ M_{\text{प्रेक्षित}} = \frac{M_{\text{सामान्य}}}{i} \] कणों की संख्या बढ़ने पर \(i > 1\) होता है, जिससे \(M_{\text{प्रेक्षित}} < M_{\text{सामान्य}}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 3: गणितीय व्यंजक का निगमन
1 मोल विद्युत-अपघट्य पर विचार करें जो \(\alpha\) वियोजन की मात्रा के साथ \(n\) आयन देता है: साम्यावस्था पर: - अवियोजित विलेय के मोल = \(1 - \alpha\) - उत्पन्न आयनों के मोल = \(n\alpha\) - कुल कणों के मोल = \((1 - \alpha) + n\alpha = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha\) परिभाषा के अनुसार: \[ i = \frac{1 + (n - 1)\alpha}{1} = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha \] यह संबंध पूर्णतः सटीक है। अतः दोनों कथन सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Henrys law and its biological applications

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: To avoid the painful and dangerous medical condition known as bends, scuba divers use breathing tanks filled with air diluted with helium.

Statement II: At high altitudes, the partial pressure of oxygen is lower than that at ground level, leading to low oxygen concentrations in blood and tissues (anoxia).

Statement III: To increase the solubility of carbon dioxide in soft drinks and soda water, bottles are sealed under very low pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बेंड्स (bends) नामक दर्दनाक और खतरनाक चिकित्सीय स्थिति से बचने के लिए, स्कूबा गोताखोर हीलियम से तनु की गई वायु से भरे सिलेंडरों का उपयोग करते हैं।

कथन II: अधिक ऊंचाई पर, ऑक्सीजन का आंशिक दाब जमीनी स्तर की तुलना में कम होता है, जिससे रक्त और ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की सांद्रता कम हो जाती है (एनोक्सिया)।

कथन III: शीतल पेयों और सोडा जल में कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड की विलेयता बढ़ाने के लिए, बोतलों को बहुत कम दाब पर सील किया जाता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas above the liquid surface: \[ p = K_{\text{H}} \, x \] where \(p\) is the partial pressure and \(x\) is the mole fraction of the dissolved gas.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First and Second Propositions
Deep underwater, high hydrostatic pressure increases the solubility of atmospheric gases in the blood of divers. During rapid ascent, pressure decreases and nitrogen bubbles out of solution, blocking capillaries and causing decompression sickness (bends). Diluting breathing air with helium (which has very low blood solubility) prevents bends. At high altitudes, low atmospheric oxygen partial pressure reduces oxygen saturation in blood tissues, causing cognitive and physical impairment known as anoxia. Thus, the first and second propositions are scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
According to Henry's law, increasing the partial pressure of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) increases its dissolved concentration in water. Therefore, soda water and soft drink bottles are sealed under high pressure, not low pressure. Hence, the third proposition is false.

Final Answer: Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
हेनरी के नियम के अनुसार, किसी द्रव में गैस की विलेयता द्रव की सतह के ऊपर गैस के आंशिक दाब के समानुपाती होती है: \[ p = K_{\text{H}} \, x \] जहाँ \(p\) आंशिक दाब है और \(x\) घुली हुई गैस का मोल अंश है।

चरण 2: पहले और दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
पानी के भीतर अत्यधिक दाब के कारण गोताखोरों के रक्त में वायुमंडलीय गैसों की विलेयता बढ़ जाती है। ऊपर आते समय दाब घटने पर नाइट्रोजन के बुलबुले बनते हैं, जो केशिकाओं को अवरुद्ध कर बेंड्स (bends) उत्पन्न करते हैं। हीलियम मिलाकर वायु को तनु करने से यह समस्या रुकती है। अधिक ऊंचाई पर ऑक्सीजन का आंशिक दाब कम होने से रक्त में ऑक्सीजन घटती है, जिसे एनोक्सिया कहते हैं। अतः पहला और दूसरा कथन सही हैं।

चरण 3: तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
हेनरी के नियम के अनुसार, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) का आंशिक दाब बढ़ाने पर जल में इसकी विलेयता बढ़ती है। इसलिए शीतल पेयों की बोतलों को उच्च दाब पर सील किया जाता है, कम दाब पर नहीं। अतः तीसरा कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statements II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Deviations from Raoults law and azeotropes

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In solutions showing positive deviation from Raoult's law, solute-solvent (A-B) intermolecular forces are weaker than A-A and B-B interactions.

Statement II: A mixture of ethanol and acetone exhibits positive deviation from Raoult's law and forms a minimum boiling azeotrope.

Statement III: The dissolution of acetone in ethanol is an exothermic process accompanied by contraction in total volume.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन प्रदर्शित करने वाले विलयनों में, विलेय-विलायक (A-B) अंतराआण्विक बल A-A और B-B अन्योन्यक्रियाओं से दुर्बल होते हैं।

कथन II: एथेनॉल और एसीटोन का मिश्रण राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन प्रदर्शित करता है और एक न्यूनतम क्वथनांक स्थिरक्वाथी बनाता है।

कथन III: एथेनॉल में एसीटोन का घुलना एक ऊष्माक्षेपी प्रक्रम है जिसके साथ कुल आयतन में संकुचन होता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Positive deviation from Raoult's law occurs when the total vapour pressure exceeds the ideal Raoult's law value: \[ p_A > p_A^\circ x_A \quad \text{and} \quad p_B > p_B^\circ x_B \] This condition arises when unlike molecular interactions (\(\text{A-B}\)) are weaker than like molecular interactions (\(\text{A-A}\) and \(\text{B-B}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First and Second Propositions
In pure ethanol, molecules are held by extensive hydrogen bonding. Adding acetone introduces molecules that disrupt these hydrogen bonds without forming equally strong bonds in return. Thus, \(\text{A-B}\) interactions are weaker, enabling both components to escape more readily into the vapour phase. Mixtures exhibiting large positive deviations from Raoult's law show a maximum in the vapour pressure curve, which corresponds to a minimum boiling azeotrope. Hence, the first and second propositions are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Because energy is required to break the stronger hydrogen bonds in pure ethanol compared to the weaker interactions formed with acetone, mixing is endothermic (\(\Delta_{\text{mix}}H > 0\)). Furthermore, the weaker interactions result in a slight expansion of volume upon mixing (\(\Delta_{\text{mix}}V > 0\)), not contraction. Therefore, the third proposition is false.

Final Answer: Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन तब होता है जब कुल वाष्प दाब आदर्श मान से अधिक होता है: \[ p_A > p_A^\circ x_A \quad \text{तथा} \quad p_B > p_B^\circ x_B \] यह तब होता है जब भिन्न अणुओं के बीच आकर्षण बल (\(\text{A-B}\)) समान अणुओं के बीच के आकर्षण बलों (\(\text{A-A}\) और \(\text{B-B}\)) से दुर्बल होते हैं।

चरण 2: पहले और दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
शुद्ध एथेनॉल में हाइड्रोजन आबंधन होता है। एसीटोन मिलाने पर ये हाइड्रोजन आबंध टूटते हैं और दुर्बल \(\text{A-B}\) अन्योन्यक्रियाएं बनती हैं, जिससे अणुओं की पलायन प्रवृत्ति बढ़ जाती है। व्यापक धनात्मक विचलन वाले मिश्रण अधिकतम वाष्प दाब बिंदु पर एक न्यूनतम क्वथनांक स्थिरक्वाथी (minimum boiling azeotrope) बनाते हैं। अतः पहला और दूसरा कथन सही हैं।

चरण 3: तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
मजबूत हाइड्रोजन आबंधों को तोड़ने के लिए ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है, इसलिए मिश्रण प्रक्रम ऊष्माशोषी (\(\Delta_{\text{mix}}H > 0\)) होता है और आयतन में प्रसार (\(\Delta_{\text{mix}}V > 0\)) होता है, संकुचन नहीं। अतः तीसरा कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct.
Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statements II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Osmotic pressure and membrane phenomena

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Osmotic pressure of a dilute solution is directly proportional to its molar concentration at a given absolute temperature.

Statement II: Osmotic pressure is widely preferred over other colligative properties for determining the molar masses of biomolecules because its magnitude is easily measurable even at very low molar concentrations.

Statement III: In reverse osmosis used for seawater desalination, applying a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure forces pure water to flow from the salt water through a semipermeable membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक निश्चित परम तापमान पर किसी तनु विलयन का परासरण दाब उसकी मोलर सांद्रता के अनुक्रमानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: जैव-अणुओं के मोलर द्रव्यमान ज्ञात करने के लिए अन्य अणुसंख्य गुणधर्मों की तुलना में परासरण दाब को प्राथमिकता दी जाती है क्योंकि अत्यंत कम मोलर सांद्रता पर भी इसका मान आसानी से मापने योग्य होता है।

कथन III: समुद्री जल के विलवणीकरण में प्रयुक्त व्युत्क्रम परासरण में, परासरण दाब से अधिक दाब लगाने पर शुद्ध जल लवणीय जल से अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली के माध्यम से प्रवाहित होता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For dilute solutions of non-electrolytes, osmotic pressure (\(\Pi\)) is described by van 't Hoff's equation: \[ \Pi = C R T = \frac{n_2}{V} R T \] where \(C\) is molarity, \(R\) is the universal gas constant, and \(T\) is absolute temperature in kelvin.

Step 2: Evaluation of Molar Mass Determination of Biomolecules
Macromolecules such as proteins and polymers have high molar masses, meaning that a measurable mass dissolved in a liter produces an extremely small molarity (\(\approx 10^{-4}\text{ to } 10^{-5}\text{ M}\)). For such dilute solutions, freezing point depression and boiling point elevation are less than \(10^{-3}\text{ K}\), which is difficult to measure accurately. In contrast, osmotic pressure for a \(10^{-3}\text{ M}\) solution at room temperature is approximately \(250\text{ mm of water}\), which is easily and precisely measured using a manometer without exposing sensitive biomolecules to thermal degradation.

Step 3: Evaluation of Reverse Osmosis
When a mechanical pressure exceeding the osmotic pressure of seawater is applied on the saltwater side of a semipermeable membrane (such as cellulose acetate), chemical potential gradients invert, forcing pure water molecules to pass through the membrane while dissolved ions are retained. Hence, all three propositions are scientifically sound.

Final Answer: Statements I, II and III are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
विद्युत-अनअपघट्यों के तनु विलयनों के लिए परासरण दाब (\(\Pi\)) वान्ट हॉफ समीकरण द्वारा दिया जाता है: \[ \Pi = C R T = \frac{n_2}{V} R T \] जहाँ \(C\) मोलरता है, \(R\) सार्वत्रिक गैस नियतांक है, और \(T\) केल्विन में परम तापमान है।

चरण 2: जैव-अणुओं के मोलर द्रव्यमान निर्धारण का मूल्यांकन
प्रोटीन और बहुलक जैसे वृहदाणुओं का मोलर द्रव्यमान बहुत अधिक होता है, जिससे उनकी मोलरता बहुत कम (\(\approx 10^{-4}\text{ से } 10^{-5}\text{ M}\)) होती है। इतनी कम सांद्रता पर क्वथनांक उन्नयन और हिमांक अवनमन \(10^{-3}\text{ K}\) से भी कम होते हैं जिन्हें मापना कठिन होता है। इसके विपरीत, कमरे के तापमान पर परासरण दाब लगभग \(250\text{ mm जल स्तंभ}\) होता है जिसे मैनोमीटर द्वारा आसानी से मापा जा सकता है।

चरण 3: व्युत्क्रम परासरण का मूल्यांकन
जब लवणीय जल की ओर परासरण दाब से अधिक बाह्य दाब लगाया जाता है, तो जल के अणु अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली (जैसे सेलुलोज एसीटेट) के माध्यम से शुद्ध जल की ओर प्रवाहित होने लगते हैं जबकि लवण के आयन रुक जाते हैं। अतः तीनों कथन पूर्णतः सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT3_Q04 - van t Hoff factor and electrolyte dissociation

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: When a solute undergoes association in solution, its van 't Hoff factor (i) is greater than 1, causing the experimentally observed molar mass to be lower than the normal molar mass.

Statement II: For an electrolyte that dissociates into n ions with a degree of dissociation α, the van 't Hoff factor is related by i = 1 + (n - 1)α.

Statement III: For strong electrolytes like potassium sulphate (K_2SO_4), the value of i approaches 3.00 only as the solution becomes extremely dilute.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब कोई विलेय विलयन में संगुणित होता है, तो उसका वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (i) 1 से अधिक होता है, जिससे प्रायोगिक रूप से प्रेक्षित मोलर द्रव्यमान सामान्य मान से कम हो जाता है।

कथन II: एक विद्युत-अपघट्य के लिए जो वियोजन की मात्रा α के साथ n आयनों में वियोजित होता है, वान्ट हॉफ गुणक i = 1 + (n - 1)α द्वारा संबंधित होता है।

कथन III: पोटेशियम सल्फेट (K_2SO_4) जैसे प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए, i का मान केवल तभी 3.00 के करीब पहुंचता है जब विलयन अत्यंत तनु हो जाता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The van 't Hoff factor (\(i\)) is defined as: \[ i = \frac{\text{Normal molar mass}}{\text{Observed molar mass}} = \frac{\text{Observed colligative property}}{\text{Calculated colligative property}} \]

Step 2: Evaluation of Association and Molar Mass
During association (such as benzoic acid forming dimers in benzene), the number of particles in solution decreases. Therefore, the observed colligative property decreases, giving \(i < 1\). Because observed molar mass is inversely proportional to the colligative property: \[ M_{\text{observed}} = \frac{M_{\text{normal}}}{i} \] A value of \(i < 1\) results in \(M_{\text{observed}} > M_{\text{normal}}\). Claiming that association gives \(i > 1\) and a lower observed molar mass is completely erroneous. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Dissociation Relations
Consider 1 mole of an electrolyte dissociating into \(n\) ions with degree of dissociation \(\alpha\): \[ \text{Total moles of particles at equilibrium} = (1 - \alpha) + n\alpha = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha \] By definition, \(i = \frac{1 + (n - 1)\alpha}{1} = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha\). For strong electrolytes such as \(\mathrm{K_2SO_4}\) (\(n = 3\)), interionic electrostatic attractions at moderate concentrations (e.g., \(0.1\text{ m}\)) cause ion pairing, yielding an experimental \(i \approx 2.32\). Only at infinite dilution (\(\approx 0.001\text{ m}\) and beyond) do interionic forces become negligible, allowing \(i\) to approach its theoretical limit of \(3.00\). Therefore, the second and third propositions are valid.

Final Answer: Statements II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (\(i\)) को निम्न रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है: \[ i = \frac{\text{सामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान}}{\text{प्रेक्षित मोलर द्रव्यमान}} = \frac{\text{प्रेक्षित अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म}}{\text{परिकलित अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म}} \]

चरण 2: संगुणन और मोलर द्रव्यमान का मूल्यांकन
संगुणन के दौरान (जैसे बेन्जीन में बेन्जोइक अम्ल का द्वितयीकरण), विलयन में कणों की संख्या घट जाती है, जिससे \(i < 1\) होता है। चूंकि प्रेक्षित मोलर द्रव्यमान अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है: \[ M_{\text{प्रेक्षित}} = \frac{M_{\text{सामान्य}}}{i} \] \(i < 1\) होने पर \(M_{\text{प्रेक्षित}} > M_{\text{सामान्य}}\) प्राप्त होता है। यह दावा करना कि संगुणन में \(i > 1\) होता है और मोलर द्रव्यमान घटता है, पूर्णतः गलत है। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: वियोजन संबंधों का मूल्यांकन
1 मोल विद्युत-अपघट्य के लिए जो \(\alpha\) वियोजन की मात्रा के साथ \(n\) आयन देता है, साम्यावस्था पर कुल कण \(1 + (n - 1)\alpha\) होते हैं, जिससे \(i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha\) प्राप्त होता है। \(\mathrm{K_2SO_4}\) (\(n = 3\)) जैसे प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य में \(0.1\text{ m}\) पर अंतर-आयनिक आकर्षण के कारण \(i \approx 2.32\) होता है, और केवल अत्यंत तनु विलयनों में ही यह मान \(3.00\) के करीब पहुँचता है। अतः दूसरा और तीसरा कथन सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct.
Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statements II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT4_Q01 - Concentration units solubility and vapour pressure relationships

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Molarity and volume percentage of a solution vary with temperature because liquid volume expands or contracts with temperature changes.

Statement II: Molality and mole fraction are independent of temperature because they are defined exclusively in terms of mass.

Statement III: The value of Henry's law constant (K_H) increases with an increase in temperature, indicating that the solubility of gases in liquids decreases with rising temperature.

Statement IV: The vapour pressure of a liquid solvent increases when a non-volatile solute is dissolved in it at a given temperature.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी विलयन की मोलरता और आयतन प्रतिशत तापमान के साथ परिवर्तित होते हैं क्योंकि तापमान में परिवर्तन के साथ द्रव का आयतन प्रसारित या संकुचित होता है।

कथन II: मोललता और मोल अंश तापमान से स्वतंत्र होते हैं क्योंकि वे विशेष रूप से द्रव्यमान के संदर्भ में परिभाषित होते हैं।

कथन III: हेनरी नियम स्थिरांक (K_H) का मान तापमान बढ़ने के साथ बढ़ता है, जो यह दर्शाता है कि बढ़ते तापमान के साथ द्रवों में गैसों की विलेयता घटती है।

कथन IV: एक निश्चित तापमान पर जब किसी द्रव विलायक में एक अवाष्पशील विलेय घोला जाता है, तो उसका वाष्प दाब बढ़ जाता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Concentration units involving solution volume depend on temperature because liquid density is temperature-sensitive, whereas units based strictly on mass remain constant. Gas solubility is governed by Henry's law: \[ p = K_{\text{H}} \, x \implies x = \frac{p}{K_{\text{H}}} \] Vapour pressure of a liquid solution is determined by the escaping tendency of volatile solvent molecules from the liquid surface.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First, Second, and Third Propositions
- Molarity (\(M = \frac{n}{V}\)) and volume percentage contain volume terms; since thermal expansion changes volume, both change with temperature. - Molality (\(m = \frac{n}{w_{\text{solvent}}}\)) and mole fraction (\(x_i = \frac{n_i}{\sum n_i}\)) depend exclusively on mass and mole numbers, which do not change with temperature. - The dissolution of gases in liquids is an exothermic process (\(\Delta_{\text{sol}}H < 0\)). As temperature increases, equilibrium shifts to favour the gas phase, decreasing solubility and causing \(K_{\text{H}}\) to increase. Thus, the first, second, and third propositions are scientifically valid.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Fourth Proposition
When a non-volatile solute is added to a volatile solvent, solute particles occupy a portion of the liquid surface, decreasing the surface area available for solvent vaporization. Consequently, the escaping tendency of solvent molecules is reduced, leading to a lowering of vapour pressure (\(p < p^\circ\)). Claiming that vapour pressure increases is incorrect. Hence, the fourth proposition is false.

Final Answer: Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
विलयन के आयतन पर आधारित सांद्रता इकाइयाँ तापमान पर निर्भर करती हैं क्योंकि द्रव का घनत्व तापमान के साथ बदलता है, जबकि द्रव्यमान पर आधारित इकाइयाँ स्थिर रहती हैं। गैस की विलेयता हेनरी के नियम द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है: \[ p = K_{\text{H}} \, x \implies x = \frac{p}{K_{\text{H}}} \] द्रव विलयन का वाष्प दाब द्रव की सतह से वाष्पशील विलायक अणुओं की पलायन प्रवृत्ति पर निर्भर करता है।

चरण 2: पहले, दूसरे और तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
- मोलरता (\(M = \frac{n}{V}\)) और आयतन प्रतिशत में आयतन शामिल होता है; चूंकि तापीय प्रसार आयतन को बदलता है, इसलिए दोनों तापमान के साथ बदलते हैं। - मोललता और मोल अंश केवल द्रव्यमान और मोलों की संख्या पर निर्भर करते हैं, जो तापमान से अप्रभावित रहते हैं। - द्रवों में गैसों का घुलना ऊष्माक्षेपी प्रक्रम (\(\Delta_{\text{sol}}H < 0\)) है। तापमान बढ़ने पर विलेयता घटती है और \(K_{\text{H}}\) बढ़ता है। अतः पहला, दूसरा और तीसरा कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं।

चरण 3: चौथे कथन का मूल्यांकन
जब किसी वाष्पशील विलायक में एक अवाष्पशील विलेय मिलाया जाता है, तो विलेय के कण सतह के कुछ भाग को घेर लेते हैं, जिससे विलायक के वाष्पीकरण के लिए उपलब्ध पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल घट जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, वाष्प दाब कम हो जाता है (\(p < p^\circ\))। यह दावा करना कि वाष्प दाब बढ़ता है, गलत है। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and IV are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.
Statements II and IV are correct, but Statements I and III are incorrect.
Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_STATEMENT4_Q02 - Thermodynamics of ideal solutions deviations and association

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: For an ideal binary solution of components A and B, the enthalpy of mixing (Δ_mix H) and volume of mixing (Δ_mix V) are both zero because A-B intermolecular attractions are nearly equal to A-A and B-B interactions.

Statement II: A mixture of chloroform and acetone shows negative deviation from Raoult's law due to the formation of a hydrogen bond between the hydrogen atom of chloroform and the oxygen atom of acetone.

Statement III: Colligative properties of dilute solutions depend strictly on the total number of solute particles in solution relative to total particles, regardless of their chemical identity.

Statement IV: When ethanoic acid undergoes complete dimerisation in benzene, the van 't Hoff factor (i) is 2.0 and the experimentally determined molar mass is half of its normal molar mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: घटकों A और B के एक आदर्श द्विअंगी विलयन के लिए, मिश्रण की एन्थैल्पी (Δ_mix H) और मिश्रण का आयतन (Δ_mix V) दोनों शून्य होते हैं क्योंकि A-B अंतराआण्विक आकर्षण बल A-A और B-B आकर्षण बलों के लगभग समान होते हैं।

कथन II: क्लोरोफॉर्म और एसीटोन का मिश्रण राउल्ट के नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन प्रदर्शित करता है क्योंकि क्लोरोफॉर्म के हाइड्रोजन परमाणु और एसीटोन के ऑक्सीजन परमाणु के बीच एक हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनता है।

कथन III: तनु विलयनों के अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म केवल विलेय कणों की कुल संख्या पर निर्भर करते हैं, उनकी रासायनिक पहचान से स्वतंत्र होते हैं।

कथन IV: जब एथेनोइक अम्ल बेन्जीन में पूर्णतः द्वितयीकृत होता है, तो वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (i) 2.0 होता है और प्रायोगिक रूप से निर्धारित मोलर द्रव्यमान इसके सामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान का आधा होता है।

उपरोक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ideal solution thermodynamics requires: \[ \Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0 \] arising from equal intermolecular cohesive forces (\(\text{A-B} \approx \text{A-A} \approx \text{B-B}\)). In non-ideal solutions, new specific interactions such as hydrogen bonding produce negative deviations. Colligative properties depend solely on solute particle count, and association or dissociation is quantified through the van 't Hoff factor: \[ i = \frac{\text{Normal molar mass}}{\text{Observed molar mass}} \]

Step 2: Evaluation of the First, Second, and Third Propositions
- In an ideal solution, energy required to disrupt \(\text{A-A}\) and \(\text{B-B}\) interactions equals energy released in forming \(\text{A-B}\) interactions, ensuring zero net heat exchange and no volume change upon mixing. - In a chloroform-acetone mixture, the acidic hydrogen of \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\) forms a strong hydrogen bond with the carbonyl oxygen of \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CO}\): \[ \mathrm{Cl_3C-H}\cdots\mathrm{O=C(CH_3)_2} \] Because \(\text{A-B}\) interactions are stronger than cohesive forces in the pure liquids, the escaping tendency is reduced, producing negative deviation from Raoult's law. - Colligative properties depend exclusively on the ratio of solute particles to total particles, irrespective of particle charge, size, or identity. Thus, the first, second, and third propositions are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Fourth Proposition
When ethanoic acid undergoes complete dimerisation in benzene: \[ 2\,\mathrm{CH_3COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\mathrm{CH_3COOH})_2 \] Two formula units associate into one dimer particle, reducing the total number of particles by half. Consequently: \[ i = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5 \] Since observed molar mass is: \[ M_{\text{observed}} = \frac{M_{\text{normal}}}{i} = \frac{60\text{ g mol}^{-1}}{0.5} = 120\text{ g mol}^{-1} \] The experimentally measured molar mass is double (twice) the normal molar mass, not half. Therefore, the fourth proposition is false.

Final Answer: Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
आदर्श विलयन ऊष्मागतिकी के अनुसार: \[ \Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0 \quad \text{तथा} \quad \Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0 \] यह तब होता है जब समान और भिन्न अणुओं के बीच आकर्षण बल समान होते हैं (\(\text{A-B} \approx \text{A-A} \approx \text{B-B}\))। अन-आदर्श विलयनों में नए अंतराआण्विक आबंध (जैसे हाइड्रोजन आबंधन) ऋणात्मक विचलन उत्पन्न करते हैं। अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म केवल विलेय कणों की संख्या पर निर्भर करते हैं, और वान्ट हॉफ गुणक निम्न प्रकार परिभाषित है: \[ i = \frac{\text{सामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान}}{\text{प्रेक्षित मोलर द्रव्यमान}} \]

चरण 2: पहले, दूसरे और तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
- आदर्श विलयन में \(\text{A-A}\) और \(\text{B-B}\) आकर्षणों को तोड़ने में लगी ऊर्जा नए \(\text{A-B}\) आकर्षणों के बनने पर उत्सर्जित ऊर्जा के बराबर होती है, जिससे \(\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0\) और \(\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0\) प्राप्त होता है। - क्लोरोफॉर्म और एसीटोन के मिश्रण में, क्लोरोफॉर्म का हाइड्रोजन परमाणु एसीटोन के कार्बोनिल ऑक्सीजन के साथ एक मजबूत अंतराआण्विक हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनाता है: \[ \mathrm{Cl_3C-H}\cdots\mathrm{O=C(CH_3)_2} \] यह \(\text{A-B}\) आकर्षण शुद्ध घटकों से मजबूत होने के कारण वाष्प दाब में कमी (ऋणात्मक विचलन) आती है। - अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म केवल विलेय कणों की संख्या पर निर्भर करते हैं, उनकी रासायनिक प्रकृति पर नहीं। अतः पहला, दूसरा और तीसरा कथन सत्य हैं।

चरण 3: चौथे कथन का मूल्यांकन
जब एथेनोइक अम्ल बेन्जीन में पूर्णतः द्वितयीकृत होता है: \[ 2\,\mathrm{CH_3COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\mathrm{CH_3COOH})_2 \] कणों की कुल संख्या आधी रह जाती है, जिससे वान्ट हॉफ गुणक: \[ i = 0.5 \] होता है। चूंकि: \[ M_{\text{प्रेक्षित}} = \frac{M_{\text{सामान्य}}}{i} = \frac{60\text{ g mol}^{-1}}{0.5} = 120\text{ g mol}^{-1} \] अतः प्रायोगिक रूप से निर्धारित मोलर द्रव्यमान सामान्य मान से दोगुना होता है, आधा नहीं। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and IV are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements II, III and IV are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II and III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q01 - Types of solutions and their examples

questiontext.text:
Match the types of solutions in Column I with their corresponding examples in Column II:

Column I (Type of Solution) Column II (Example)
(A) Gas in solid (I) Camphor in nitrogen gas
(B) Solid in gas (II) Solution of hydrogen in palladium
(C) Liquid in solid (III) Chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas
(D) Liquid in gas (IV) Amalgam of mercury with sodium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
Gas in solid represents a solution where the solvent is a solid and the solute is a gas; a classic textbook example is a solution of hydrogen in palladium, where hydrogen gas atoms occupy interstitial sites within the solid palladium metal lattice.

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
Solid in gas represents a solution where the solvent is a gas and the solute is a solid; camphor in nitrogen gas represents this type, as solid camphor particles sublime directly into nitrogen gas.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Liquid in solid represents a solution where the solvent is a solid and the solute is a liquid; an amalgam of mercury with sodium is a homogeneous solid solution where liquid mercury is dispersed throughout solid sodium.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Liquid in gas represents a solution where the solvent is a gas and the solute is a liquid; chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas is an example where liquid chloroform evaporates and disperses into nitrogen gas.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Gas in solid pairs with solution of hydrogen in palladium; solid in gas pairs with camphor in nitrogen gas; liquid in solid pairs with amalgam of mercury with sodium; and liquid in gas pairs with chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q02 - Concentration units and their defining expressions

questiontext.text:
Match the concentration expressions in Column I with their corresponding units or characteristics in Column II:

Column I (Concentration Term) Column II (Unit or Characteristic)
(A) Molarity (I) Dimensionless quantity with no units
(B) Molality (II) \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) (dependent on temperature)
(C) Mole fraction (III) Ratio of parts of solute per \(10^6\) parts of solution
(D) Parts per million (IV) \(\text{mol kg}^{-1}\) (independent of temperature)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
Molarity is defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution; its unit is \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) or \(\text{mol dm}^{-3}\), and because volume changes with expansion or contraction of liquid, it is temperature dependent.

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
Molality is defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved per kilogram of solvent; its unit is \(\text{mol kg}^{-1}\), and since mass does not change with temperature, molality is independent of temperature.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Mole fraction is the ratio of the number of moles of a specific component to the total number of moles of all components present in the mixture; being a ratio of identical quantities (moles to moles), it is a dimensionless quantity without units.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Parts per million (ppm) is used to express concentrations of trace solutes and represents the ratio of parts of solute per \(10^6\) (one million) parts of solution, useful for atmospheric pollutants or water hardness.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Molarity pairs with moles per litre (temperature dependent); molality pairs with moles per kilogram (temperature independent); mole fraction pairs with dimensionless quantity with no units; and parts per million pairs with ratio of parts of solute per million parts of solution.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q03 - Everyday applications governed by Henry law

questiontext.text:
Match the physiological or industrial phenomena in Column I with their governing Henry's law explanations in Column II:

Column I (Phenomenon) Column II (Governing Mechanism)
(A) Carbonated beverage bottle opening (I) Henry's constant increases with temperature, decreasing oxygen solubility
(B) Decompression sickness in deep-sea divers (II) High pressure during bottling increases gas solubility, escaping at atmospheric pressure
(C) Mental confusion and anoxia in mountaineers (III) Dissolved nitrogen forms bubbles in blood capillaries upon rapid ascent
(D) Thermal pollution harming aquatic life (IV) Low atmospheric partial pressure leads to inadequate blood oxygen levels

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
Carbonated beverage bottles are sealed under high pressure to increase the solubility of carbon dioxide according to Henry's law; opening the bottle releases the pressure, decreasing gas solubility and causing gas bubbles to effervesce.

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
Deep-sea divers breathe air under high hydrostatic pressure, causing excess nitrogen to dissolve in blood; rapid ascent causes decompression where dissolved nitrogen escapes rapidly to form gas bubbles that block capillaries, producing bends or decompression sickness.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
At high altitudes, the atmospheric pressure and hence partial pressure of oxygen is much lower than at sea level, resulting in low oxygen concentration in blood and tissues of climbers, causing weakness and poor mental function known as anoxia.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Dissolution of gases in liquids is an exothermic process, which means the Henry's law constant increases with rising temperature and gas solubility decreases; warm water discharged as thermal pollution contains less dissolved oxygen, endangering aquatic life.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Carbonated beverage bottle opening pairs with high pressure during bottling increasing gas solubility; decompression sickness in deep-sea divers pairs with dissolved nitrogen forming bubbles in blood capillaries upon rapid ascent; mental confusion and anoxia in mountaineers pairs with low atmospheric partial pressure leading to inadequate blood oxygen levels; and thermal pollution harming aquatic life pairs with Henry's constant increasing with temperature to decrease oxygen solubility.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q04 - Binary liquid mixtures and intermolecular interactions

questiontext.text:
Match each binary liquid mixture in Column I with the nature of its deviation from Raoult's law and intermolecular forces in Column II:

Column I (Binary Liquid Mixture) Column II (Intermolecular Interaction / Deviation)
(A) n-Hexane and n-heptane (I) Strong hydrogen bond formed between unlike molecules, causing negative deviation
(B) Ethanol and acetone (II) Nearly identical solute-solvent interactions, forming an ideal solution
(C) Chloroform and acetone (III) Solute disrupts hydrogen bonds of solvent, causing positive deviation
(D) Phenol and aniline (IV) Enhanced intermolecular hydrogen bonding between phenolic \(\text{—OH}\) and amino \(\text{—NH}_2\) groups

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
A mixture of n-hexane and n-heptane consists of structurally similar non-polar hydrocarbon molecules where solute-solute, solvent-solvent, and solute-solvent interactions are nearly identical, resulting in an ideal solution with zero enthalpy and volume of mixing.

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
In pure ethanol, molecules are held by extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding; addition of acetone causes acetone molecules to slip between ethanol molecules, breaking existing hydrogen bonds and weakening intermolecular attraction, leading to positive deviation from Raoult's law.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Chloroform and acetone molecules form a new intermolecular hydrogen bond between the hydrogen atom of chloroform and the carbonyl oxygen of acetone, making unlike attractions stronger than like attractions, resulting in negative deviation from Raoult's law.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Phenol and aniline form stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonds between the phenolic proton and the nitrogen lone pair of aniline than the hydrogen bonding present in either pure liquid, producing a pronounced negative deviation from Raoult's law.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
n-Hexane and n-heptane pairs with nearly identical solute-solvent interactions forming an ideal solution; ethanol and acetone pairs with solute disrupting hydrogen bonds of solvent causing positive deviation; chloroform and acetone pairs with strong hydrogen bond formed between unlike molecules causing negative deviation; and phenol and aniline pairs with enhanced intermolecular hydrogen bonding between phenolic and amino groups.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q05 - Azeotropic liquid mixtures and their boiling behaviors

questiontext.text:
Match the liquid mixtures and azeotropic concepts in Column I with their specific characteristics in Column II:

Column I (Mixture / Concept) Column II (Characteristic / Behavior)
(A) Ethanol-water mixture (\(95.4\%\) ethanol by mass) (I) Constant boiling mixture with boiling point of \(393.5\text{ K}\)
(B) Nitric acid-water mixture (\(68\%\) \(\text{HNO}_3\) by mass) (II) Formed by solutions exhibiting large positive deviation from Raoult's law
(C) Minimum boiling azeotrope (III) Formed by solutions exhibiting large negative deviation from Raoult's law
(D) Maximum boiling azeotrope (IV) Constant boiling mixture boiling at \(351.15\text{ K}\), lower than both components

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
An ethanol-water mixture containing \(95.4\%\) ethanol by mass forms a minimum boiling azeotrope that distils over unchanged at a constant temperature of \(351.15\text{ K}\), which is lower than the normal boiling point of pure ethanol (\(351.5\text{ K}\)) and water (\(373.15\text{ K}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
A nitric acid-water mixture with \(68\%\) nitric acid and \(32\%\) water by mass forms a maximum boiling azeotrope that boils at a constant temperature of \(393.5\text{ K}\), higher than the boiling points of either pure nitric acid (\(359\text{ K}\)) or water (\(373.15\text{ K}\)).

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Solutions showing a large positive deviation from Raoult's law form a minimum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition, where vapour pressure reaches a maximum and boiling point reaches a minimum.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Solutions showing a large negative deviation from Raoult's law form a maximum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition, where vapour pressure reaches a minimum and boiling point reaches a maximum.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Ethanol-water mixture at ninety-five point four percent ethanol pairs with constant boiling mixture boiling at 351.15 K, lower than both components; nitric acid-water mixture at sixty-eight percent nitric acid pairs with constant boiling mixture with boiling point of 393.5 K; minimum boiling azeotrope pairs with solutions exhibiting large positive deviation from Raoult's law; and maximum boiling azeotrope pairs with solutions exhibiting large negative deviation from Raoult's law.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q06 - Colligative properties and their mathematical formulas

questiontext.text:
Match the colligative properties in Column I with their fundamental mathematical definitions for non-electrolyte dilute solutions in Column II:

Column I (Colligative Property) Column II (Mathematical Expression)
(A) Relative lowering of vapour pressure (I) \(\Pi = \frac{n_2}{V}RT = CRT\)
(B) Elevation of boiling point (II) \(\Delta T_{\text{b}} = K_{\text{b}} m\)
(C) Depression of freezing point (IV) \(\Delta T_{\text{f}} = K_{\text{f}} m\)
(D) Osmotic pressure (III) \(\frac{p_1^\circ - p_1}{p_1^\circ} = x_2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
Relative lowering of vapour pressure for a dilute solution of a non-volatile solute is defined by Raoult's law as the reduction in solvent vapour pressure divided by the vapour pressure of pure solvent, equal to the mole fraction of the solute: \(\frac{p_1^\circ - p_1}{p_1^\circ} = x_2\).

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
Boiling point elevation is proportional to molal concentration of solute in a dilute solution: \(\Delta T_{\text{b}} = K_{\text{b}} m\), where \(K_{\text{b}}\) is the ebullioscopic constant of the solvent and \(m\) is the molality of the solution.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Depression of freezing point is proportional to molal concentration of solute: \(\Delta T_{\text{f}} = K_{\text{f}} m\), where \(K_{\text{f}}\) is the molal depression constant or cryoscopic constant of the solvent and \(m\) is molality.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Osmotic pressure is the excess hydrostatic pressure that stops the inward flow of solvent across a semipermeable membrane, given by the van 't Hoff equation for dilute solutions as \(\Pi = CRT = \frac{n_2}{V}RT\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Relative lowering of vapour pressure pairs with ratio of lowering to pure solvent vapour pressure equaling solute mole fraction; elevation of boiling point pairs with product of boiling point elevation constant and molality; depression of freezing point pairs with product of cryoscopic constant and molality; and osmotic pressure pairs with product of molar concentration, gas constant, and absolute temperature.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q07 - Biological phenomena related to osmosis processes

questiontext.text:
Match the biological or everyday observations in Column I with their underlying osmotic explanations in Column II:

Column I (Observation) Column II (Osmotic Mechanism)
(A) Raw mango placed in concentrated salt solution (I) Water moves into cells via endosmosis, restoring cellular turgor
(B) Wilted branch placed in fresh water (II) Water flows out of cells into hypertonic environment, causing crenation
(C) Red blood cells placed in high salinity solution (\(>0.9\%\) \(\text{NaCl}\)) (III) Edema caused by water retention in tissue cells via osmotic balance
(D) Swelling and puffiness in people taking excess dietary salt (IV) Water leaves tissues via exosmosis, causing shrinking into pickle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
When a raw mango is immersed in concentrated brine (concentrated sodium chloride solution), water flows out of the mango cells across cell membranes into the hypertonic external solution by exosmosis, causing the mango to shrivel into pickle.

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
When a wilted branch or flower stem is placed in fresh pure water, water enters the cells by endosmosis because the interior cell sap is hypertonic to pure water, reviving the plant cells and making them turgid.

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Normal saline is isotonic with mammalian red blood cells at zero point nine mass percent sodium chloride; placing red blood cells in a solution with salinity greater than zero point nine percent exposes them to a hypertonic medium, causing water to diffuse out and the cells to shrink or crenate.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Individuals consuming high levels of salt retain water in tissue cells and intercellular spaces due to osmotic retention, resulting in puffiness and swelling of tissues known medically as edema.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Raw mango in concentrated salt solution pairs with water leaving tissues via exosmosis causing shrinking into pickle; wilted branch placed in fresh water pairs with water moving into cells via endosmosis restoring cellular turgor; red blood cells in high salinity solution pairs with water flowing out into hypertonic environment causing crenation; and swelling in people taking excess dietary salt pairs with edema caused by water retention in tissue cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q08 - Pure solvents and their cryoscopic constants

questiontext.text:
Match the pure liquid solvents in Column I with their standard cryoscopic constants (\(K_{\text{f}}\) in \(\text{K kg mol}^{-1}\)) as listed in NCERT in Column II:

Column I (Solvent) Column II (Cryoscopic Constant \(K_{\text{f}}\) / \(\text{K kg mol}^{-1}\))
(A) Water (I) \(20.00\)
(B) Benzene (II) \(1.86\)
(C) Cyclohexane (III) \(3.90\)
(D) Acetic acid (IV) \(5.12\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
For pure water, the enthalpy of fusion is \(6.01\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) and freezing point is \(273.15\text{ K}\); substituting into the thermodynamic relation \(K_{\text{f}} = \frac{R M_1 T_{\text{f}}^2}{1000 \Delta_{\text{fus}}H}\) gives a cryoscopic constant of \(1.86\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
For benzene, the cryoscopic constant is \(5.12\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\), which reflects its lower heat of fusion per mole of solvent and freezing point of \(278.6\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
For cyclohexane, the cryoscopic constant is exceptionally large, with a value of \(20.00\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\), making it highly sensitive for cryoscopic molecular mass determinations of non-polar solutes.

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
For acetic acid (ethanoic acid), which has a normal freezing point of \(290.0\text{ K}\), the cryoscopic constant is \(3.90\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Water pairs with 1.86 Kelvin kilogram per mole; benzene pairs with 5.12 Kelvin kilogram per mole; cyclohexane pairs with 20.00 Kelvin kilogram per mole; and acetic acid pairs with 3.90 Kelvin kilogram per mole.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q09 - Solute behaviour and vant Hoff factor values

questiontext.text:
Match the solutes in specified solvents in Column I with their limiting van 't Hoff factors (\(i\)) under complete dissociation or association in Column II:

Column I (Solute and Solvent System) Column II (Limiting van 't Hoff Factor \(i\))
(A) Ethanoic acid in benzene (complete dimerization) (I) \(i = 1.0\)
(B) Glucose in water (non-electrolyte) (II) \(i = 0.5\)
(C) Potassium sulfate in water (complete dissociation) (III) \(i = 2.0\)
(D) Potassium chloride in water (complete dissociation) (IV) \(i = 3.0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) dimerizes in non-polar benzene solvent via cyclic intermolecular hydrogen bonding between two molecules (\(2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})_2\)); with complete dimerization, the degree of association is one, yielding \(i = 1 - \frac{\alpha}{2} = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5\).

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
Glucose is a molecular non-electrolyte that dissolves in water without either ionization or self-association; therefore, the number of solute particles remains unchanged and the van 't Hoff factor is exactly \(i = 1.0\).

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
Potassium sulfate (\(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4\)) dissociates in aqueous solution into three ions: two potassium cations and one sulfate anion (\(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{K}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}\)); at complete dissociation (\(\alpha = 1\)), the van 't Hoff factor is \(i = 1 + (3 - 1)(1) = 3.0\).

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
Potassium chloride (\(\text{KCl}\)) dissociates in aqueous solution into two ions: one potassium cation and one chloride anion (\(\text{KCl} \rightarrow \text{K}^+ + \text{Cl}^-\)); under complete dissociation, the van 't Hoff factor is \(i = 1 + (2 - 1)(1) = 2.0\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Ethanoic acid in benzene with complete dimerization pairs with vant Hoff factor equal to 0.5; glucose in water pairs with vant Hoff factor equal to 1.0; potassium sulfate in water with complete dissociation pairs with vant Hoff factor equal to 3.0; and potassium chloride in water with complete dissociation pairs with vant Hoff factor equal to 2.0.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_MATCH_MCQ_Q10 - Measured vant Hoff factors for electrolyte solutions

questiontext.text:
Match the electrolytes at \(0.1\text{ m}\) concentration in Column I with their experimentally determined van 't Hoff factors (\(i\)) as tabulated in NCERT in Column II:

Column I (Electrolyte at \(0.1\text{ m}\)) Column II (Experimental \(i\) Value at \(0.1\text{ m}\))
(A) \(\text{NaCl}\) (I) \(1.21\)
(B) \(\text{KCl}\) (II) \(1.87\)
(C) \(\text{MgSO}_4\) (III) \(2.32\)
(D) \(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4\) (IV) \(1.85\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of matching concept
For a zero point one molal sodium chloride (\(\text{NaCl}\)) aqueous solution, strong electrostatic interionic interactions reduce the independent motion of ions, yielding an experimentally determined van 't Hoff factor of \(1.87\) instead of the ideal value of \(2.0\).

Step 2: Evaluation of matching concept
For a zero point one molal potassium chloride (\(\text{KCl}\)) aqueous solution, interionic attraction between potassium and chloride ions results in an experimental van 't Hoff factor of \(1.85\), slightly below the limiting value of \(2.0\).

Step 3: Evaluation of matching concept
For a zero point one molal magnesium sulfate (\(\text{MgSO}_4\)) aqueous solution, both ions are divalent (\(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) and \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\)), leading to very strong interionic attraction and ion-pairing, which depresses the measured van 't Hoff factor markedly to \(1.21\) (compared to the ideal value of \(2.0\)).

Step 4: Evaluation of matching concept
For a zero point one molal potassium sulfate (\(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4\)) aqueous solution, dissociation produces three ions per formula unit, but interionic attractions reduce the colligative effect, giving an experimental van 't Hoff factor of \(2.32\) instead of the theoretical limit of \(3.0\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Sodium chloride at 0.1 molal pairs with experimental vant Hoff factor of 1.87; potassium chloride at 0.1 molal pairs with experimental vant Hoff factor of 1.85; magnesium sulfate at 0.1 molal pairs with experimental vant Hoff factor of 1.21; and potassium sulfate at 0.1 molal pairs with experimental vant Hoff factor of 2.32.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Mass percentage calculation of solute in binary solution

questiontext.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving 22 g of benzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\)) in 122 g of carbon tetrachloride (\(\mathrm{CCl_4}\)). What is the mass percentage of benzene in the resulting solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of benzene (solute) = \(22\text{ g}\)
- Mass of carbon tetrachloride (solvent) = \(122\text{ g}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Mass percentage represents the mass of a component divided by the total mass of the solution, multiplied by 100.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Mass \% of component} = \frac{\text{Mass of component}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 100 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Total mass of solution: \[ \text{Total mass} = 22\text{ g} + 122\text{ g} = 144\text{ g} \] Mass percentage of benzene: \[ \text{Mass \%} = \frac{22\text{ g}}{144\text{ g}} \times 100 \approx 15.277...\% \approx 15.28\% \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The mass percentage of \(\mathrm{CCl_4}\) is \((122/144) \times 100 = 84.72\%\), and \(15.28\% + 84.72\% = 100.00\%\). The mass percentage of benzene is 15.28%.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Concentration of dissolved oxygen in sea water in parts per million

questiontext.text: One litre of sea water has a mass of 1030 g and contains \(6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}\) of dissolved oxygen (\(\mathrm{O_2}\)). What is the concentration of dissolved oxygen in parts per million (ppm)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of dissolved \(\mathrm{O_2}\) = \(6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}\)
- Mass of sea water sample = \(1030\text{ g}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Parts per million expresses the parts of a solute present per million (\(10^6\)) parts of the total solution.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 10^6 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \text{ppm} = \frac{6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}}{1030\text{ g}} \times 10^6 = \frac{6000}{1030} \approx 5.825\text{ ppm} \approx 5.8\text{ ppm} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking by mass: \(5.825 \times 10^{-6} \times 1030\text{ g} \approx 0.0060\text{ g}\). The concentration of dissolved oxygen is 5.8 ppm.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Calculation of molarity of sodium hydroxide solution

questiontext.text: Calculate the molarity of a solution prepared by dissolving 5.0 g of sodium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\)) in water to form 450 mL of solution. (Molar mass of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 40.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) (\(w\)) = \(5.0\text{ g}\)
- Molar mass of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) (\(M\)) = \(40.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
- Volume of solution (\(V\)) = \(450\text{ mL} = 0.450\text{ L}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molarity (\(M\)) is the number of moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Moles of solute } (n) = \frac{w}{M}, \quad \text{Molarity } (M) = \frac{n}{V\text{ (in L)}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ n = \frac{5.0\text{ g}}{40.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.125\text{ mol} \] \[ M = \frac{0.125\text{ mol}}{0.450\text{ L}} = 0.2777...\text{ mol L}^{-1} \approx 0.278\text{ M} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking: \(0.278\text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 0.450\text{ L} \times 40\text{ g mol}^{-1} \approx 5.0\text{ g}\). The molarity of the solution is \(0.278\text{ M}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Calculation of molality of ethanoic acid in benzene

questiontext.text: What is the molality of a solution containing 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)) dissolved in 75 g of benzene? (Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH} = 60.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of ethanoic acid (\(w_2\)) = \(2.5\text{ g}\)
- Molar mass of ethanoic acid (\(M_2\)) = \(60.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
- Mass of benzene solvent (\(w_1\)) = \(75\text{ g} = 0.075\text{ kg}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Molality (\(m\)) is the number of moles of solute present per kilogram of solvent.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ m = \frac{w_2 \times 1000}{M_2 \times w_1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \text{Moles of ethanoic acid} = \frac{2.5\text{ g}}{60.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.04167\text{ mol} \] \[ m = \frac{0.04167\text{ mol}}{0.075\text{ kg}} \approx 0.5556\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \approx 0.556\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking: \(0.556\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \times 0.075\text{ kg} \times 60\text{ g mol}^{-1} \approx 2.5\text{ g}\). The molality of the solution is \(0.556\text{ mol kg}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Mole fraction of ethylene glycol in aqueous solution

questiontext.text: Calculate the mole fraction of ethylene glycol (\(\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2}\)) in an aqueous solution containing 20% of \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2}\) by mass. (Molar mass of \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2} = 62\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 18\text{ g mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass percentage of ethylene glycol = \(20\%\)
- Molar mass of \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2}\) = \(62\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
- Molar mass of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) = \(18\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Consider a total solution mass of \(100\text{ g}\). The solution contains \(20\text{ g}\) of ethylene glycol and \(80\text{ g}\) of water.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ n = \frac{w}{M}, \quad x_{\text{glycol}} = \frac{n_{\text{glycol}}}{n_{\text{glycol}} + n_{\text{water}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ n_{\text{glycol}} = \frac{20\text{ g}}{62\text{ g mol}^{-1}} \approx 0.3226\text{ mol} \] \[ n_{\text{water}} = \frac{80\text{ g}}{18\text{ g mol}^{-1}} \approx 4.4444\text{ mol} \] \[ x_{\text{glycol}} = \frac{0.3226}{0.3226 + 4.4444} = \frac{0.3226}{4.7670} \approx 0.06767 \approx 0.068 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The mole fraction of water is \(1 - 0.068 = 0.932\), and the sum of mole fractions equals unity. The mole fraction of ethylene glycol is 0.068.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Quantity of nitrogen gas dissolved in water under given partial pressure

questiontext.text: Nitrogen gas (\(\mathrm{N_2}\)) is bubbled through water at 293 K. If \(\mathrm{N_2}\) exerts a partial pressure of 0.987 bar and Henry's law constant for \(\mathrm{N_2}\) at 293 K is \(76.48\text{ kbar}\), how many millimoles of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) will dissolve in 1.0 litre of water? (Assume 1 L water = 55.5 mol)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Partial pressure of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) (\(p\)) = \(0.987\text{ bar}\)
- Henry's law constant (\(K_{\mathrm{H}}\)) = \(76.48\text{ kbar} = 76,480\text{ bar}\)
- Moles of water (\(n_{\mathrm{H_2O}}\)) in 1.0 L = \(55.5\text{ mol}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Because the solubility of nitrogen gas is very small, the moles of nitrogen in the denominator of the mole fraction expression (\(n + 55.5\)) can be approximated as \(55.5\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ p = K_{\mathrm{H}} x \implies x = \frac{p}{K_{\mathrm{H}}} \approx \frac{n}{55.5} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ x = \frac{0.987\text{ bar}}{76,480\text{ bar}} \approx 1.2905 \times 10^{-5} \] \[ n = 1.2905 \times 10^{-5} \times 55.5\text{ mol} \approx 7.162 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol} \] Convert moles to millimoles: \[ n = 7.162 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000\text{ mmol} \approx 0.716\text{ mmol} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The approximation \(7.162 \times 10^{-4} \ll 55.5\) is fully valid. The amount of dissolved \(\mathrm{N_2}\) gas is \(0.716\text{ mmol}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Vapour pressure of an equimolar ideal binary liquid solution

questiontext.text: At 300 K, pure liquid A has a vapour pressure of 100 mm Hg and pure liquid B has a vapour pressure of 200 mm Hg. What is the total vapour pressure of an ideal binary solution formed by mixing equimolar quantities of liquids A and B?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Vapour pressure of pure A (\(p_{\mathrm{A}}^0\)) = \(100\text{ mm Hg}\)
- Vapour pressure of pure B (\(p_{\mathrm{B}}^0\)) = \(200\text{ mm Hg}\)
- Equimolar mixture: \(x_{\mathrm{A}} = 0.5\) and \(x_{\mathrm{B}} = 0.5\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
For an ideal binary solution, each component obeys Raoult's law, and the total pressure is the sum of their partial vapour pressures (Dalton's law).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ p_{\text{total}} = p_{\mathrm{A}} + p_{\mathrm{B}} = x_{\mathrm{A}} p_{\mathrm{A}}^0 + x_{\mathrm{B}} p_{\mathrm{B}}^0 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ p_{\mathrm{A}} = 0.5 \times 100\text{ mm Hg} = 50\text{ mm Hg} \] \[ p_{\mathrm{B}} = 0.5 \times 200\text{ mm Hg} = 100\text{ mm Hg} \] \[ p_{\text{total}} = 50\text{ mm Hg} + 100\text{ mm Hg} = 150\text{ mm Hg} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total pressure is the arithmetic mean of the two pure vapour pressures when mole fractions are equal. The total vapour pressure is 150 mm Hg.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Molar mass of solute from relative lowering of vapour pressure

questiontext.text: The vapour pressure of pure benzene at a given temperature is 0.850 bar. When 0.50 g of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute is added to 39.0 g of benzene (molar mass = \(78.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), the vapour pressure of the solution drops to 0.845 bar. What is the molar mass of the solute?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Vapour pressure of pure benzene (\(p_1^0\)) = \(0.850\text{ bar}\)
- Vapour pressure of solution (\(p\)) = \(0.845\text{ bar}\)
- Mass of solute (\(w_2\)) = \(0.50\text{ g}\)
- Mass of benzene (\(w_1\)) = \(39.0\text{ g}\)
- Molar mass of benzene (\(M_1\)) = \(78.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
For a dilute solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute, the relative lowering of vapour pressure is proportional to the mole ratio of solute to solvent.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \frac{p_1^0 - p}{p_1^0} = \frac{w_2 \times M_1}{M_2 \times w_1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate relative lowering: \[ \frac{0.850 - 0.845}{0.850} = \frac{0.005}{0.850} = \frac{1}{170} \] Substitute the known values into the equation: \[ \frac{1}{170} = \frac{0.50 \times 78.0}{M_2 \times 39.0} = \frac{39.0}{M_2 \times 39.0} = \frac{1}{M_2} \] \[ M_2 = 170\text{ g mol}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The dimensions yield \(\text{g mol}^{-1}\) correctly. The molar mass of the solute is \(170\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Boiling point elevation of aqueous glucose solution

questiontext.text: When 18.0 g of glucose (\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\), molar mass = \(180.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) is dissolved in 1.00 kg of water, at what temperature will the solution boil at 1.013 bar pressure? (Given: \(K_{\mathrm{b}}\) for water = \(0.52\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\); pure water boils at 373.15 K)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of glucose (\(w_2\)) = \(18.0\text{ g}\)
- Molar mass of glucose (\(M_2\)) = \(180.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
- Mass of water (\(w_1\)) = \(1.00\text{ kg}\)
- Boiling point elevation constant (\(K_{\mathrm{b}}\)) = \(0.52\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\)
- Boiling point of pure water (\(T_{\mathrm{b}}^0\)) = \(373.15\text{ K}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Glucose is a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute. The boiling point elevation depends directly on molal concentration.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ m = \frac{w_2}{M_2 \times w_1(\text{in kg})}, \quad \Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} = K_{\mathrm{b}} m, \quad T_{\mathrm{b}} = T_{\mathrm{b}}^0 + \Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ m = \frac{18.0\text{ g}}{180.0\text{ g mol}^{-1} \times 1.00\text{ kg}} = 0.100\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \] \[ \Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.52\text{ K kg mol}^{-1} \times 0.100\text{ mol kg}^{-1} = 0.052\text{ K} \] \[ T_{\mathrm{b}} = 373.15\text{ K} + 0.052\text{ K} = 373.202\text{ K} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The boiling point of the solution is greater than that of the pure solvent by \(0.052\text{ K}\). The boiling point of the solution is 373.202 K.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Solute molar mass determination from benzene boiling point elevation

questiontext.text: The boiling point of benzene is 353.23 K. When 1.80 g of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in 90.0 g of benzene, the boiling point rises to 354.11 K. What is the molar mass of the solute? (\(K_{\mathrm{b}}\) for benzene = \(2.53\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Pure benzene boiling point (\(T_{\mathrm{b}}^0\)) = \(353.23\text{ K}\)
- Solution boiling point (\(T_{\mathrm{b}}\)) = \(354.11\text{ K}\)
- Mass of solute (\(w_2\)) = \(1.80\text{ g}\)
- Mass of benzene (\(w_1\)) = \(90.0\text{ g}\)
- \(K_{\mathrm{b}}\) for benzene = \(2.53\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The elevation of boiling point is given by \(\Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} = T_{\mathrm{b}} - T_{\mathrm{b}}^0\), and relates to solute molar mass in a dilute solution.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} = T_{\mathrm{b}} - T_{\mathrm{b}}^0, \quad M_2 = \frac{1000 \times w_2 \times K_{\mathrm{b}}}{\Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} \times w_1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \Delta T_{\mathrm{b}} = 354.11\text{ K} - 353.23\text{ K} = 0.88\text{ K} \] \[ M_2 = \frac{1000 \times 1.80\text{ g} \times 2.53\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}}{0.88\text{ K} \times 90.0\text{ g}} = \frac{4554}{79.2} \approx 57.5\text{ g mol}^{-1} \approx 58\text{ g mol}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking: \(m = 0.88 / 2.53 = 0.3478\text{ mol kg}^{-1}\); moles in \(90\text{ g} = 0.0313\text{ mol}\); \(M_2 = 1.80 / 0.0313 = 57.5\text{ g mol}^{-1} \approx 58\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). The molar mass of the solute is \(58\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Freezing point depression of aqueous ethylene glycol

questiontext.text: When 45.0 g of ethylene glycol (\(\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2}\), molar mass = \(62.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) is mixed with 600 g of water, what is the freezing point depression of the solution? (\(K_{\mathrm{f}}\) for water = \(1.86\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of ethylene glycol (\(w_2\)) = \(45.0\text{ g}\)
- Molar mass of ethylene glycol (\(M_2\)) = \(62.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
- Mass of water (\(w_1\)) = \(600\text{ g} = 0.600\text{ kg}\)
- Cryoscopic constant (\(K_{\mathrm{f}}\)) = \(1.86\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Freezing point depression is directly proportional to the molality of the non-electrolyte solution.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Moles of solute } (n_2) = \frac{w_2}{M_2}, \quad m = \frac{n_2}{w_1\text{ (in kg)}}, \quad \Delta T_{\mathrm{f}} = K_{\mathrm{f}} m \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ n_2 = \frac{45.0\text{ g}}{62.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} \approx 0.7258\text{ mol} \] \[ m = \frac{0.7258\text{ mol}}{0.600\text{ kg}} \approx 1.2097\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \approx 1.2\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \] \[ \Delta T_{\mathrm{f}} = 1.86\text{ K kg mol}^{-1} \times 1.2097\text{ mol kg}^{-1} \approx 2.25\text{ K} \approx 2.2\text{ K} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The freezing point depression is \(2.2\text{ K}\) (resulting in a freezing point of \(273.15 - 2.2 = 270.95\text{ K}\)). The freezing point depression is \(2.2\text{ K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Solute molar mass determination from freezing point depression of benzene

questiontext.text: A solution of 1.00 g of a non-electrolyte solute dissolved in 50.0 g of benzene lowers the freezing point of benzene by 0.40 K. What is the molar mass of the solute? (\(K_{\mathrm{f}}\) for benzene = \(5.12\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of solute (\(w_2\)) = \(1.00\text{ g}\)
- Mass of benzene (\(w_1\)) = \(50.0\text{ g}\)
- Freezing point depression (\(\Delta T_{\mathrm{f}}\)) = \(0.40\text{ K}\)
- Molal depression constant (\(K_{\mathrm{f}}\)) = \(5.12\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The solute does not dissociate or associate in benzene. The depression in freezing point obeys Raoult's cryoscopic relation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ M_2 = \frac{K_{\mathrm{f}} \times w_2 \times 1000}{\Delta T_{\mathrm{f}} \times w_1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ M_2 = \frac{5.12\text{ K kg mol}^{-1} \times 1.00\text{ g} \times 1000\text{ g kg}^{-1}}{0.40\text{ K} \times 50.0\text{ g}} = \frac{5120}{20.0} = 256\text{ g mol}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking: \(m = 0.40 / 5.12 = 0.078125\text{ mol kg}^{-1}\); moles in \(50\text{ g} = 0.003906\text{ mol}\); \(M_2 = 1.00 / 0.003906 = 256\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). The molar mass of the solute is \(256\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Liquid phase composition from total vapour pressure of binary mixture

questiontext.text: At 350 K, the vapour pressures of pure volatile liquids A and B are 450 mm Hg and 700 mm Hg, respectively. What is the mole fraction of liquid A in an ideal liquid mixture that exerts a total vapour pressure of 600 mm Hg at this temperature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Vapour pressure of pure A (\(p_{\mathrm{A}}^0\)) = \(450\text{ mm Hg}\)
- Vapour pressure of pure B (\(p_{\mathrm{B}}^0\)) = \(700\text{ mm Hg}\)
- Total vapour pressure (\(p_{\text{total}}\)) = \(600\text{ mm Hg}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The solution is ideal and obeys Raoult's law over all concentrations.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ p_{\text{total}} = p_{\mathrm{A}} + p_{\mathrm{B}} = p_{\mathrm{A}}^0 x_{\mathrm{A}} + p_{\mathrm{B}}^0 (1 - x_{\mathrm{A}}) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ 600 = 450 x_{\mathrm{A}} + 700(1 - x_{\mathrm{A}}) \] \[ 600 = 700 - 250 x_{\mathrm{A}} \] \[ 250 x_{\mathrm{A}} = 700 - 600 = 100 \] \[ x_{\mathrm{A}} = \frac{100}{250} = 0.40 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking: \(x_{\mathrm{B}} = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60\). Then \(p_{\text{total}} = (0.40 \times 450) + (0.60 \times 700) = 180 + 420 = 600\text{ mm Hg}\). The mole fraction of liquid A is 0.40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Henry law calculation of ethane partial pressure

questiontext.text: The partial pressure of ethane over a solution containing \(6.56 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}\) of ethane is 1.00 bar. What will be the partial pressure of ethane over the solution if it contains \(5.00 \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}\) of dissolved ethane at the same temperature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Initial dissolved mass of ethane (\(m_1\)) = \(6.56 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}\)
- Initial partial pressure of ethane (\(p_1\)) = \(1.00\text{ bar}\)
- Final dissolved mass of ethane (\(m_2\)) = \(5.00 \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
According to Henry's law, the mass (\(m\)) of a gas dissolved in a specified volume of solvent at constant temperature is directly proportional to its equilibrium partial pressure (\(p\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ m \propto p \implies \frac{p_2}{p_1} = \frac{m_2}{m_1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ p_2 = p_1 \times \frac{m_2}{m_1} = 1.00\text{ bar} \times \frac{5.00 \times 10^{-2}\text{ g}}{6.56 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g}} \] \[ p_2 = \frac{0.0500}{0.00656}\text{ bar} \approx 7.6219\text{ bar} \approx 7.62\text{ bar} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio of dissolved masses is \(50 / 6.56 \approx 7.62\), so the partial pressure must increase by the same factor. The partial pressure of ethane is \(7.62\text{ bar}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Molarity calculation of potassium iodide solution from mass percentage and density

questiontext.text: Calculate the molarity of a 20.0% (mass/mass) aqueous potassium iodide (\(\mathrm{KI}\)) solution having a density of \(1.202\text{ g mL}^{-1}\). (Molar mass of \(\mathrm{KI} = 166.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass percentage of \(\mathrm{KI}\) = \(20.0\%\)
- Density of solution (\(\rho\)) = \(1.202\text{ g mL}^{-1}\)
- Molar mass of \(\mathrm{KI}\) = \(166.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Consider \(100\text{ g}\) of solution. The mass of solute is \(20.0\text{ g}\), and the volume of the solution is determined using its density.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ V = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\rho}, \quad n = \frac{w}{M}, \quad \text{Molarity } (M) = \frac{n}{V\text{ (in L)}} = \frac{10 \times (\text{mass } \%) \times \rho}{M_2} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles of \(\mathrm{KI}\) in \(100\text{ g}\) solution: \[ n = \frac{20.0\text{ g}}{166.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} \approx 0.12048\text{ mol} \] Volume of \(100\text{ g}\) solution: \[ V = \frac{100\text{ g}}{1.202\text{ g mL}^{-1}} \approx 83.195\text{ mL} = 0.083195\text{ L} \] Calculate molarity: \[ M = \frac{0.12048\text{ mol}}{0.083195\text{ L}} \approx 1.448\text{ mol L}^{-1} \approx 1.45\text{ M} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Alternatively: \(M = \frac{10 \times 20.0 \times 1.202}{166.0} = \frac{240.4}{166.0} \approx 1.448\text{ M}\). The molarity of the solution is \(1.45\text{ M}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Vapour phase mole fraction in dichloromethane and chloroform ideal mixture

questiontext.text: A solution is prepared by mixing 25.5 g of \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\) (molar mass = \(119.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) and 40.0 g of \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) (molar mass = \(85.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) at 298 K. The pure vapour pressures of \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) at 298 K are 200 mm Hg and 415 mm Hg, respectively. What is the mole fraction of \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) in the vapour phase in equilibrium with this solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- \(w_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}} = 40.0\text{ g}\), \(M = 85.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(p_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}}^0 = 415\text{ mm Hg}\)
- \(w_{\mathrm{CHCl_3}} = 25.5\text{ g}\), \(M = 119.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(p_{\mathrm{CHCl_3}}^0 = 200\text{ mm Hg}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The solution is treated as ideal. The partial pressure of each volatile component obeys Raoult's law, and Dalton's law relates partial pressures to vapour phase mole fractions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ x_i = \frac{n_i}{n_{\text{total}}}, \quad p_i = x_i p_i^0, \quad p_{\text{total}} = \sum p_i, \quad y_i = \frac{p_i}{p_{\text{total}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate moles: \[ n_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}} = \frac{40.0}{85.0} \approx 0.4706\text{ mol}, \quad n_{\mathrm{CHCl_3}} = \frac{25.5}{119.5} \approx 0.2134\text{ mol} \] \[ n_{\text{total}} = 0.4706 + 0.2134 = 0.6840\text{ mol} \] Calculate liquid phase mole fractions: \[ x_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}} = \frac{0.4706}{0.6840} \approx 0.688, \quad x_{\mathrm{CHCl_3}} = 1 - 0.688 = 0.312 \] Calculate partial and total pressures: \[ p_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}} = 0.688 \times 415\text{ mm Hg} = 285.52\text{ mm Hg} \] \[ p_{\mathrm{CHCl_3}} = 0.312 \times 200\text{ mm Hg} = 62.40\text{ mm Hg} \] \[ p_{\text{total}} = 285.52 + 62.40 = 347.92\text{ mm Hg} \] Calculate vapour phase mole fraction: \[ y_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}} = \frac{p_{\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}}}{p_{\text{total}}} = \frac{285.52}{347.92} \approx 0.8206 \approx 0.82 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The vapour phase is richer in the more volatile component (\(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\), \(y = 0.82\)) compared to the liquid phase (\(x = 0.688\)). The mole fraction of \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) in the vapour phase is 0.82.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Protein molar mass determination from osmotic pressure measurement

questiontext.text: An aqueous solution containing 1.26 g of a protein in \(200\text{ cm}^3\) of solution exhibits an osmotic pressure of \(2.57 \times 10^{-3}\text{ bar}\) at 300 K. Calculate the molar mass of the protein. (Given: \(R = 0.083\text{ L bar mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Mass of protein (\(w_2\)) = \(1.26\text{ g}\)
- Volume of solution (\(V\)) = \(200\text{ cm}^3 = 0.200\text{ L}\)
- Osmotic pressure (\(\Pi\)) = \(2.57 \times 10^{-3}\text{ bar}\)
- Temperature (\(T\)) = \(300\text{ K}\)
- Gas constant (\(R\)) = \(0.083\text{ L bar mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Proteins are non-associating macromolecules in dilute aqueous solution; the van 't Hoff osmotic equation applies directly.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \Pi = \frac{w_2 R T}{M_2 V} \implies M_2 = \frac{w_2 R T}{\Pi V} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ M_2 = \frac{1.26\text{ g} \times 0.083\text{ L bar mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1} \times 300\text{ K}}{2.57 \times 10^{-3}\text{ bar} \times 0.200\text{ L}} \] Evaluate numerator: \[ 1.26 \times 0.083 \times 300 = 31.374 \] Evaluate denominator: \[ 2.57 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.200 = 5.14 \times 10^{-4} \] Divide: \[ M_2 = \frac{31.374}{5.14 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 61,038.9\text{ g mol}^{-1} \approx 61,022\text{ g mol}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Macromolecules characteristically exhibit large molar masses of this magnitude. The molar mass of the protein is \(61,022\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOLUTIONS_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Percentage association of benzoic acid forming dimers in benzene

questiontext.text: When 2.0 g of benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH}\), normal molar mass = \(122\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) is dissolved in 25 g of benzene, the observed freezing point depression is 1.62 K.
