Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Linear plots and concentration dependence of half lives

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A plot of \(\ln[\text{R}]\) versus time \(t\) for a first-order reaction gives a straight line with a slope of \(-k\) and an intercept of \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\).

Statement II: The half-life of a zero-order reaction is directly proportional to the initial concentration of the reactant.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया के लिए समय \(t\) के विरुद्ध \(\ln[\text{R}]\) का आलेख \(-k\) ढाल और \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\) अंतःखंड वाली एक सीधी रेखा देता है।

कथन II: शून्य कोटि की अभिक्रिया का अर्ध-आयु काल अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता के सीधे समानुपाती होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Integrating the first-order differential equation yields \(\ln[\text{R}] = -kt + \ln[\text{R}]_0\). Comparing this directly with the linear form \(y = mx + c\), a plot of \(\ln[\text{R}]\) on the vertical axis against \(t\) on the horizontal axis produces a line with slope \(m = -k\) and intercept \(c = \ln[\text{R}]_0\). Therefore, the logarithmic graphical analysis is correct.

Step 2
For a zero-order reaction, the integrated equation \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\) evaluated at \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0/2\) gives \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\). This expression proves that half-life is directly proportional to initial concentration \([\text{R}]_0\). Therefore, the zero-order half-life relationship is correct.

Step 3
Both statements are correct.

चरण 1
प्रथम कोटि के समाकलित वेग समीकरण \(\ln[\text{R}] = -kt + \ln[\text{R}]_0\) की तुलना सरल रेखा समीकरण \(y = mx + c\) से करने पर \(\ln[\text{R}]\) बनाम \(t\) का आलेख \(-k\) ढाल तथा \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\) अंतःखंड वाली सरल रेखा देता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2
शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए समाकलित समीकरण से अर्ध-आयु काल \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\) प्राप्त होता है, जो स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाता है कि अर्ध-आयु प्रारंभिक सांद्रता \([\text{R}]_0\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3
दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Theoretical prediction of complex reaction order and molecularity

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For any complex chemical reaction, the molecularity is equal to the sum of the stoichiometric coefficients of all reacting species in the balanced equation.

Statement II: The rate law and order of a complex reaction can be predicted theoretically by inspecting the overall balanced chemical equation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी भी जटिल रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के लिए, आणविकता संतुलित समीकरण में सभी भाग लेने वाले अभिकारकों के रससमीकरणमितीय गुणांकों के योग के बराबर होती है।

कथन II: किसी जटिल अभिक्रिया के दर नियम और कोटि की भविष्यवाणी समग्र संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण का निरीक्षण करके सैद्धांतिक रूप से की जा सकती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Molecularity is defined exclusively for single-step elementary reactions. In complex multistep reactions involving multiple consecutive or simultaneous elementary events, collisions occur in separate stages; therefore, molecularity has no physical meaning for the overall balanced equation. Hence, the assertion regarding overall molecularity is incorrect.

Step 2
A balanced stoichiometric equation never reveals the underlying microscopic mechanism or which intermediate stage is the rate-determining step. Rate laws reflect the reaction mechanism and must be deduced from experimental measurements; they cannot be predicted theoretically from overall stoichiometry. Hence, the assertion regarding theoretical prediction of rate law is incorrect.

Step 3
Both statements are incorrect.

चरण 1
आणविकता केवल एकल-पद प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए परिभाषित होती है। जटिल बहु-पद अभिक्रियाओं में रासायनिक क्रिया कई अलग-अलग पदों में संपन्न होती है, अतः पूरी संतुलित समीकरण के लिए आणविकता का कोई भौतिक अर्थ नहीं होता। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2
एक संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण यह नहीं दर्शाती कि अभिक्रिया किस क्रियाविधि से होती है या कौन सा पद दर निर्धारक है। दर नियम और कोटि केवल प्रायोगिक रूप से निर्धारित किए जा सकते हैं, सैद्धांतिक रूप से नहीं। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3
दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q07 - Temperature invariance at zero activation energy and catalyst thermodynamics

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to the Arrhenius equation, if the activation energy of a chemical reaction is zero, its rate constant becomes completely independent of temperature.

Statement II: A catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of products in a reversible reaction by making the standard Gibbs free energy change more negative.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: आर्रेनियस समीकरण के अनुसार, यदि किसी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया की सक्रियण ऊर्जा शून्य हो, तो इसका दर स्थिरांक तापमान से पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र हो जाता है।

कथन II: उत्प्रेरक मानक गिब्स मुक्त ऊर्जा परिवर्तन को अधिक ऋणात्मक बनाकर उत्क्रमणीय अभिक्रिया में उत्पादों की साम्य लब्धि को बढ़ा देता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
The Arrhenius relation is \(k = A e^{-E_a/RT}\). Setting the activation energy \(E_a = 0\) simplifies the exponential term to \(e^0 = 1\), reducing the expression to \(k = A\). Because \(A\) is treated as a reaction-specific constant over normal temperature ranges, the rate constant exhibits zero temperature dependence. Therefore, the deduction regarding zero activation energy is correct.

Step 2
A catalyst accelerates the rates of both forward and reverse reactions by lowering the activation energy barrier to an identical extent without altering the chemical nature of initial reactants or final products. Consequently, the enthalpy of reaction (\(\Delta H\)), standard Gibbs free energy change (\(\Delta G^\circ\)), and equilibrium constant (\(K\)) remain strictly unchanged; a catalyst only shortens the time required to reach equilibrium. Therefore, the claim regarding altered Gibbs free energy and equilibrium yield is incorrect.

Step 3
The first statement is correct and the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1
आर्रेनियस समीकरण \(k = A e^{-E_a/RT}\) में सक्रियण ऊर्जा \(E_a = 0\) रखने पर चरघातांकी पद \(e^0 = 1\) हो जाता है, जिससे \(k = A\) प्राप्त होता है। यह दर्शाता है कि शून्य सक्रियण ऊर्जा पर दर स्थिरांक ताप पर निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2
उत्प्रेरक अग्र और पश्च दोनों अभिक्रियाओं के सक्रियण ऊर्जा अवरोध को समान रूप से घटाता है तथा अभिकारकों और उत्पादों की मूल ऊर्जा अवस्थाओं को नहीं बदलता। अतः अभिक्रिया की मानक गिब्स ऊर्जा (\(\Delta G^\circ\)) और साम्य स्थिरांक अपरिवर्तित रहते हैं; केवल साम्यावस्था तेजी से प्राप्त होती है। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3
पहला कथन सही है तथा दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q08 - Collision theory energetic and steric criteria for effective collisions

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the collision theory of chemical reactions, every collision between reactant molecules possessing kinetic energy greater than or equal to the activation energy successfully produces product molecules.

Statement II: An effective collision leading to chemical bond breaking and formation requires both sufficient threshold energy and proper spatial orientation of the colliding species.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: रासायनिक अभिक्रियाओं के संघट्ट सिद्धांत में, सक्रियण ऊर्जा के बराबर या उससे अधिक गतिज ऊर्जा वाले अभिकारक अणुओं के बीच होने वाली प्रत्येक टक्कर सफलतापूर्वक उत्पाद अणुओं का निर्माण करती है।

कथन II: रासायनिक बंधों के टूटने और बनने के लिए अनुकूल प्रभावी संघट्ट हेतु पर्याप्त देहली ऊर्जा और टकराने वाले कणों के उचित त्रिविम अभिविन्यास दोनों की आवश्यकता होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Meeting the energetic threshold (\(E \ge E_a\)) is necessary but not sufficient on its own. If energetic molecules collide with improper stereochemical orientation, their reactive functional centers cannot interact to form intermediate bonds, and the molecules simply bounce apart without reacting. Therefore, the assertion that all energetic collisions yield products is incorrect.

Step 2
Collision theory formalizes the reaction rate as \(\text{Rate} = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_a/RT}\), explicitly combining the energetic requirement (the Boltzmann fraction \(e^{-E_a/RT}\)) with the stereochemical alignment requirement (the steric probability factor \(P\)). Thus, both criteria must be fulfilled simultaneously for a collision to be effective. Therefore, the dual-condition requirement is scientifically correct.

Step 3
The first statement is incorrect and the second statement is correct.

चरण 1
सक्रियण ऊर्जा के बराबर या उससे अधिक ऊर्जा होना अनिवार्य है, परंतु पर्याप्त नहीं। यदि अत्यधिक ऊर्जा वाले अणु गलत दिशा या अभिविन्यास में टकराते हैं, तो वे बिना बंध बनाए केवल वापस उछल जाते हैं और उत्पाद नहीं बनते। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2
संघट्ट सिद्धांत के अनुसार दर समीकरण \(\text{दर} = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_a/RT}\) होता है, जिसमें देहली ऊर्जा (ऊर्जा अवरोध) तथा त्रिविम कारक \(P\) (उचित अभिविन्यास अवरोध) दोनों का एक साथ पूरा होना अनिवार्य है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3
पहला कथन गलत है तथा दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Distinguishing pseudo first order reactions and radioactive kinetics

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The inversion of cane sugar into glucose and fructose in the presence of dilute acid is a pseudo first-order reaction because water is present in large excess.

Statement II: The order of a chemical reaction can be zero, fractional, or an integer, but the molecularity of an elementary reaction can never be zero or fractional.

Statement III: All natural and artificial radioactive decays of unstable atomic nuclei obey second-order reaction kinetics.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: तनु अम्ल की उपस्थिति में इक्षु-शर्करा (केन शुगर) का ग्लूकोस एवं फ्रुक्टोस में प्रतीपन (इनवर्जन) एक छद्म प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया है क्योंकि जल अत्यधिक आधिक्य में उपस्थित होता है।

कथन II: किसी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया की कोटि शून्य, भिन्नात्मक या एक पूर्णांक हो सकती है, परंतु किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया की आणविकता कभी भी शून्य या भिन्नात्मक नहीं हो सकती है।

कथन III: अस्थिर परमाणु नाभिकों के सभी प्राकृतिक एवं कृत्रिम रेडियोऐक्टिव क्षय द्वितीय कोटि की अभिक्रिया गतिकी का पालन करते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
In the acid-catalyzed inversion of sucrose (\(\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)), water acts as the solvent and is present in such large excess that its concentration remains practically constant throughout the reaction. Consequently, the rate law simplifies to \(\text{Rate} = k' [\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}]\), exhibiting pseudo first-order behavior. Therefore, the proposition regarding cane sugar inversion is correct.

Step 2
The order of a reaction is an empirical exponent sum derived from experimental measurements, allowing it to take values of zero, fractions, or integers. In contrast, molecularity represents the actual physical count of discrete reacting species colliding simultaneously in an elementary step; hence, it can only be a positive whole integer (1, 2, or 3) and cannot be zero or fractional. Therefore, the proposition regarding reaction order and molecularity is correct.

Step 3
All spontaneous and induced nuclear disintegrations proceed at a rate directly proportional solely to the number of radioactive nuclei currently present (\(-\text{d}N/\text{d}t = \lambda N\)), which fundamentally defines first-order kinetics rather than second-order kinetics. Therefore, the proposition regarding radioactive decay kinetics is incorrect.

Step 4
The first and second propositions are correct, while the third proposition is incorrect.

चरण 1
सुक्रोस के अम्ल-उत्प्रेरित प्रतीपन (\(\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) में जल विलायक के रूप में अत्यधिक आधिक्य में उपस्थित रहता है, जिससे पूरी अभिक्रिया के दौरान इसकी सांद्रता व्यावहारिक रूप से स्थिर रहती है। परिणामस्वरूप, दर नियम \(\text{Rate} = k' [\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}]\) बन जाता है, जो छद्म प्रथम कोटि व्यवहार प्रदर्शित करता है। अतः इक्षु-शर्करा के प्रतीपन से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 2
अभिक्रिया की कोटि एक प्रायोगिक मान है जो शून्य, भिन्न अथवा पूर्णांक हो सकती है। इसके विपरीत, आणविकता किसी प्राथमिक पद में एक साथ टकराने वाले कणों की वास्तविक संख्या होती है; अतः यह केवल धनात्मक पूर्णांक (1, 2 अथवा 3) ही हो सकती है और कभी शून्य या भिन्नात्मक नहीं हो सकती। अतः कोटि और आणविकता से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 3
सभी प्राकृतिक एवं कृत्रिम रेडियोऐक्टिव क्षय की दर केवल उपस्थित अस्थिर नाभिकों की संख्या के समानुपाती होती है (\(-\text{d}N/\text{d}t = \lambda N\)), जो कि प्रथम कोटि गतिकी का लक्षण है, न कि द्वितीय कोटि का। अतः रेडियोऐक्टिव क्षय की कोटि से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

चरण 4
पहला और दूसरा कथन सही है, जबकि तीसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II and Statement III are incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I and Statement II are incorrect, but Statement III is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Graphical analysis of zero and first order reactions

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: For a zero-order chemical reaction, the half-life period (\(t_{1/2}\)) is directly proportional to the initial concentration of the reactant.

Statement II: For a first-order chemical reaction, a plot of \(\log \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\) versus time \(t\) is a straight line passing through the origin with a slope equal to \(k / 2.303\).

Statement III: The rate constant (\(k\)) of a first-order reaction has the dimension of \(\text{time}^{-1}\) and its numerical value is independent of the concentration units chosen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक शून्य-कोटि की रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के लिए, अर्ध-आयु काल (\(t_{1/2}\)) अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता के अनुक्रमानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: एक प्रथम-कोटि की रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के लिए, समय \(t\) के विरुद्ध \(\log \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\) का आलेख मूलबिंदु से गुजरने वाली एक सरल रेखा होती है जिसकी ढाल \(k / 2.303\) के बराबर होती है।

कथन III: प्रथम-कोटि की अभिक्रिया के दर स्थिरांक (\(k\)) की विमा \(\text{time}^{-1}\) होती है और इसका संख्यात्मक मान चुनी गई सांद्रता की इकाइयों से स्वतंत्र होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
The integrated rate expression for zero-order kinetics is \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\). Substituting \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 / 2\) at \(t = t_{1/2}\) yields \(t_{1/2} = [\text{R}]_0 / (2k)\). Thus, the half-life is directly proportional to the initial reactant concentration \([\text{R}]_0\). Therefore, the proposition regarding zero-order half-life is correct.

Step 2
The integrated first-order rate law in logarithmic form is \(k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\), which rearranges to \(\log \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]} = \left(\frac{k}{2.303}\right)t\). Comparing this with the linear relation \(y = mx\), the plot of \(\log ([\text{R}]_0/[\text{R}])\) versus \(t\) passes through the origin with slope \(k / 2.303\). Therefore, the proposition regarding the first-order plot is correct.

Step 3
For a first-order rate process, \(k = \text{Rate}/[\text{R}] = (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1})/(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}) = \text{s}^{-1}\). The concentration units cancel out completely in the dimensional ratio; thus, \(k\) has dimensions of \(\text{time}^{-1}\) and its numerical magnitude does not depend on concentration units. Therefore, the proposition regarding first-order rate constant dimensions is correct.

Step 4
All three propositions are correct.

चरण 1
शून्य-कोटि अभिक्रिया का समाकलित दर समीकरण \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\) होता है। अर्ध-आयु \(t = t_{1/2}\) पर \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 / 2\) रखने पर \(t_{1/2} = [\text{R}]_0 / (2k)\) प्राप्त होता है, जो दर्शाता है कि अर्ध-आयु प्रारंभिक सांद्रता के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है। अतः शून्य-कोटि की अर्ध-आयु से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 2
प्रथम-कोटि अभिक्रिया के समाकलित रूप \(k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log \frac{[text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\) को \(\log \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]} = \left(\frac{k}{2.303}\right)t\) के रूप में लिखा जा सकता है। यह \(y = mx\) का एक रैखिक समीकरण है, जिसकी ढाल \(k / 2.303\) होती है और यह मूलबिंदु से गुजरता है। अतः प्रथम-कोटि के आलेख से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 3
प्रथम-कोटि के लिए \(k = \text{दर}/[\text{R}] = (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1})/(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}) = \text{s}^{-1}\) होता है। सांद्रता की इकाइयाँ आपस में निरस्त हो जाती हैं, जिससे \(k\) की विमा केवल \(\text{time}^{-1}\) रहती है और इसका मान सांद्रता की इकाई पर निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः दर स्थिरांक की विमा से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 4
तीनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II and Statement III are incorrect.
Statement I and Statement II are incorrect, but Statement III is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Mechanism of complex reactions and catalytic energy pathways

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In a complex multi-step reaction, the overall rate of reaction is controlled by the fastest elementary step in the reaction mechanism.

Statement II: Elementary reactions with a molecularity of three or greater are very common because the simultaneous collision of three or more molecules is highly probable.

Statement III: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway associated with a lower activation energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक जटिल बहु-पदीय अभिक्रिया में, अभिक्रिया की समग्र दर क्रियाविधि के सबसे तीव्र प्राथमिक पद द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है।

कथन II: तीन या उससे अधिक आणविकता वाली प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाएँ अत्यंत सामान्य होती हैं क्योंकि तीन या अधिक अणुओं के एक साथ टकराने की संभावना बहुत अधिक होती है।

कथन III: एक उत्प्रेरक कम संक्रियण ऊर्जा वाला एक वैकल्पिक अभिक्रिया पथ प्रदान करके रासायनिक अभिक्रिया की दर को बढ़ाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
In a complex sequential process involving multiple elementary steps, the overall speed is throttled by the slowest step, known as the rate-determining step, analogous to the narrowest bottleneck in a funnel. Therefore, the proposition that the fastest step controls the rate is incorrect.

Step 2
The statistical probability that three or more independent gas or solute molecules collide simultaneously at precisely the same point in space with proper orientation is exceptionally small. Consequently, elementary reactions with molecularity three are extremely rare and slow, while molecularity greater than three is not observed. Therefore, the proposition claiming trimolecular reactions are common is incorrect.

Step 3
A catalyst participates transiently to form an intermediate complex, opening an alternative reaction pathway characterized by a lower activation barrier (\(E_a\)). According to the Arrhenius relation \(k = A e^{-E_a/RT}\), reducing \(E_a\) exponentially increases the fraction of effective collisions and thus accelerates the reaction. Therefore, the proposition regarding catalytic pathway lowering activation energy is correct.

Step 4
The first and second propositions are incorrect, while the third proposition is correct.

चरण 1
कई प्राथमिक पदों वाली जटिल अभिक्रिया में, संपूर्ण अभिक्रिया की गति सबसे धीमे पद द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है, जिसे दर-निर्धारक पद कहा जाता है। सबसे तीव्र पद समग्र दर निर्धारित नहीं करता। अतः सबसे तीव्र पद द्वारा दर नियंत्रण से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

चरण 2
तीन या उससे अधिक अणुओं के एक ही क्षण और एक ही बिंदु पर उचित अभिविन्यास के साथ परस्पर टकराने की सांख्यिकीय संभावना अत्यंत नगण्य होती है। इसी कारण तीन आणविकता वाली प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाएँ अत्यंत दुर्लभ होती हैं तथा तीन से अधिक आणविकता वाली अभिक्रियाएँ नहीं पाई जाती हैं। अतः त्रिमॉलिक्यूलर अभिक्रियाओं के सामान्य होने का कथन गलत है।

चरण 3
उत्प्रेरक मध्यवर्ती संकुल बनाकर एक वैकल्पिक पथ उपलब्ध कराता है जिसकी संक्रियण ऊर्जा (\(E_a\)) मूल पथ से कम होती है। आर्हीनियस समीकरण \(k = A e^{-E_a/RT}\) के अनुसार संक्रियण ऊर्जा कम होने से प्रभावी टक्करों का अनुपात तेजी से बढ़ता है और अभिक्रिया तीव्र हो जाती है। अतः उत्प्रेरक द्वारा संक्रियण ऊर्जा घटाने का कथन सही है।

चरण 4
पहला और दूसरा कथन गलत है, जबकि तीसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I and Statement II are incorrect, but Statement III is correct.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Collision theory principles and temperature influence on rates

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: A catalyst increases the yield of products in a reversible reaction by shifting the chemical equilibrium constant toward the forward reaction.

Statement II: A \(10^\circ\text{C}\) rise in temperature nearly doubles the reaction rate primarily because the collision frequency between reacting molecules increases by \(100\%\).

Statement III: According to collision theory, in addition to possessing kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, colliding molecules must also have proper orientation for a collision to be effective.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक उत्प्रेरक रासायनिक साम्य स्थिरांक को अग्र अभिक्रिया की ओर विस्थापित करके एक उत्क्रमणीय अभिक्रिया में उत्पादों की लब्धि (यील्ड) को बढ़ा देता है।

कथन II: तापमान में \(10^\circ\text{C}\) की वृद्धि अभिक्रिया की दर को लगभग दोगुना कर देती है, इसका मुख्य कारण यह है कि टकराने वाले अणुओं के बीच संघट्ट आवृत्ति \(100\%\) बढ़ जाती है।

कथन III: संघट्ट सिद्धांत के अनुसार, संक्रियण ऊर्जा के बराबर या उससे अधिक गतिज ऊर्जा होने के अतिरिक्त, संघट्ट के प्रभावी होने के लिए टकराने वाले अणुओं का उचित अभिविन्यास भी आवश्यक है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
A catalyst accelerates both the forward and reverse reactions equally by reducing the activation energy for both directions by the exact same amount. Consequently, it does not alter the equilibrium constant (\(K_{\text{eq}}\)), the state of equilibrium, or the standard Gibbs free energy change (\(\Delta G^\circ\)); it merely reduces the time required to attain equilibrium. Therefore, the proposition that a catalyst alters the equilibrium constant or shifts equilibrium is incorrect.

Step 2
The collision frequency \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) is proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\). For a \(10^\circ\text{C}\) increase near room temperature, \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) increases by only about \(1\%\) to \(2\%\). The nearly twofold increase in reaction rate is instead governed by the Boltzmann factor \(e^{-E_a/RT}\), as the fraction of molecules possessing kinetic energy greater than or equal to \(E_a\) nearly doubles. Therefore, attributing the rate doubling to a \(100\%\) increase in collision frequency is incorrect.

Step 3
In collision theory, acquiring threshold energy (\(E \ge E_a\)) is a necessary but insufficient condition for product formation. Reacting species must collide with suitable geometric orientation so that the appropriate chemical bonds can break and new bonds can form simultaneously. This geometric requirement is incorporated via the steric factor \(P\) in the modified collision rate equation \(k = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_a/RT}\). Therefore, the proposition requiring proper orientation alongside activation energy is correct.

Step 4
The first and second propositions are incorrect, while the third proposition is correct.

चरण 1
उत्प्रेरक अग्र एवं पश्च दोनों अभिक्रियाओं की संक्रियण ऊर्जा को समान मात्रा में घटाकर दोनों की दरों को समान रूप से बढ़ाता है। अतः यह साम्य स्थिरांक (\(K_{\text{eq}}\)), साम्यावस्था की स्थिति अथवा मानक गिब्स ऊर्जा परिवर्तन (\(\Delta G^\circ\)) में कोई परिवर्तन नहीं करता; यह केवल साम्य तक पहुँचने के समय को कम करता है। अतः उत्प्रेरक द्वारा साम्य स्थिरांक बदलने का कथन गलत है।

चरण 2
संघट्ट आवृत्ति \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) तापमान के वर्गमूल (\(\sqrt{T}\)) के समानुपाती होती है। अतः \(10^\circ\text{C}\) तापमान वृद्धि से संघट्ट आवृत्ति में केवल \(1\%\) से \(2\%\) की ही वृद्धि होती है। दर के दोगुना होने का वास्तविक कारण बोल्ट्ज़मान पद \(e^{-E_a/RT}\) है, जिससे \(E_a\) या उससे अधिक ऊर्जा वाले अणुओं का अंश लगभग दोगुना हो जाता है। अतः संघट्ट आवृत्ति में \(100\%\) वृद्धि के दावे का कथन गलत है।

चरण 3
संघट्ट सिद्धांत के अनुसार, केवल संक्रियण ऊर्जा प्राप्त करना ही पर्याप्त नहीं है। उत्पाद निर्माण के लिए टकराने वाले अणुओं का उचित आकाशीय (ज्यामितीय) अभिविन्यास में होना भी अनिवार्य है ताकि पुराने बंध टूट सकें और नए बंध बन सकें। इसे संशोधित दर समीकरण \(k = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_a/RT}\) में त्रिविम कारक (स्टेरिक फैक्टर) \(P\) द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है। अतः संक्रियण ऊर्जा के साथ उचित अभिविन्यास आवश्यक होने का कथन सही है।

चरण 4
पहला और दूसरा कथन गलत है, जबकि तीसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II and Statement III are incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I and Statement II are incorrect, but Statement III is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Rate laws half life and surface catalysis

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: The unit of the rate constant for a zero-order reaction is identical to the unit of the reaction rate, which is \(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}\).

Statement II: A plot of \(\ln [\text{R}]\) versus time \(t\) for a first-order reaction gives a straight line with a positive slope equal to the rate constant \(k\).

Statement III: The half-life period of a first-order chemical reaction is completely independent of the initial concentration of the reactant.

Statement IV: The decomposition of gaseous ammonia on a hot platinum surface at high pressure is a zero-order reaction because the catalyst surface becomes saturated with gas molecules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: शून्य-कोटि की अभिक्रिया के दर स्थिरांक की इकाई अभिक्रिया की दर की इकाई के समान होती है, जो कि \(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}\) है।

कथन II: प्रथम-कोटि की अभिक्रिया के लिए समय \(t\) के विरुद्ध \(\ln [\text{R}]\) का आलेख दर स्थिरांक \(k\) के बराबर धनात्मक ढाल वाली एक सरल रेखा देता है।

कथन III: प्रथम-कोटि की रासायनिक अभिक्रिया का अर्ध-आयु काल अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता से पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र होता है।

कथन IV: उच्च दाब पर तप्त प्लैटिनम की सतह पर गैसीय अमोनिया का अपघटन एक शून्य-कोटि की अभिक्रिया है क्योंकि उत्प्रेरक की सतह गैस के अणुओं से संतृप्त हो जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
For a general reaction of order \(n\), the units of the rate constant are \((\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\ \text{s}^{-1}\). For a zero-order reaction (\(n = 0\)), the rate constant has units of \(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}\), which is identical to the units of reaction rate (change in molarity per second). Therefore, the proposition regarding zero-order rate constant units is correct.

Step 2
The integrated rate equation for a first-order reaction is \(\ln [\text{R}] = -kt + \ln [\text{R}]_0\). Comparing this with the linear form \(y = mx + c\), a plot of \(\ln [\text{R}]\) against \(t\) produces a straight line having a negative slope equal to \(-k\), rather than a positive slope. Therefore, the proposition asserting a positive slope for the first-order logarithmic plot is incorrect.

Step 3
For a first-order process, the half-life is given by \(t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}\). Because the initial reactant concentration term \([\text{R}]_0\) does not appear in this expression, the half-life is strictly constant and independent of the starting amount. Therefore, the proposition regarding first-order half-life independence is correct.

Step 4
In heterogeneous catalysis on metal surfaces at elevated pressures, the active platinum adsorption sites become completely saturated by adsorbed ammonia molecules. Consequently, increasing the gaseous ammonia concentration cannot further increase the amount adsorbed or the rate of reaction, reducing the rate expression to \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{NH}_3]^0 = k\). Therefore, the proposition regarding ammonia surface decomposition kinetics is correct.

Step 5
The first, third, and fourth propositions are correct, while the second proposition is incorrect.

चरण 1
\(n\) कोटि की अभिक्रिया के लिए दर स्थिरांक की इकाई \((\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\ \text{s}^{-1}\) होती है। शून्य-कोटि की अभिक्रिया (\(n = 0\)) के लिए दर स्थिरांक की इकाई \(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}\) होती है, जो अभिक्रिया की दर की इकाई के बिल्कुल समान है। अतः शून्य-कोटि दर स्थिरांक की इकाई से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 2
प्रथम-कोटि अभिक्रिया का समाकलित दर समीकरण \(\ln [\text{R}] = -kt + \ln [\text{R}]_0\) होता है। इसे \(y = mx + c\) से तुलना करने पर, \(t\) के विरुद्ध \(\ln [\text{R}]\) का आलेख \(-k\) के बराबर ऋणात्मक ढाल प्रदर्शित करता है, न कि धनात्मक ढाल। अतः धनात्मक ढाल बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 3
प्रथम-कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए अर्ध-आयु \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\) होती है। इस व्यंजक में प्रारंभिक सांद्रता \([\text{R}]_0\) का पद नहीं होता, अतः अर्ध-आयु प्रारंभिक सांद्रता से पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र होती है। अतः प्रथम-कोटि की अर्ध-आयु से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 4
उच्च दाब पर धातु की सतह पर उत्प्रेरण में, प्लैटिनम की सक्रिय सतह अमोनिया के अणुओं से पूर्णतः संतृप्त हो जाती है। परिणामस्वरूप, दाब या सांद्रता बढ़ाने पर भी सतह पर अधिशोषित अमोनिया की मात्रा और अभिक्रिया की दर नहीं बढ़ती, जिससे अभिक्रिया की दर \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{NH}_3]^0 = k\) हो जाती है। अतः अमोनिया के अपघटन से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 5
पहला, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही है, जबकि दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III and Statement IV are incorrect.
Statement I, Statement III, and Statement IV are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II, Statement III, and Statement IV are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Catalytic thermodynamics Arrhenius parameters and collision criteria

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: The presence of a catalyst increases the rates of both the forward and backward reactions to the same extent and does not alter the equilibrium constant of a reversible reaction.

Statement II: According to the Arrhenius equation, a plot of \(\ln k\) versus \(1/T\) produces a straight line with a slope equal to \(-E_{\text{a}}/R\) and an intercept equal to \(\ln A\).

Statement III: The nearly doubling of the reaction rate for a \(10^\circ\text{C}\) temperature rise is primarily caused by a twofold increase in the collision frequency \(Z_{\text{AB}}\).

Statement IV: In basic collision theory, reacting molecules are assumed to be deformable structures whose internal geometric orientations are inherently accounted for without introducing additional correction factors.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक उत्प्रेरक की उपस्थिति अग्र एवं पश्च दोनों अभिक्रियाओं की दरों को समान सीमा तक बढ़ाती है और एक उत्क्रमणीय अभिक्रिया के साम्य स्थिरांक को परिवर्तित नहीं करती है।

कथन II: आर्हीनियस समीकरण के अनुसार, \(1/T\) के विरुद्ध \(\ln k\) का आलेख \(-E_{\text{a}}/R\) के बराबर ढाल और \(\ln A\) के बराबर अंतःखंड वाली एक सरल रेखा देता है।

कथन III: \(10^\circ\text{C}\) तापमान वृद्धि पर अभिक्रिया दर का लगभग दोगुना होना मुख्य रूप से संघट्ट आवृत्ति \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) में दोगुनी वृद्धि के कारण होता है।

कथन IV: मूल संघट्ट सिद्धांत में, टकराने वाले अणुओं को विकृत होने वाली संरचनाएँ माना जाता है जिनके आंतरिक ज्यामितीय अभिविन्यास बिना किसी अतिरिक्त सुधार कारक के स्वतः समाहित होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
A catalyst provides an alternate pathway with a lower potential energy barrier that diminishes the activation energy for both the forward and backward reactions by the identical magnitude. Consequently, it accelerates both directions equally without shifting the equilibrium position or modifying the equilibrium constant \(K_{\text{eq}}\), merely facilitating faster attainment of equilibrium. Therefore, the proposition concerning catalytic influence on equilibrium is correct.

Step 2
Taking the natural logarithm of the Arrhenius relation \(k = A e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\) gives the linear equation \(\ln k = -\left(\frac{E_{\text{a}}}{R}\right)\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) + \ln A\). Matching this with \(y = mx + c\), a plot of \(\ln k\) against \(1/T\) is linear with a slope of \(-E_{\text{a}}/R\) and an intercept of \(\ln A\). Therefore, the proposition regarding the Arrhenius plot parameters is correct.

Step 3
Collision frequency \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) varies with the square root of absolute temperature (\(\sqrt{T}\)) and increases by merely \(1\%\) to \(2\%\) over a \(10^\circ\text{C}\) temperature rise. The exponential rate doubling is instead governed by the Boltzmann fraction \(e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\), which represents the proportion of reacting molecules possessing energy equal to or exceeding the activation threshold \(E_{\text{a}}\). Therefore, the proposition attributing rate doubling to collision frequency doubling is incorrect.

Step 4
Basic collision theory models reactant molecules as rigid, hard spheres and neglects their structural geometry and molecular complexity. Because all collisions between hard spheres do not possess proper spatial alignment to facilitate bond breaking and formation, an empirical steric or probability factor \(P\) must be explicitly introduced to yield \(\text{Rate} = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\). Therefore, the proposition claiming collision theory assumes deformable structures with inherent orientation accounting is incorrect.

Step 5
The first and second propositions are correct, while the third and fourth propositions are incorrect.

चरण 1
उत्प्रेरक कम स्थितिज ऊर्जा अवरोध वाला वैकल्पिक पथ प्रदान करता है जो अग्र एवं पश्च दोनों अभिक्रियाओं की संक्रियण ऊर्जा को समान मान से कम करता है। फलस्वरूप, यह दोनों दिशाओं को समान रूप से त्वरित करता है और साम्यावस्था की स्थिति अथवा साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_{\text{eq}}\) में कोई परिवर्तन नहीं करता, बल्कि केवल साम्यावस्था को शीघ्र प्राप्त करने में सहायता करता है। अतः साम्यावस्था पर उत्प्रेरक के प्रभाव से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 2
आर्हीनियस समीकरण \(k = A e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\) का प्राकृतिक लघुगणक लेने पर \(\ln k = -\left(\frac{E_{\text{a}}}{R}\right)\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) + \ln A\) प्राप्त होता है। \(y = mx + c\) से तुलना करने पर, \(1/T\) के विरुद्ध \(\ln k\) का आलेख \(-E_{\text{a}}/R\) ढाल और \(\ln A\) अंतःखंड वाली सरल रेखा होता है। अतः आर्हीनियस आलेख के प्राचलों से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 3
संघट्ट आवृत्ति \(Z_{\text{AB}}\) परम ताप के वर्गमूल (\(\sqrt{T}\)) के समानुपाती होती है और \(10^\circ\text{C}\) ताप वृद्धि पर इसमें केवल \(1\%\) से \(2\%\) की ही वृद्धि होती है। दर के दोगुना होने का कारण बोल्ट्ज़मान अंश \(e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\) है, जो संक्रियण ऊर्जा \(E_{\text{a}}\) के बराबर या उससे अधिक ऊर्जा रखने वाले अणुओं के अंश को लगभग दोगुना कर देता है। अतः संघट्ट आवृत्ति के दोगुना होने का दावा करने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 4
मूल संघट्ट सिद्धांत में अणुओं को कठोर गोले (हार्ड स्फीयर) माना जाता है और उनके संरचनात्मक पहलुओं की उपेक्षा की जाती है। चूंकि केवल ऊर्जा पर्याप्त नहीं होती और बंध निर्माण के लिए उचित आकाशीय अभिविन्यास आवश्यक होता है, इसलिए सिद्धांत में त्रिविम कारक (स्टेरिक फैक्टर) \(P\) को अलग से जोड़ना पड़ता है (\(\text{Rate} = P Z_{\text{AB}} e^{-E_{\text{a}}/RT}\))। अतः संघट्ट सिद्धांत में विकृत संरचना और स्वतः अभिविन्यास समाहित होने का कथन गलत है।

चरण 5
पहला और दूसरा कथन सही है, जबकि तीसरा और चौथा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV are all correct.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III and Statement IV are incorrect.
Statement III and Statement IV are correct, but Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q01 - Units of rate constant for reaction orders

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Order)List II (SI Units of Rate Constant)
A. Zero-order reactionI. \(\text{s}^{-1}\)
B. First-order reactionII. \(\text{mol}^{1/2}\cdot\text{L}^{-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)
C. Second-order reactionIII. \(\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)
D. Half-order reactionIV. \(\text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For an \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction, the general unit of the rate constant is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\). For a zero-order reaction (\(n = 0\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-0}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit III.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction (\(n = 1\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit I.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For a second-order reaction (\(n = 2\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For a half-order reaction (\(n = 1/2\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{1/2}\cdot\text{L}^{-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit II.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Pairing each reaction order with its corresponding SI unit yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q02 - Chemical reactions and their kinetic reaction categories

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Chemical Reaction)List II (Kinetic Classification)
A. Decomposition of ammonia on hot platinum at high pressureI. First-order chemical reaction
B. Hydrogenation of etheneII. Pseudo-first-order reaction
C. Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of ethyl acetate in excess waterIII. Nuclear first-order decay
D. Radioactive disintegration of radium-226IV. Zero-order heterogeneous catalytic reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
The decomposition of gaseous ammonia on a hot platinum catalyst at elevated pressure saturates the active metal surface, making the reaction rate independent of ammonia concentration. Thus, it is classified as a zero-order heterogeneous catalytic reaction (IV).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
The hydrogenation of ethene according to \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2(\text{g}) \to \text{C}_2\text{H}_6(\text{g})\) follows the differential rate law \(\text{Rate} = k[\text{C}_2\text{H}_4]\), which represents a classic first-order chemical reaction (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
In the acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate, water is present in enormous excess so that its concentration remains virtually unchanged throughout the reaction, simplifying the second-order rate expression to a pseudo-first-order reaction (II).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
All natural and artificial radioactive decays of unstable nuclei, including the alpha-decay of radium-226, follow first-order kinetics strictly governed by nuclear decay constants (III).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Combining these kinetic characteristics yields the one-to-one correspondence A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
Final Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q03 - Integrated rate equations and half life formulas

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic Parameter)List II (Mathematical Expression)
A. Integrated rate equation for zero-order reactionI. \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\)
B. Exponential concentration expression for first-order reactionII. \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\)
C. Half-life expression for zero-order reactionIII. \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\)
D. Half-life expression for first-order reactionIV. \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Integrating the zero-order differential equation \(-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\text{R}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k\) from \(t = 0\) to \(t\) yields \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\), matching expression II.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Integrating the first-order differential equation \(-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\text{R}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k[\text{R}]\) yields \(\ln\frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0} = -kt\), which upon exponentiation gives \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}\), matching expression IV.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
Setting \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0/2\) in the zero-order equation gives \(kt_{1/2} = [\text{R}]_0/2\), so \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\), matching expression I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
Setting \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0/2\) in the first-order equation gives \(t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}\), matching expression III.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Matching each kinetic parameter with its mathematical formula produces A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q04 - Linear kinetic plots and their corresponding slopes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Linear Graphical Plot)List II (Slope of the Straight Line)
A. \([\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) for a zero-order reactionI. \(\frac{k}{2.303}\)
B. \(\ln[\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) for a first-order reactionII. \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\)
C. \(\log\left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right)\) versus \(t\) for a first-order reactionIII. \(-k\) with vertical intercept \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\)
D. \(\ln k\) versus \(\frac{1}{T}\) in the Arrhenius equationIV. \(-k\) with vertical intercept \([\text{R}]_0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For a zero-order reaction, \([\text{R}] = -kt + [\text{R}]_0\). A plot of \([\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) yields a straight line with slope \(-k\) and intercept \([\text{R}]_0\), matching item IV.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction, \(\ln[\text{R}] = -kt + \ln[\text{R}]_0\). A plot of \(\ln[\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) yields a straight line with slope \(-k\) and intercept \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\), matching item III.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
Rearranging the first-order rate law gives \(\log\left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right) = \left(\frac{k}{2.303}\right)t\). A plot against \(t\) passes through the origin with slope \(\frac{k}{2.303}\), matching item I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
The logarithmic Arrhenius equation is \(\ln k = -\left(\frac{E_a}{R}\right)\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) + \ln A\). Plotting \(\ln k\) against \(1/T\) produces a straight line with slope \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\), matching item II.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Correlating each graph with its specific linear slope gives A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.
Final Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q05 - Percentage completion times for first order reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Extent of First-Order Reaction)List II (Time Required in Terms of Rate Constant \(k\))
A. \(50\%\) completionI. \(\frac{2.079}{k}\)
B. \(75\%\) completionII. \(\frac{0.693}{k}\)
C. \(87.5\%\) completionIII. \(\frac{6.909}{k}\)
D. \(99.9\%\) completionIV. \(\frac{1.386}{k}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For \(50\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.5[\text{R}]_0\). \(t_{50\%} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log 2 = \frac{0.693}{k}\), matching II.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For \(75\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.25[\text{R}]_0 = [\text{R}]_0/4\), which corresponds to 2 successive half-lives. \(t_{75\%} = 2 \times \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{1.386}{k}\), matching IV.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For \(87.5\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.125[\text{R}]_0 = [\text{R}]_0/8\), corresponding to 3 successive half-lives. \(t_{87.5\%} = 3 \times \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{2.079}{k}\), matching I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For \(99.9\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.001[\text{R}]_0 = 10^{-3}[\text{R}]_0\). \(t_{99.9\%} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log(10^3) = \frac{6.909}{k} \approx 10 t_{1/2}\), matching III.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Evaluating the logarithmic multiplier for each completion stage gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q06 - Mechanistic features of elementary and complex reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Entity)List II (Defining Mechanistic Feature)
A. Elementary reactionI. Proceeds via a sequence of steps; overall rate controlled by the bottleneck step
B. Complex reactionII. Provides an alternate reaction pathway with reduced activation energy without being consumed
C. Reaction intermediateIII. Occurs in a single event where molecularity and reaction order are identical
D. CatalystIV. Chemical species formed during an intermediate step and consumed before final products emerge

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
An elementary reaction occurs in a single isolated collision event; for all elementary reactions, the order with respect to each reactant equals its molecularity (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
A complex reaction occurs through a sequence of elementary steps termed the mechanism; its overall rate is dictated by the slowest rate-determining step (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
A reaction intermediate (such as \(\text{IO}^-\) in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide) is produced in an early elementary step and completely consumed in a subsequent step, never appearing in the net balanced equation (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
A catalyst interacts chemically with reactants to form a low-energy activated complex, increasing the reaction velocity, and is regenerated chemically unchanged upon completion (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Assigning each kinetic entity to its defining mechanistic feature gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q07 - External parameters and their kinetic acceleration mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Change in Condition)List II (Physical / Molecular Consequence)
A. Increase in reactant concentrationI. Broadens Maxwell-Boltzmann curve and roughly doubles fraction with \(E \ge E_a\)
B. Rise in temperature by \(10\text{ K}\)II. Increases number of accessible active adsorption sites on the surface
C. Addition of a positive catalystIII. Increases number of molecular collisions per second per unit volume
D. Finely dividing a solid catalystIV. Decreases activation energy barrier equally for forward and backward processes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Increasing the concentration increases the number of molecules per unit volume, which directly raises the collision frequency \(Z\) (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
A \(10\text{ K}\) rise in temperature shifts the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, nearly doubling the area corresponding to molecules possessing energy \(E \ge E_a\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
A positive catalyst provides an alternate reaction pathway with a lower potential energy barrier, reducing \(E_a\) equally for both directions (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
Finely dividing a solid catalyst drastically increases its specific surface area, providing more active catalytic sites for adsorption of reacting molecules (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Connecting each reaction condition alteration to its fundamental kinetic consequence yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q08 - Arrhenius parameters and collision theory kinetic factors

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic / Collision Theory Term)List II (Physical Interpretation)
A. Pre-exponential factor \(A\)I. Probability factor reflecting proper geometric molecular alignment during collision
B. Activation energy \(E_a\)II. Frequency factor representing the total collision rate per unit concentration
C. Steric factor \(P\)III. Fraction of colliding molecules possessing kinetic energy \(E \ge E_a\)
D. Exponential factor \(e^{-E_a/RT}\)IV. Energy difference between the activated complex and the reacting ground state

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
The Arrhenius pre-exponential factor \(A\) is the frequency factor, directly related to the total bimolecular collision frequency \(Z_{AB}\) in the system (II).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Activation energy \(E_a\) is the energy required to lift reacting species from their average reactant energy level to the peak of the activated complex barrier (IV).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
The steric factor \(P\) is introduced in collision theory (\(k = P Z_{AB} e^{-E_a/RT}\)) to account for the probability that colliding molecules possess mutually favorable spatial orientations to facilitate bond transformation (I).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
The Boltzmann exponential factor \(e^{-E_a/RT}\) represents the fraction of total molecules in the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution having energy equal to or exceeding \(E_a\) (III).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Aligning each collision theory term with its precise physical meaning gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q09 - Reaction order dependence of half life periods

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Order)List II (Half-Life Proportionality with Initial Concentration \([\text{R}]_0\))
A. Zero-order reactionI. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^0\) (independent of initial concentration)
B. First-order reactionII. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{1-n}\) (general \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order relation)
C. Second-order reactionIII. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^1\) (directly proportional to initial concentration)
D. General \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction (\(n \ne 1\))IV. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{-1}\) (inversely proportional to initial concentration)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For a zero-order reaction, \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\), which means \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^1\) (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction, \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\), which contains no concentration term, so \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^0\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For a second-order reaction, integration yields \(t_{1/2} = \frac{1}{k[\text{R}]_0}\), meaning \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{-1}\) (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For a general \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction where \(n \ne 1\), dimensional analysis and integration demonstrate that \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{1-n}\) (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Pairing each reaction order with its initial concentration power dependence yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q10 - Quantitative temperature dependence and activation energy calculations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic Situation / Problem)List II (Calculated Value / Quantitative Law)
A. Reaction rate doubles for a \(10\text{ K}\) rise from \(298\text{ K}\) to \(308\text{ K}\)I. \(\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]\)
B. Two-temperature integrated Arrhenius relationshipII. Activation energy \(E_a \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)
C. Fraction of molecules with \(E \ge E_a\) when \(E_a = 209.5\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) at \(581\text{ K}\)III. \(x = e^{-E_a/RT} \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-19}\)
D. Reaction rate quadruples for a \(20\text{ K}\) rise from \(293\text{ K}\) to \(313\text{ K}\)IV. Activation energy \(E_a \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Using the Arrhenius formula \(\log 2 = \frac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314}\left[\frac{10}{298 \times 308}\right]\), solving for \(E_a\) gives \(E_a = \frac{0.3010 \times 19.147 \times 91784}{10} \approx 52.897\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) (II).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Subtracting \(\ln k_1 = -\frac{E_a}{RT_1} + \ln A\) from \(\ln k_2 = -\frac{E_a}{RT_2} + \ln A\) and converting to base-10 logarithm gives \(\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
The fraction of molecules with \(E \ge E_a\) is \(x = e^{-E_a/RT}\). Taking \(\log x = -\frac{E_a}{2.303 RT} = -\frac{209500}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 581} = -18.832\). Taking antilog gives \(x = 10^{-18.832} = 10^{0.168 - 19} \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-19}\) (III).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
If the rate quadruples (\(k_2/k_1 = 4\)) between \(293\text{ K}\) and \(313\text{ K}\), \(\log 4 = 0.6021 = \frac{E_a}{19.147}\left[\frac{20}{293 \times 313}\right]\). Solving gives \(E_a = \frac{0.6021 \times 19.147 \times 91709}{20} \approx 52.86\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) (IV).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Matching each calculation problem with its exact numerical result or governing formula gives A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q01 - Average rate of reactant concentration change

questiontext.text: For the hypothetical reaction \(2\text{A} \rightarrow \text{Products}\), the concentration of reactant \(\text{A}\) decreases from \(0.50\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) to \(0.38\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) in \(10\text{ minutes}\). What is the average rate of the reaction during this time interval?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial concentration of reactant \(\text{A}\), \([\text{A}]_1 = 0.50\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Final concentration of reactant \(\text{A}\), \([\text{A}]_2 = 0.38\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Time taken, \(\Delta t = 10\text{ min}\).
Stoichiometric coefficient of \(\text{A}\) in the balanced chemical equation is \(2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The volume of the reaction mixture remains constant during the process.
By convention, the rate of reaction is always expressed as a positive quantity; hence a negative sign is applied to the rate of consumption of a reactant.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For the general reaction \(a\text{A} \rightarrow \text{Products}\), the average rate of reaction is defined as the rate of disappearance of reactant \(\text{A}\) divided by its stoichiometric coefficient \(a\):\[\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{a} \frac{\Delta [\text{A}]}{\Delta t} = -\frac{1}{a} \frac{[\text{A}]_2 - [\text{A}]_1}{\Delta t}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the change in concentration of reactant \(\text{A}\):\[\Delta [\text{A}] = 0.38\text{ mol L}^{-1} - 0.50\text{ mol L}^{-1} = -0.12\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]Substitute \(\Delta [\text{A}] = -0.12\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \(a = 2\), and \(\Delta t = 10\text{ min}\) into the rate expression:\[\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{-0.12\text{ mol L}^{-1}}{10\text{ min}}\right) = \frac{0.12}{20}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1} = 0.006\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional check: concentration divided by time yields \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\), which is correct for rate.
Physical check: the rate is positive and half the rate of disappearance of \(\text{A}\) (\(0.012\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\)).
Final Answer: The average rate of the reaction during this interval is \(0.006\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q02 - Rate of disappearance from appearance rate

questiontext.text: In an aqueous solution, the redox reaction proceeds according to the equation:\[5\text{Br}^-(\text{aq}) + \text{BrO}_3^-(\text{aq}) + 6\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 3\text{Br}_2(\text{aq}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\]If the rate of appearance of bromine, \(\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}_2]}{\Delta t}\), at a particular instant is \(1.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), what is the rate of disappearance of bromide ions, \(-\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}^-]}{\Delta t}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rate of appearance of \(\text{Br}_2\): \(\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}_2]}{\Delta t} = 1.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).
Stoichiometric coefficient of \(\text{Br}^-\) is \(5\).
Stoichiometric coefficient of \(\text{Br}_2\) is \(3\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction takes place in a homogeneous solution of constant volume.
The rate of disappearance is defined with a negative sign so that its numeric value is strictly positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a reaction with unequal stoichiometric coefficients, the rate of reaction is related to the rates of change of species by dividing each by its stoichiometric coefficient:\[\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{5}\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}^-]}{\Delta t} = \frac{1}{3}\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}_2]}{\Delta t}\]Rearranging to solve for the rate of disappearance of bromide ions:\[-\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}^-]}{\Delta t} = \frac{5}{3} \left(\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}_2]}{\Delta t}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}_2]}{\Delta t} = 1.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) into the relation:\[-\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}^-]}{\Delta t} = \frac{5}{3} \times (1.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1})\]\[-\frac{\Delta [\text{Br}^-]}{\Delta t} = 5 \times (0.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}) = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: Since 5 moles of bromide ions are consumed for every 3 moles of bromine formed, the rate of consumption of bromide must be greater than the rate of appearance of bromine by a factor of \(5/3 = 1.67\).
\(1.67 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-3} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), which confirms the calculation.
Final Answer: The rate of disappearance of bromide ions is \(3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q03 - Rate constant from first order half life

questiontext.text: The thermal decomposition of sulfuryl chloride, \(\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\), follows first-order kinetics. If the time required to decompose \(\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}_2\) to half of its initial amount is \(60\text{ minutes}\), what is the value of the rate constant of the reaction in \(\text{s}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Order of reaction: First order.
Half-life period, \(t_{1/2} = 60\text{ minutes}\).
Target unit of rate constant: \(\text{s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
First-order kinetics applies throughout the entire decomposition.
Time must be converted from minutes to seconds: \(1\text{ min} = 60\text{ s}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a first-order chemical reaction, the half-life period \(t_{1/2}\) is related to the rate constant \(k\) by the formula:\[t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}\]Rearranging for the rate constant:\[k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Convert half-life to seconds:\[t_{1/2} = 60\text{ min} \times 60\text{ s min}^{-1} = 3600\text{ s}\]Calculate the rate constant:\[k = \frac{0.693}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{0.693}{3.6 \times 10^3\text{ s}} = 0.1925 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1} = 1.925 \times 10^{-4}\text{ s}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Unit check: for a first-order reaction, \(k\) has the dimension of \(\text{time}^{-1}\), which matches \(\text{s}^{-1}\).
Numerical check: \(1.925 \times 10^{-4} \times 3600 = 0.693\), which verifies exact reciprocal consistency.
Final Answer: The rate constant of the reaction is \(1.925 \times 10^{-4}\text{ s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q04 - Overall order from experimental rate expression

questiontext.text: A chemical reaction has the experimentally determined rate expression:\[\text{Rate} = k [\text{A}]^{3/2} [\text{B}]^{-1/2} [\text{C}]^{1}\]What is the overall order of this reaction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rate expression: \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{A}]^x [\text{B}]^y [\text{C}]^z\).
Exponent with respect to reactant \(\text{A}\): \(x = 3/2\).
Exponent with respect to reactant \(\text{B}\): \(y = -1/2\).
Exponent with respect to reactant \(\text{C}\): \(z = 1\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction order is defined solely by the powers of concentration terms appearing in the experimental rate law, irrespective of the balanced equation stoichiometry.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The overall order of a reaction, denoted as \(n\), is the algebraic sum of the exponents of all concentration terms present in the rate expression:\[n = x + y + z\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the individual exponents into the summation:\[n = \frac{3}{2} + \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + 1\]Combine the fractional terms:\[\frac{3}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{2} = 1\]Add the remaining integer:\[n = 1 + 1 = 2\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(1.5 - 0.5 + 1.0 = 2.0\). An overall order of 2 signifies that the reaction behaves overall as a second-order reaction.
Final Answer: The overall order of the reaction is \(2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q05 - Rate constant evaluation from initial rates

questiontext.text:
For the gas-phase reaction \(2\text{NO}(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2(\text{g})\), kinetic measurements at constant temperature yielded the following initial rate data:

ExperimentInitial \([\text{NO}]\text{ (mol L}^{-1})\)Initial \([\text{O}_2]\text{ (mol L}^{-1})\)Initial Rate of Formation of \(\text{NO}_2\text{ (mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1})\)
10.300.300.096
20.600.300.384
30.300.600.192

What is the numerical value of the rate constant \(k\) in \(\text{mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Experiment 1: \([\text{NO}] = 0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \([\text{O}_2] = 0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \(\text{Rate}_1 = 0.096\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).
Experiment 2: \([\text{NO}] = 0.60\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \([\text{O}_2] = 0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \(\text{Rate}_2 = 0.384\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).
Experiment 3: \([\text{NO}] = 0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \([\text{O}_2] = 0.60\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \(\text{Rate}_3 = 0.192\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The rate law has the form \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{NO}]^x [\text{O}_2]^y\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are the reaction orders with respect to \(\text{NO}\) and \(\text{O}_2\) respectively.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Comparing Experiment 2 to Experiment 1 (where \([\text{O}_2]\) is constant):\[\frac{\text{Rate}_2}{\text{Rate}_1} = \left(\frac{[\text{NO}]_2}{[\text{NO}]_1}\right)^x \implies \frac{0.384}{0.096} = \left(\frac{0.60}{0.30}\right)^x \implies 4 = 2^x \implies x = 2\]Comparing Experiment 3 to Experiment 1 (where \([\text{NO}]\) is constant):\[\frac{\text{Rate}_3}{\text{Rate}_1} = \left(\frac{[\text{O}_2]_3}{[\text{O}_2]_1}\right)^y \implies \frac{0.192}{0.096} = \left(\frac{0.60}{0.30}\right)^y \implies 2 = 2^y \implies y = 1\]Thus, the rate law is: \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{NO}]^2 [\text{O}_2]\).
Rearranging for the rate constant: \(k = \frac{\text{Rate}}{[\text{NO}]^2 [\text{O}_2]}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Using the data from Experiment 1:\[k = \frac{0.096\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}}{(0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1})^2 \times (0.30\text{ mol L}^{-1})}\]\[k = \frac{0.096}{0.090 \times 0.30} = \frac{0.096}{0.027} = 3.5556\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1} \approx 3.56\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verify with Experiment 2:\[k = \frac{0.384}{(0.60)^2 \times (0.30)} = \frac{0.384}{0.36 \times 0.30} = \frac{0.384}{0.108} \approx 3.56\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\]Unit check: \(\frac{\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}}{(\text{mol L}^{-1})^3} = \text{mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\).
Final Answer: The value of the rate constant is \(3.56\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q06 - Reaction rate after reactant partial consumption

questiontext.text: For the reaction \(2\text{A} + \text{B} \rightarrow \text{A}_2\text{B}\), the rate law is given by:\[\text{Rate} = k [\text{A}] [\text{B}]^2\]with \(k = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\). Initially, the concentrations are \([\text{A}] = 0.10\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) and \([\text{B}] = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}\). What is the rate of the reaction when \([\text{A}]\) is reduced to \(0.06\text{ mol L}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial concentrations: \([\text{A}]_0 = 0.10\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), \([\text{B}]_0 = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Final concentration of \(\text{A}\): \([\text{A}] = 0.06\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Rate constant: \(k = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}\).
Stoichiometry: 2 moles of \(\text{A}\) react with 1 mole of \(\text{B}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction proceeds in a closed vessel at constant volume so that changes in concentration directly reflect stoichiometric molar consumption.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Amount of \(\text{A}\) consumed: \(\Delta [\text{A}] = [\text{A}]_0 - [\text{A}]\).
Amount of \(\text{B}\) consumed based on reaction stoichiometry:\[\Delta [\text{B}] = \frac{1}{2} \Delta [\text{A}]\]Remaining concentration of \(\text{B}\): \([\text{B}] = [\text{B}]_0 - \Delta [\text{B}]\).
Rate law: \(\text{Rate} = k [\text{A}] [\text{B}]^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the decrease in concentration of \(\text{A}\):\[\Delta [\text{A}] = 0.10\text{ mol L}^{-1} - 0.06\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.04\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]Determine the decrease in concentration of \(\text{B}\):\[\Delta [\text{B}] = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.04\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]Determine the remaining concentration of \(\text{B}\):\[[\text{B}] = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1} - 0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.18\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]Calculate the new rate of reaction:\[\text{Rate} = (2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}) \times (0.06\text{ mol L}^{-1}) \times (0.18\text{ mol L}^{-1})^2\]\[(0.18)^2 = 0.0324\text{ mol}^2\text{L}^{-2}\]\[\text{Rate} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.06 \times 0.0324 = 2.0 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.001944 = 3.888 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\]\[\text{Rate} \approx 3.89 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Initial rate was \(2.0 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.10 \times 0.04 = 8.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).
As both reactants are consumed, the rate must decrease below the initial rate. \(3.89 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1} < 8.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), which is physically sound.
Final Answer: The rate of the reaction when \([\text{A}]\) is reduced to \(0.06\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) is \(3.89 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q07 - Time required for first order reactant depletion

questiontext.text:
A first-order reaction has a rate constant \(k = 1.15 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}\). How long (in seconds) will it take for \(5.0\text{ g}\) of this reactant to be reduced to \(3.0\text{ g}\)?

[Given: \(\log_{10} 5 = 0.6990\), \(\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771\), \(\log_{10}(5/3) = 0.2219\)]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rate constant, \(k = 1.15 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}\).
Initial amount of reactant, \([\text{R}]_0 = 5.0\text{ g}\).
Final amount of reactant, \([\text{R}] = 3.0\text{ g}\).
\(\log_{10}(5/3) = 0.2219\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction adheres strictly to first-order integrated kinetics.
The ratio of masses can be used directly in place of molar concentration ratios because volume and molar mass are constant.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The integrated rate equation for a first-order reaction is:\[t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10} \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the equation:\[t = \frac{2.303}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}} \log_{10} \left(\frac{5.0\text{ g}}{3.0\text{ g}}\right)\]Evaluate the division:\[\frac{2.303}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} = 2002.61\text{ s}\]Multiply by \(\log_{10}(1.667) = 0.2219\):\[t = 2002.61 \times 0.2219 = 444.38\text{ s} \approx 444\text{ s}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Half-life of this reaction is \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 602.6\text{ s}\).
Reducing from \(5.0\text{ g}\) to \(2.5\text{ g}\) would require \(602.6\text{ s}\). Since reducing to \(3.0\text{ g}\) is less than one half-life, the required time must be less than \(603\text{ s}\). The calculated value of \(444\text{ s}\) is completely consistent.
Final Answer: The time required is \(444\text{ s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q08 - Time for completion of zero order reaction

questiontext.text: A zero-order reaction \(\text{R} \rightarrow \text{P}\) begins with an initial concentration of \([\text{R}]_0 = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) and has a rate constant \(k = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\). What is the time required for the reaction to reach \(75\%\) completion?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction order: Zero order.
Initial concentration, \([\text{R}]_0 = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Rate constant, \(k = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).
Percentage completion: \(75\%\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In zero-order kinetics, the rate is independent of reactant concentration until the reactant is entirely depleted.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The integrated rate law for a zero-order reaction is:\[[\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt \implies kt = [\text{R}]_0 - [\text{R}]\]Rearranging for time:\[t = \frac{[\text{R}]_0 - [\text{R}]}{k} = \frac{\Delta [\text{R}]_{\text{reacted}}}{k}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the amount of reactant consumed at \(75\%\) completion:\[\Delta [\text{R}]_{\text{reacted}} = 0.75 \times [\text{R}]_0 = 0.75 \times 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.15\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]Substitute into the time expression:\[t = \frac{0.15\text{ mol L}^{-1}}{4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}} = \frac{0.15}{0.0040}\text{ s} = 37.5\text{ s}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The half-life of this zero-order reaction is \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k} = \frac{0.20}{2 \times 0.004} = 25.0\text{ s}\).
The time for \(100\%\) completion is \(t_{100\%} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{k} = \frac{0.20}{0.004} = 50.0\text{ s}\).
Because rate is constant in a zero-order reaction, \(75\%\) completion must occur at exactly \(0.75 \times 50.0\text{ s} = 37.5\text{ s}\).
Final Answer: The time required for \(75\%\) completion is \(37.5\text{ s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q09 - Time to reach fractional concentration in decay

questiontext.text: The rate constant for a first-order decomposition reaction is \(6.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}\). How much time (in seconds) will it take to reduce the initial concentration of the reactant to \(1/16^{\text{th}}\) of its initial value?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rate constant, \(k = 6.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}\).
Final concentration, \([\text{R}] = \frac{1}{16} [\text{R}]_0\).
Reaction order: First order.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction obeys first-order kinetics throughout all successive decay periods.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Method 1: Half-life relation.
Since \(\frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0} = \frac{1}{16} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4\), the elapsed time corresponds to exactly \(4\) half-lives (\(n = 4\)):
\(t = 4 \times t_{1/2}\), where \(t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}\).
Method 2: Integrated rate law.
\(t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10} \left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10}(16)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the half-life period:\[t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{6.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}} = \frac{0.693}{0.060}\text{ s} = 11.55\text{ s}\]Calculate the total time for 4 half-lives:\[t = 4 \times 11.55\text{ s} = 46.2\text{ s}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Using the logarithmic formula directly:\[t = \frac{2.303}{0.060} \times 4 \times \log_{10} 2 = \frac{2.303}{0.060} \times 4 \times 0.3010 = 38.383 \times 1.204 = 46.21\text{ s}\]Both methods give identical results.
Final Answer: The time required is \(46.2\text{ s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q10 - Age of archaeological artifact by radiocarbon decay

questiontext.text:
The half-life for radioactive decay of \(^{14}\text{C}\) is \(5730\text{ years}\). An archaeological artifact containing wood was found to have only \(80\%\) of the \(^{14}\text{C}\) activity found in a living tree. Estimate the age of the artifact in years.

[Given: \(\log_{10} 2 = 0.3010\), \(\log_{10}(1.25) = 0.0969\)]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Half-life of \(^{14}\text{C}\), \(t_{1/2} = 5730\text{ years}\).
Current activity / initial activity ratio, \(\frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0} = 80\% = 0.80\).
\(\log_{10}(100/80) = \log_{10}(1.25) = 0.0969\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All radioactive decays follow first-order kinetics.
The initial concentration of \(^{14}\text{C}\) in living organisms has remained constant over the timescale under consideration.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The decay constant \(\lambda\) (or \(k\)) is related to half-life by:\[k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}\]The age \(t\) is determined from the first-order integrated rate law:\[t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10} \left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right) = \frac{2.303 \times t_{1/2}}{0.693} \log_{10} \left(\frac{100}{80}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(t_{1/2} = 5730\text{ years}\) into the decay constant expression:\[k = \frac{0.693}{5730\text{ yr}} = 1.2094 \times 10^{-4}\text{ yr}^{-1}\]Calculate the age \(t\):\[t = \frac{2.303}{1.2094 \times 10^{-4}\text{ yr}^{-1}} \times \log_{10}(1.25)\]\[t = 19042.5 \times 0.0969\text{ yr} = 1845.2\text{ years} \approx 1846\text{ years}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
At 1 half-life (\(5730\text{ yr}\)), activity is \(50\%\).
Since \(80\%\) activity remains, the age must be substantially less than half a half-life (\(2865\text{ yr}\)). An age of \(1846\text{ years}\) is physically reasonable and consistent.
Final Answer: The estimated age of the artifact is \(1846\text{ years}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q11 - Rate of product appearance in decomposition

questiontext.text: The decomposition of dinitrogen pentoxide in carbon tetrachloride at \(318\text{ K}\) proceeds as:\[2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{g}) \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})\]Initially, the concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) is \(2.33\text{ mol L}^{-1}\), and after \(184\text{ minutes}\), it decreases to \(2.08\text{ mol L}^{-1}\). What is the average rate of production of \(\text{NO}_2\) during this period?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\): \([\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]_1 = 2.33\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Final concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\): \([\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]_2 = 2.08\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Time interval: \(\Delta t = 184\text{ min}\).
Reaction: \(2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction takes place in a closed vessel with constant volume.
The rate of production (appearance) is inherently positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
