Final Conceptual Conclusion: The assertions regarding the high-temperature conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol and the facile hydrolysis of 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene with warm water are correct, whereas the claim that a meta-nitro group accelerates substitution via resonance carbanion stabilisation is incorrect.

चरण 1: क्लोरोबेन्जीन के जलअपघटन के लिए डाऊ प्रक्रम का मूल्यांकन
अनुनाद के कारण आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण, एरोमैटिक कार्बन के \(sp^2\) संकरण तथा \(\pi\)-इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रतिकर्षण के कारण अक्रियकृत ऐरिल हैलाइड नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति अत्यंत कम क्रियाशील होते हैं। क्लोरोबेन्जीन से फीनॉल प्राप्त करने के लिए कठोर परिस्थितियों की आवश्यकता होती है: \(623\,\mathrm{K}\) ताप तथा \(300\,\mathrm{atm}\) दाब पर जलीय \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) के साथ गर्म करना और तत्पश्चात अम्लीकरण। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: मेटा-नाइट्रो समूह के अनुनाद प्रभाव का विश्लेषण
इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक नाइट्रो समूह (\(-\mathrm{NO}_2\)) केवल तभी नाभिकरागी एरोमैटिक प्रतिस्थापन को सक्रिय करता है जब वह ऑर्थो या पैरा स्थिति पर स्थित हो। मध्यवर्ती कार्बेनायन (माइसेनहाइमर संकुल) में ऋणावेश केवल ऑर्थो और पैरा स्थितियों से ही नाइट्रो समूह के ऑक्सीजन परमाणुओं पर विस्थानिकृत होता है। मेटा-स्थिति पर, किसी भी अनुनादी संरचना में नाइट्रो समूह वाले कार्बन पर ऋणावेश नहीं आता; अतः मेटा-नाइट्रो समूह अनुनाद द्वारा कार्बेनायन को स्थायित्व प्रदान नहीं कर पाता। इसलिए मेटा-स्थिति पर तीव्र सक्रियण का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन की क्रियाशीलता का मूल्यांकन
2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन में दोनों ऑर्थो तथा पैरा स्थितियों पर तीन प्रबल इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक नाइट्रो समूह उपस्थित होते हैं। ये वलय से इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व खींचकर मध्यवर्ती के ऋणावेश को अत्यधिक विस्थानिकृत कर देते हैं। इस कारण सक्रियण ऊर्जा इतनी कम हो जाती है कि केवल \(323\,\mathrm{K}\) पर गर्म जल के साथ हिलाने मात्र से ही क्लोरीन प्रतिस्थापित होकर 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोफीनॉल (पिक्रिक अम्ल) बन जाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष का संश्लेषण
क्लोरोबेन्जीन से फीनॉल के कठोर परिस्थितियों में रूपांतरण तथा 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन के गर्म जल द्वारा सुगम जलअपघटन से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि मेटा-नाइट्रो समूह द्वारा अनुनादी स्थायित्व का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक निष्कर्ष: क्लोरोबेन्जीन से फीनॉल के कठोर परिस्थितियों में रूपांतरण तथा 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन के गर्म जल द्वारा सुगम जलअपघटन से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि मेटा-नाइट्रो समूह द्वारा अनुनादी स्थायित्व का दावा गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_STM4_Q01 - Preparation and stereochemical aspects of haloalkanes

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Thionyl chloride (\(\mathrm{SOCl}_2\)) is preferred for preparing alkyl chlorides from alcohols because the other reaction products (\(\mathrm{SO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\)) are escapable gases.

Statement II: Free-radical chlorination of alkanes gives a clean, single monochloroalkane in high yield.

Statement III: The Finkelstein reaction involves the conversion of alkyl chlorides or bromides into alkyl iodides using sodium iodide in dry acetone.

Statement IV: The unimolecular nucleophilic substitution (\(S_N1\)) of an optically active haloalkane proceeds with complete retention of configuration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: ऐल्कोहॉल से ऐल्किल क्लोराइड बनाने के लिए थायोनाइल क्लोराइड (\(\mathrm{SOCl}_2\)) को प्राथमिकता दी जाती है क्योंकि अभिक्रिया के अन्य उत्पाद (\(\mathrm{SO}_2\) और \(\mathrm{HCl}\)) पलायनशील गैसें होती हैं।

कथन II: ऐल्केनों का मुक्त मूलक क्लोरीनीकरण उच्च लब्धि (yield) में एक शुद्ध, एकल मोनोक्लोरोऐल्केन प्रदान करता है।

कथन III: फिंकेलस्टाइन अभिक्रिया में शुष्क ऐसीटोन में सोडियम आयोडाइड का उपयोग करके ऐल्किल क्लोराइड या ब्रोमाइड को ऐल्किल आयोडाइड में परिवर्तित किया जाता है।

कथन IV: एक प्रकाशिक रूप से सक्रिय हैलोऐल्केन का एक-अणुक नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन (\(S_N1\)) विन्यास के पूर्ण धारण (retention) के साथ संपन्न होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the reaction between alcohols and thionyl chloride
When alcohols react with thionyl chloride, the reaction equation is: \(\mathrm{R-OH} + \mathrm{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R-Cl} + \mathrm{SO}_2\uparrow + \mathrm{HCl}\uparrow\). Because both sulfur dioxide and hydrogen chloride are volatile gases that escape from the reaction mixture, the alkyl chloride is obtained in pure form without tedious separation. Thus, this assertion is scientifically correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the free-radical halogenation of alkanes
Free-radical chlorination of alkanes proceeds through non-selective radical intermediates, typically resulting in a complex mixture of isomeric monochloroalkanes as well as polyhalogenated derivatives that are difficult to separate, yielding very low amounts of any single pure product. Thus, asserting that it gives a single monochloroalkane in high yield is scientifically incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Finkelstein halogen exchange reaction
In the Finkelstein reaction, alkyl chlorides or alkyl bromides are treated with sodium iodide dissolved in dry acetone: \(\mathrm{R-X} + \mathrm{NaI} \xrightarrow{\text{acetone}} \mathrm{R-I} + \mathrm{NaX}\downarrow\) (where \(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Cl, Br}\)). Sodium chloride and sodium bromide precipitate out in dry acetone due to poor solubility, driving the reaction forward according to Le Chatelier's principle. Hence, this assertion is scientifically correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the stereochemical outcome of unimolecular substitution
In an \(S_N1\) mechanism, the rate-determining step produces an achiral, planar carbocation intermediate. The incoming nucleophile can attack the planar carbocation with comparable likelihood from both the front and rear faces, yielding an equimolar mixture of enantiomers (racemisation), rather than complete retention of configuration. Thus, claiming complete retention of configuration is scientifically incorrect.

Step 5: Synthesis of the conceptual conclusion
The assertions regarding the advantage of using thionyl chloride for alkyl chloride synthesis and the conversion of haloalkanes to alkyl iodides via the Finkelstein reaction are correct, whereas the claims of selective alkane chlorination and complete stereochemical retention during unimolecular nucleophilic substitution are incorrect.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: The assertions regarding the advantage of using thionyl chloride for alkyl chloride synthesis and the conversion of haloalkanes to alkyl iodides via the Finkelstein reaction are correct, whereas the claims of selective alkane chlorination and complete stereochemical retention during unimolecular nucleophilic substitution are incorrect.

चरण 1: ऐल्कोहॉल और थायोनाइल क्लोराइड की अभिक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
जब ऐल्कोहॉल थायोनाइल क्लोराइड के साथ अभिक्रिया करता है, तो अभिक्रिया इस प्रकार होती है: \(\mathrm{R-OH} + \mathrm{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R-Cl} + \mathrm{SO}_2\uparrow + \mathrm{HCl}\uparrow\)। चूँकि सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड और हाइड्रोजन क्लोराइड दोनों गैसीय उत्पाद हैं और अभिक्रिया मिश्रण से बाहर निकल जाते हैं, अतः शुद्ध ऐल्किल क्लोराइड प्राप्त होता है। अतः यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही है।

चरण 2: ऐल्केनों के मुक्त मूलक हैलोजनीकरण का मूल्यांकन
ऐल्केनों का मुक्त मूलक क्लोरीनीकरण विभिन्न समावयवी मोनो- तथा पॉली-हैलोऐल्केनों का एक जटिल मिश्रण देता है जिन्हें शुद्ध रूप में अलग करना कठिन होता है, जिससे किसी एकल यौगिक की लब्धि बहुत कम होती है। अतः उच्च लब्धि में एकल मोनोक्लोरोऐल्केन मिलने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: फिंकेलस्टाइन हैलोजन विनिमय अभिक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
फिंकेलस्टाइन अभिक्रिया में शुष्क ऐसीटोन में ऐल्किल क्लोराइड या ब्रोमाइड की अभिक्रिया सोडियम आयोडाइड से कराई जाती है: \(\mathrm{R-X} + \mathrm{NaI} \xrightarrow{\text{ऐसीटोन}} \mathrm{R-I} + \mathrm{NaX}\downarrow\) (जहाँ \(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Cl, Br}\))। ऐसीटोन में सोडियम क्लोराइड या ब्रोमाइड अवक्षेपित हो जाते हैं, जिससे ला-शातेलिए नियम के अनुसार अग्र अभिक्रिया सुगम होती है। अतः यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही है।

चरण 4: एक-अणुक प्रतिस्थापन के त्रिविम-रासायनिक परिणाम का मूल्यांकन
\(S_N1\) क्रियाविधि में मध्यवर्ती एक समतलीय कार्बधनायन बनता है। समतलीय ज्यामिति के कारण नाभिकरागी दोनों फलकों से समान रूप से आक्रमण कर सकता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप रेसिमीकरण होता है, न कि पूर्ण विन्यास धारण। अतः पूर्ण धारण का दावा वैज्ञानिक रूप से गलत है।

चरण 5: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष का संश्लेषण
थायोनाइल क्लोराइड के उपयोग के लाभ तथा फिंकेलस्टाइन अभिक्रिया द्वारा ऐल्किल आयोडाइड बनाने से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि मुक्त मूलक क्लोरीनीकरण की चयनात्मकता और एक-अणुक प्रतिस्थापन में पूर्ण विन्यास धारण से संबंधित दावे गलत हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक निष्कर्ष: थायोनाइल क्लोराइड के उपयोग के लाभ तथा फिंकेलस्टाइन अभिक्रिया द्वारा ऐल्किल आयोडाइड बनाने से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि मुक्त मूलक क्लोरीनीकरण की चयनात्मकता और एक-अणुक प्रतिस्थापन में पूर्ण विन्यास धारण से संबंधित दावे गलत हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_STM4_Q02 - Nucleophilic reactivity and environmental aspects of polyhalogens

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Haloalkanes react with potassium cyanide (\(\mathrm{KCN}\)) to yield predominantly alkyl cyanides, whereas reaction with silver cyanide (\(\mathrm{AgCN}\)) yields predominantly isocyanides.

Statement II: In haloarenes, the carbon-halogen bond is shorter and stronger than in haloalkanes because the carbon atom attached to the halogen is \(sp^2\)-hybridised and resonance imparts partial double bond character.

Statement III: In dehydrohalogenation (Saytzeff elimination) of haloalkanes, the preferred product is the alkene having the lesser number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms.

Statement IV: 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene undergoes nucleophilic substitution to form picric acid simply upon warming with water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: हैलोऐल्केन पोटैशियम सायनाइड (\(\mathrm{KCN}\)) के साथ अभिक्रिया करके मुख्य रूप से ऐल्किल सायनाइड बनाते हैं, जबकि सिल्वर सायनाइड (\(\mathrm{AgCN}\)) के साथ अभिक्रिया करने पर मुख्य रूप से आइसोसायनाइड प्राप्त होता है।

कथन II: हैलोऐरीन में कार्बन-हैलोजन आबंध हैलोऐल्केन की तुलना में छोटा और अधिक प्रबल होता है क्योंकि हैलोजन से जुड़ा कार्बन परमाणु \(sp^2\)-संकरित होता है तथा अनुनाद के कारण आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण आ जाता है।

कथन III: हैलोऐल्केनों के विहाइड्रोहैलोजनीकरण (सैत्ज़ेफ विलोपन) में, मुख्य उत्पाद वह ऐल्कीन होती है जिसमें द्वि-आबंधित कार्बन परमाणुओं पर ऐल्किल समूहों की संख्या कम होती है।

कथन IV: 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन केवल जल के साथ हल्का गर्म करने पर ही नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन प्रदर्शित करके पिक्रिक अम्ल बनाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of ambident nucleophile substitution with cyanide salts
Potassium cyanide (\(\mathrm{KCN}\)) is predominantly ionic in nature and releases ambident cyanide ions (\([\mathrm{:C\equiv N:}]^-\)). The attack on the carbocationic center takes place predominantly through the carbon atom because the formation of a \(\mathrm{C-C}\) single bond is thermodynamically more stable than a \(\mathrm{C-N}\) bond, yielding alkyl cyanides. In contrast, silver cyanide (\(\mathrm{AgCN}\)) is covalent, with the carbon-silver bond largely intact, leaving the lone pair on nitrogen free to attack, predominantly forming alkyl isocyanides. Hence, this assertion is scientifically correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of bond hybridisation and resonance in haloarenes
In haloarenes, the halogen-bearing carbon is \(sp^2\)-hybridised with greater \(s\)-character (\(33.3\%\)), holding electrons closer and resulting in a shorter bond length (\(169\,\mathrm{pm}\) compared to \(177\,\mathrm{pm}\) in haloalkanes). Moreover, the halogen unshared pairs conjugate with the aromatic \(\pi\)-system, imparting partial double bond character to the \(\mathrm{C-X}\) bond, which makes it significantly stronger and more resistant to cleavage. Hence, this assertion is scientifically correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Saytzeff's elimination rule
According to Saytzeff's rule for dehydrohalogenation (\(\beta\)-elimination) of haloalkanes, the preferred and predominant alkene product is the one that possesses the greater number of alkyl substituents attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms (the more substituted, thermodynamically more stable alkene). Stating that the alkene with fewer alkyl groups is preferred is scientifically incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of nucleophilic substitution in polynitro haloarenes
In 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, the presence of three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups situated at both ortho positions and the para position disperses the developing negative charge of the Meisenheimer intermediate exceptionally effectively across the ring and nitro oxygens. This drastic activation allows the chlorine leaving group to be displaced smoothly simply by warming with neutral water at \(323\,\mathrm{K}\) to form 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid). Hence, this assertion is scientifically correct.

Step 5: Synthesis of the conceptual conclusion
The assertions concerning the divergent nucleophilic substitution products with potassium cyanide versus silver cyanide, the shortening and strengthening of the carbon-halogen bond in haloarenes through hybridisation and resonance, and the facile hydrolysis of 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene with water are correct, whereas the formulation of Saytzeff's rule specifying an alkene with fewer alkyl groups is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: The assertions concerning the divergent nucleophilic substitution products with potassium cyanide versus silver cyanide, the shortening and strengthening of the carbon-halogen bond in haloarenes through hybridisation and resonance, and the facile hydrolysis of 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene with water are correct, whereas the formulation of Saytzeff's rule specifying an alkene with fewer alkyl groups is incorrect.

चरण 1: सायनाइड लवणों के साथ उभयदंती नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन का मूल्यांकन
पोटैशियम सायनाइड (\(\mathrm{KCN}\)) मुख्य रूप से आयनिक होता है और विलयन में सायनाइड आयन प्रदान करता है। \(\mathrm{C-C}\) आबंध \(\mathrm{C-N}\) आबंध की तुलना में अधिक स्थायी होने के कारण आक्रमण मुख्यतः कार्बन परमाणु द्वारा होता है, जिससे ऐल्किल सायनाइड बनता है। दूसरी ओर, सिल्वर सायनाइड (\(\mathrm{AgCN}\)) मुख्य रूप से सहसंयोजक होता है और नाइट्रोजन परमाणु इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म दान करने के लिए स्वतंत्र होता है, जिससे मुख्य उत्पाद आइसोसायनाइड बनता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: हैलोऐरीन में संकरण और अनुनाद प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन
हैलोऐरीन में हैलोजन से जुड़ा कार्बन \(sp^2\)-संकरित होता है जिसमें \(s\)-लक्षण अधिक (\(33.3\%\)) होता है, जिससे आबंध लंबाई घटकर \(169\,\mathrm{pm}\) रह जाती है (हैलोऐल्केन में \(177\,\mathrm{pm}\))। साथ ही, अनुनाद के कारण \(\mathrm{C-X}\) आबंध में आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण आ जाता है, जिससे यह अधिक प्रबल और विदलन के प्रति प्रतिरोधी हो जाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: सैत्ज़ेफ विलोपन नियम का मूल्यांकन
सैत्ज़ेफ नियम के अनुसार, हैलोऐल्केनों के विहाइड्रोहैलोजनीकरण में मुख्य उत्पाद वह ऐल्कीन होती है जिसमें द्वि-आबंधित कार्बनों से जुड़े ऐल्किल समूहों की संख्या अधिक (अधिक प्रतिस्थापित ऐल्कीन) होती है। अतः कम ऐल्किल समूहों वाली ऐल्कीन के मुख्य होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: पॉलीनाइट्रो हैलोऐरीन में नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन का मूल्यांकन
2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन में दोनों ऑर्थो और पैरा स्थितियों पर तीन प्रबल इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक नाइट्रो समूह उपस्थित होते हैं। ये मध्यवर्ती कार्बेनायन के ऋणावेश को अत्यधिक स्थायित्व प्रदान करते हैं। इसके फलस्वरूप केवल गर्म जल (\(323\,\mathrm{K}\)) के साथ गर्म करने मात्र से क्लोरीन प्रतिस्थापित होकर 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोफीनॉल (पिक्रिक अम्ल) बन जाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष का संश्लेषण
पोटैशियम सायनाइड व सिल्वर सायनाइड के भिन्न उत्पादों, हैलोऐरीन में कार्बन-हैलोजन आबंध की प्रबलता तथा 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन के जल द्वारा सुगम जलअपघटन से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि सैत्ज़ेफ नियम के संबंध में कम ऐल्किल समूहों वाली ऐल्कीन का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक निष्कर्ष: पोटैशियम सायनाइड व सिल्वर सायनाइड के भिन्न उत्पादों, हैलोऐरीन में कार्बन-हैलोजन आबंध की प्रबलता तथा 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्जीन के जल द्वारा सुगम जलअपघटन से संबंधित तथ्य सही हैं, जबकि सैत्ज़ेफ नियम के संबंध में कम ऐल्किल समूहों वाली ऐल्कीन का दावा गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q01 - Clinical and industrial applications of halogen compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Compound) List-II (Application / Significance)
A. Chloramphenicol (i) Synthetic compound used for treatment of malaria
B. Thyroxine (ii) Volatile anaesthetic used during surgery
C. Halothane (iii) Chlorine-containing antibiotic used for treatment of typhoid fever
D. Chloroquine (iv) Iodine-containing hormone whose deficiency causes goiter

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Clinical role of Chloramphenicol
Chloramphenicol is a naturally occurring chlorine-containing broad-spectrum antibiotic produced by soil microorganisms, specifically prescribed for the clinical treatment of typhoid fever.

Step 2: Physiological role of Thyroxine
Thyroxine is an essential iodine-containing hormone secreted by the thyroid gland; inadequate dietary intake of iodine or deficiency of this hormone causes the metabolic disease known as goiter.

Step 3: Medical application of Halothane
Halothane (\(\mathrm{CF}_3\mathrm{CHBrCl}\)) is a synthetic polyhalogenated alkane widely utilized in modern medicine as a non-flammable inhalation general anaesthetic during surgical procedures.

Step 4: Therapeutic application of Chloroquine
Chloroquine is a synthetic halogen-containing pharmaceutical agent used worldwide for the prophylaxis and treatment of malaria.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Pairing each substance with its primary physiological or medicinal property gives: Chloramphenicol — Chlorine-containing antibiotic used for treatment of typhoid fever; Thyroxine — Iodine-containing hormone whose deficiency causes goiter; Halothane — Volatile anaesthetic used during surgery; Chloroquine — Synthetic compound used for treatment of malaria. This establishes the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q02 - Classification of halides based on carbon hybridisation

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Class of Halide) List-II (Defining Structural Characteristic)
A. Allylic halide (i) Halogen atom directly bonded to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon of an aromatic ring
B. Vinylic halide (ii) Halogen atom bonded to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon attached to an aromatic ring
C. Benzylic halide (iii) Halogen atom bonded to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond
D. Aryl halide (iv) Halogen atom bonded to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon of an aliphatic carbon-carbon double bond

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Allylic Halides
Allylic halides are compounds in which the halogen atom is bonded to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon atom that is positioned immediately adjacent to an aliphatic carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)), termed an allylic carbon.

Step 2: Classification of Vinylic Halides
Vinylic halides are defined as compounds where the halogen atom is bonded directly to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon atom constituting an aliphatic carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)).

Step 3: Classification of Benzylic Halides
Benzylic halides contain a halogen atom bonded to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon atom that is directly attached to an aromatic ring (such as a benzene nucleus).

Step 4: Classification of Aryl Halides
Aryl halides (haloarenes) feature a halogen atom bonded directly to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon atom belonging to an aromatic ring.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Matching each class of halide with its defining structural characteristic establishes: Allylic halide — Halogen bonded to \(sp^3\) carbon adjacent to double bond; Vinylic halide — Halogen bonded to \(sp^2\) carbon of double bond; Benzylic halide — Halogen bonded to \(sp^3\) carbon attached to aromatic ring; Aryl halide — Halogen directly bonded to \(sp^2\) carbon of aromatic ring. This yields the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q03 - Name reactions in haloalkane and haloarene synthesis

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Named Reaction) List-II (Reagent and Primary Synthetic Outcome)
A. Finkelstein reaction (i) Heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a metallic fluoride like \(\mathrm{AgF}\) to yield an alkyl fluoride
B. Swarts reaction (ii) Treatment of a diazonium salt with cuprous chloride or bromide to replace the diazonium group
C. Wurtz reaction (iii) Reaction of an alkyl chloride or bromide with \(\mathrm{NaI}\) in dry acetone to yield an alkyl iodide
D. Sandmeyer reaction (iv) Treatment of alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether to yield a symmetrical alkane with doubled carbons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism and transformation of the Finkelstein reaction
The Finkelstein reaction is a classical halogen exchange method in which alkyl chlorides or bromides react with sodium iodide (\(\mathrm{NaI}\)) dissolved in dry acetone. Precipitation of poorly soluble \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) or \(\mathrm{NaBr}\) in dry acetone drives the equilibrium forward by Le Chatelier's principle, synthesizing alkyl iodides (\(\mathrm{R-I}\)).

Step 2: Mechanism and transformation of the Swarts reaction
The Swarts reaction provides the standard route for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides (\(\mathrm{R-F}\)) by heating an alkyl chloride or bromide in the presence of heavy metallic fluorides, such as \(\mathrm{AgF}\), \(\mathrm{Hg}_2\mathrm{F}_2\), \(\mathrm{CoF}_2\), or \(\mathrm{SbF}_3\).

Step 3: Mechanism and transformation of the Wurtz reaction
In the Wurtz reaction, two molecules of alkyl halide are coupled by reaction with metallic sodium in anhydrous dry ether to generate higher symmetrical alkanes containing twice the carbon atoms of the initial halide.

Step 4: Mechanism and transformation of the Sandmeyer reaction
In the Sandmeyer reaction, freshly prepared arenediazonium salts undergo nucleophilic replacement of the diazo group (\(-\mathrm{N}_2^+\)) upon mixing with cuprous salts (\(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\) or \(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{Br}_2\)), producing aryl chlorides or aryl bromides with the liberation of nitrogen gas.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Correlating each reaction with its characteristic reagents and products gives: Finkelstein reaction — \(\mathrm{NaI}\) in dry acetone yielding alkyl iodide; Swarts reaction — Metallic fluorides yielding alkyl fluoride; Wurtz reaction — Sodium in dry ether yielding higher alkane; Sandmeyer reaction — Diazonium salt with cuprous halide yielding aryl halide. This matches the sequence A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q04 - Ambident nucleophiles and nucleophilic substitution products

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagent reacting with \(\mathrm{R-X}\)) List-II (Major Substitution Product Class Formed)
A. \(\mathrm{KCN}\) (i) Nitroalkane (\(\mathrm{R-NO}_2\))
B. \(\mathrm{AgCN}\) (ii) Alkyl isocyanide (\(\mathrm{R-NC}\))
C. \(\mathrm{KNO}_2\) (iii) Alkyl nitrite (\(\mathrm{R-O-N=O}\))
D. \(\mathrm{AgNO}_2\) (iv) Alkyl cyanide / nitrile (\(\mathrm{R-CN}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Behaviour of Potassium Cyanide (\(\mathrm{KCN}\))
Potassium cyanide is predominantly ionic in solution and dissociates completely into cyanide ions (\(:\!\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{N}:^-\)). Although both carbon and nitrogen possess lone pairs capable of attack, the nucleophilic substitution occurs predominantly through the carbon atom because the formed carbon-carbon (\(\mathrm{C-C}\)) bond is thermodynamically much more stable than a carbon-nitrogen (\(\mathrm{C-N}\)) bond, yielding an alkyl cyanide (nitrile, \(\mathrm{R-CN}\)).

Step 2: Behaviour of Silver Cyanide (\(\mathrm{AgCN}\))
Silver cyanide is predominantly covalent in nature; the bond between silver and carbon is largely covalent, leaving the lone pair on the nitrogen atom freely available to initiate nucleophilic attack on the alkyl halide, resulting primarily in an alkyl isocyanide (\(\mathrm{R-NC}\)).

Step 3: Behaviour of Potassium Nitrite (\(\mathrm{KNO}_2\))
Potassium nitrite is an ionic salt providing ambident nitrite ions (\(^{-}\mathrm{O-N=O}\)). In solution, nucleophilic attack occurs through the oxygen atom possessing a formal negative charge, which forms an alkyl nitrite (\(\mathrm{R-O-N=O}\)) as the major product.

Step 4: Behaviour of Silver Nitrite (\(\mathrm{AgNO}_2\))
Silver nitrite possesses a predominantly covalent \(\mathrm{Ag-O}\) bond; consequently, the nitrogen atom donates its electron lone pair to attack the electrophilic carbon of the alkyl halide, yielding a nitroalkane (\(\mathrm{R-NO}_2\)) as the major product.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Correlating each ambident reagent with its dominant substitution product class gives: \(\mathrm{KCN}\) — Alkyl cyanide (\(\mathrm{R-CN}\)); \(\mathrm{AgCN}\) — Alkyl isocyanide (\(\mathrm{R-NC}\)); \(\mathrm{KNO}_2\) — Alkyl nitrite (\(\mathrm{R-O-N=O}\)); \(\mathrm{AgNO}_2\) — Nitroalkane (\(\mathrm{R-NO}_2\)). This corresponds to the sequence A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q05 - Environmental and health effects of polyhalogen compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Polyhalogen Compound) List-II (Key Application / Physiological and Environmental Hazard)
A. Dichloromethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\)) (i) Historically used as an antiseptic due to the slow liberation of free iodine
B. Trichloromethane (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) (ii) Process solvent and paint remover that harms the central nervous system and impairs vision
C. Triiodomethane (\(\mathrm{CHI}_3\)) (iii) Industrial degreaser and fire extinguisher that causes ozone depletion and liver damage
D. Tetrachloromethane (\(\mathrm{CCl}_4\)) (iv) Precursor for Freon R-22 that oxidises slowly in light and air to form toxic phosgene gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Properties of Dichloromethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\))
Dichloromethane (methylene chloride) is widely employed as a paint remover, aerosol propellant, and solvent in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals. Exposure harms the human central nervous system, leading to impaired hearing, diminished vision, dizziness, and peripheral numbness.

Step 2: Properties of Trichloromethane (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\))
Trichloromethane (chloroform) is primarily used today in the industrial manufacturing of the refrigerant Freon R-22. In the presence of sunlight and atmospheric oxygen, it undergoes slow photo-oxidation to produce carbonyl chloride (\(\mathrm{COCl}_2\)), a deadly poisonous gas known as phosgene.

Step 3: Properties of Triiodomethane (\(\mathrm{CHI}_3\))
Triiodomethane (iodoform) was formerly used as an antiseptic. Its therapeutic antiseptic properties are not intrinsic to the \(\mathrm{CHI}_3\) molecule itself, but are entirely due to the slow liberation of elemental iodine upon application.

Step 4: Properties of Tetrachloromethane (\(\mathrm{CCl}_4\))
Tetrachloromethane (carbon tetrachloride) was extensively used as a cleaning agent, degreasing fluid, and fire extinguisher. When released into the atmosphere, it rises to the stratosphere where it depletes the protective ozone layer; chronic exposure causes liver cancer and severe neurological damage.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Matching each polyhalogen compound with its primary hazard or role gives: Dichloromethane — Solvent and paint remover that harms the central nervous system; Trichloromethane — Precursor for Freon R-22 that oxidises to phosgene; Triiodomethane — Antiseptic acting via liberation of free iodine; Tetrachloromethane — Degreaser and fire extinguisher that causes ozone depletion. This establishes the sequence A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q06 - Basic terminology and principles of optical isomerism

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Stereochemical Concept) List-II (Precise Definition / Characteristic)
A. Chirality (i) An equimolar mixture of two enantiomers exhibiting zero net optical rotation
B. Enantiomers (ii) Preservation of the relative spatial arrangement of bonds to an asymmetric centre during a reaction
C. Racemic mixture (iii) Geometric property of an object or molecule that is non-superimposable on its mirror image
D. Retention of configuration (iv) Non-superimposable mirror-image stereoisomers that rotate plane-polarised light by equal magnitude in opposite directions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific definition of Chirality
Chirality is the geometric property of asymmetry displayed by an object or molecular structure that cannot be superimposed onto its own mirror image. Chiral molecules lack an internal plane or centre of symmetry and exhibit optical activity.

Step 2: Scientific definition of Enantiomers
Enantiomers are a pair of optical stereoisomers that are related as non-superimposable mirror images of one another. They possess identical chemical and physical properties in achiral environments but rotate plane-polarised light in equal magnitudes in opposite directions (dextrorotatory and laevorotatory).

Step 3: Scientific definition of a Racemic mixture
A racemic mixture (or racemic modification) contains equal proportions (50:50) of dextrorotatory and laevorotatory enantiomers. The optical rotation caused by molecules of one isomer is exactly compensated and cancelled by the opposite rotation of the other isomer, resulting in an optically inactive mixture designated as \((\pm)\) or \(dl\).

Step 4: Scientific definition of Retention of configuration
Retention of configuration describes a chemical reaction in which the relative three-dimensional spatial orientation of bonds at an asymmetric stereocentre remains completely preserved without inversion or change of absolute configuration.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Aligning each term with its rigorous definition yields: Chirality — Property of non-superimposability on mirror image; Enantiomers — Non-superimposable mirror images rotating light in opposite directions; Racemic mixture — Equimolar mixture showing zero net optical rotation; Retention of configuration — Preservation of spatial arrangement of bonds to an asymmetric centre. This corresponds to the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q07 - Electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions of chlorobenzene

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reaction Conditions on Chlorobenzene) List-II (Major Organic Substitution Product)
A. \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) (i) 4-Chlorobenzenesulfonic acid
B. Concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) + concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) (ii) 4-Chloroacetophenone
C. Heating with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) (iii) 1,4-Dichlorobenzene
D. \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCl}\) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\) (iv) 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Directing influence in electrophilic substitution of chlorobenzene
The chlorine substituent on the benzene ring is weakly deactivating due to its strong \(-I\) (inductive) effect, but acts as an ortho-, para-directing group due to \(+R\) (resonance) electron donation that increases electron density predominantly at the ortho and para positions. Steric hindrance at the ortho position makes the symmetrical para-substituted product the predominant major product in all cases.

Step 2: Electrophilic chlorination of chlorobenzene
Treatment of chlorobenzene with chlorine gas in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) catalyst introduces an electrophilic chloronium ion, yielding 1,4-dichlorobenzene (para-isomer) as the major product alongside 1,2-dichlorobenzene (ortho-isomer) as the minor product.

Step 3: Electrophilic nitration of chlorobenzene
Reaction of chlorobenzene with nitrating mixture (concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) and concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)) produces the nitronium ion (\(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\)), which attacks preferentially to form 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene as the major product.

Step 4: Electrophilic sulphonation of chlorobenzene
Heating chlorobenzene with concentrated sulphuric acid produces sulphur trioxide electrophile, yielding 4-chlorobenzenesulfonic acid as the major product.

Step 5: Friedel-Crafts acylation of chlorobenzene
Reaction of chlorobenzene with acetyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCl}\)) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\) Lewis acid generates the acylium electrophile (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{C}^+=\mathrm{O}\)), producing 4-chloroacetophenone as the major product.

Step 6: Conceptual matching conclusion
Matching each set of electrophilic conditions with the resulting major product gives: Chlorination — 1,4-Dichlorobenzene; Nitration — 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene; Sulphonation — 4-Chlorobenzenesulfonic acid; Friedel-Crafts acylation — 4-Chloroacetophenone. This establishes the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q08 - Boiling point dipole moment and lattice symmetry trends

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Substance / Isomer) List-II (Characteristic Physical Trend / Experimental Property)
A. Chloromethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}\)) (i) Highest melting point among isomeric dihalobenzenes due to molecular symmetry and lattice fit
B. Iodomethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}\)) (ii) Lowest boiling point among isomeric bromobutanes due to spherical shape and minimal surface area
C. \(p\)-Dichlorobenzene (iii) Highest dipole moment among monohalomethanes (\(1.860\text{ D}\)) due to balance of charge and bond length
D. 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (iv) Lowest \(\mathrm{C-X}\) bond enthalpy (\(234\text{ kJ/mol}\)) and highest boiling point among methyl halides

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Dipole moment of Chloromethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}\))
Dipole moment is the product of partial charge and bond distance (\(\mu = q \times d\)). Although fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, the \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\) bond distance (\(178\text{ pm}\)) is significantly larger than the \(\mathrm{C-F}\) bond distance (\(139\text{ pm}\)). Consequently, chloromethane exhibits the highest dipole moment (\(1.860\text{ D}\)) among all halomethanes.

Step 2: Physical properties of Iodomethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}\))
Because the iodine atom has the largest atomic size and mass among the halogens, \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}\) experiences the strongest van der Waals dispersion forces, giving it the highest boiling point among the methyl halides. Concurrently, the greater bond length (\(214\text{ pm}\)) produces the lowest carbon-halogen bond dissociation enthalpy (\(234\text{ kJ/mol}\)).

Step 3: Melting point of \(p\)-Dichlorobenzene
While ortho-, meta-, and para-dichlorobenzene have very similar boiling points (\(453\text{ K}\), \(446\text{ K}\), and \(448\text{ K}\)), the melting point of the para-isomer (\(323\text{ K}\)) is substantially higher than the ortho- (\(256\text{ K}\)) and meta- (\(249\text{ K}\)) isomers. This is due to the high molecular symmetry of the para-isomer, which packs far more closely and securely into the crystal lattice.

Step 4: Boiling point of 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane
Among the constitutional isomers of bromobutane (\(\mathrm{C}_4\mathrm{H}_9\mathrm{Br}\)), branching increases from 1-bromobutane to 2-bromobutane to 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. Branching makes the molecule more spherical, diminishing surface contact area and lowering the magnitude of intermolecular van der Waals forces, which results in the lowest boiling point (\(346\text{ K}\)).

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Correlating each substance with its specific physical behavior establishes: Chloromethane — Highest dipole moment among monohalomethanes; Iodomethane — Lowest bond enthalpy and highest methyl halide boiling point; \(p\)-Dichlorobenzene — Highest melting point among dihalobenzenes due to crystal symmetry; 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane — Lowest boiling point among bromobutanes due to branching. This yields the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q09 - Mechanistic and stereochemical pathways in substitution elimination

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reaction / Transformation) List-II (Mechanistic Course and Stereochemical / Product Outcome)
A. \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) reaction of an optically active secondary alkyl halide (i) Single-step concerted pathway yielding complete inversion of configuration
B. \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) reaction of an optically active secondary alkyl halide (ii) Requires drastic conditions (\(623\text{ K}\), \(300\text{ atm}\)) due to partial double-bond character of \(\mathrm{C-X}\)
C. Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopentane with alcoholic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) (iii) Two-step pathway via a planar achiral carbocation leading to racemisation
D. Hydrolysis of chlorobenzene to phenol (iv) Governed by Zaitsev's rule yielding pent-2-ene as the major, more substituted alkene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) substitution on chiral substrates
In an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) reaction, the rate-determining slow step generates an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbocation intermediate that is trigonal planar and achiral. The incoming nucleophile attacks with equal probability from either side of the plane, giving equal amounts of retained and inverted products, which results in racemisation.

Step 2: Mechanism of \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) substitution on chiral substrates
An \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) reaction proceeds via a single-step concerted bimolecular mechanism where the nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon from the rear (opposite to the departing halide). As the leaving group departs, the tetrahedral geometry flips like an umbrella in high wind, producing complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion).

Step 3: Elimination pathway in 2-bromopentane
When 2-bromopentane is heated with alcoholic \(\mathrm{KOH}\), it undergoes \(\beta\)-elimination of hydrogen and bromine. According to Zaitsev's (Saytzeff's) rule, the preferred alkene is that having the greater number of alkyl substituents on the double bond; hence, pent-2-ene is formed as the major product (\(81\%\)) while pent-1-ene is minor (\(19\%\)).

Step 4: Nucleophilic substitution of chlorobenzene
Chlorobenzene is exceptionally unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution compared to alkyl halides because resonance delocalisation gives the \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\) bond partial double-bond character (\(169\text{ pm}\) vs \(177\text{ pm}\)), and the \(sp^2\) carbon is more electronegative. Hence, conversion to phenol requires drastic industrial conditions (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\), \(623\text{ K}\), \(300\text{ atm}\)).

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Pairing each reaction with its characteristic mechanistic behaviour gives: \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) on chiral halide — Planar carbocation intermediate leading to racemisation; \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) on chiral halide — Concerted pathway giving inversion of configuration; Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopentane — Follows Zaitsev's rule to yield pent-2-ene; Hydrolysis of chlorobenzene — Requires drastic conditions due to partial double-bond character. This matches the sequence A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q10 - Activating influence of nitro groups on haloarenes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Substrate undergoing Nucleophilic Hydroxylation) List-II (Specific Reaction Conditions for Phenol Formation)
A. Chlorobenzene (i) Aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), \(368\text{ K}\) followed by dilute \(\mathrm{H}^+\)
B. 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene (ii) Simply warming with water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\))
C. 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (iii) Aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), \(623\text{ K}\), \(300\text{ atm}\) followed by dilute \(\mathrm{H}^+\)
D. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (iv) Aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), \(443\text{ K}\) followed by dilute \(\mathrm{H}^+\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Hydrolysis of unsubstituted Chlorobenzene
In chlorobenzene, nucleophilic attack of hydroxide ion is hindered by the electron-rich \(\pi\)-system and resonance stabilization of the \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\) bond. Conversion to phenol requires extremely harsh conditions: heating with aqueous sodium hydroxide at \(623\text{ K}\) under \(300\text{ atm}\) of pressure followed by acidification.

Step 2: Hydrolysis of 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene
The introduction of a strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group (\(-\mathrm{NO}_2\)) at the para-position stabilizes the developing negative charge on the Meisenheimer carbanionic intermediate through resonance. This facilitates nucleophilic substitution at a significantly milder temperature of \(443\text{ K}\) with aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\).

Step 3: Hydrolysis of 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene
With two strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups located at both ortho and para positions relative to chlorine, the intermediate carbanion is delocalised and stabilised even further. As a consequence, substitution occurs smoothly at \(368\text{ K}\) in aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\).

Step 4: Hydrolysis of 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene
When three nitro groups occupy all two ortho positions and the para position (2, 4, and 6), the benzene ring is intensely electron-deficient and the resulting carbanion intermediate is exceptionally stable. The chlorine atom is displaced simply by warming with water without requiring any added sodium hydroxide.

Step 5: Conceptual matching conclusion
Matching each nitro-substituted chlorobenzene derivative with the corresponding reaction conditions yields: Chlorobenzene — \(623\text{ K}\), \(300\text{ atm}\); 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene — \(443\text{ K}\); 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene — \(368\text{ K}\); 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene — Simply warming with water. This establishes the sequence A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Total structural isomers of bromopentane

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of structural isomers possible for the alkyl halide having molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_5H_{11}Br}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molecular formula of alkyl halide: \(\mathrm{C_5H_{11}Br}\).
Requirement: Find the total number of structural (constitutional) isomers without considering stereoisomers.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Structural isomers share the same molecular formula but have different connectivities of carbon skeletons or positions of the halogen substituent. Stereoisomers (enantiomers/diastereomers) are not counted separately as distinct structural isomers unless specified.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Categorisation
Pentane has three carbon skeleton isomers:
1. Straight chain: pentane skeleton (\(\mathrm{C-C-C-C-C}\))
2. Branched chain: 2-methylbutane skeleton (isopentane)
3. Highly branched: 2,2-dimethylpropane skeleton (neopentane)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Enumerate the position isomers for each carbon skeleton:
- For the n-pentane skeleton, attaching \(-\mathrm{Br}\) at position 1 gives 1-bromopentane; at position 2 gives 2-bromopentane; at position 3 gives 3-bromopentane. This yields 3 isomers.
- For the 2-methylbutane skeleton, attaching \(-\mathrm{Br}\) gives 1-bromo-2-methylbutane, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, 3-bromo-2-methylbutane (2-bromo-3-methylbutane), and 1-bromo-3-methylbutane. This yields 4 isomers.
- For the 2,2-dimethylpropane skeleton, all four methyl groups are equivalent, attaching \(-\mathrm{Br}\) gives 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane. This yields 1 isomer.
Total structural isomers = \(3 + 4 + 1 = 8\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The three skeletons yield 3, 4, and 1 structural isomers respectively. All positions are accounted for and no duplicate structures exist.
Total number of structural isomers = 8.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Monochloro structural isomers of isopentane

questiontext.text: Find the total number of monochloro structural isomers formed upon free radical chlorination of 2-methylbutane \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCH_2CH_3}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Starting hydrocarbon: 2-methylbutane \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3}\).
Reaction: Free radical monochlorination (\(\mathrm{Cl_2 / h\nu}\)).
Requirement: Determine the number of constitutionally distinct monochloro products.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In free radical chlorination, a chlorine atom replaces a hydrogen atom at any non-equivalent carbon. The number of monochloro structural isomers corresponds to the number of chemically non-equivalent types of hydrogen atoms in 2-methylbutane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Symmetry Analysis
Examine the non-equivalent positions of hydrogen atoms in 2-methylbutane:
\(\mathrm{C1}\): primary hydrogens on the two equivalent methyl groups attached to \(\mathrm{C2}\).
\(\mathrm{C2}\): tertiary hydrogen attached to \(\mathrm{CH}\).
\(\mathrm{C3}\): secondary hydrogens on the methylene \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) group.
\(\mathrm{C4}\): primary hydrogens on the terminal methyl group.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitution of hydrogen at each distinct site yields:
1. Replacement of \(\mathrm{H}\) at \(\mathrm{C1}\) gives 1-chloro-2-methylbutane.
2. Replacement of \(\mathrm{H}\) at \(\mathrm{C2}\) gives 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.
3. Replacement of \(\mathrm{H}\) at \(\mathrm{C3}\) gives 2-chloro-3-methylbutane.
4. Replacement of \(\mathrm{H}\) at \(\mathrm{C4}\) gives 1-chloro-3-methylbutane.
These represent 4 unique structural isomers.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since there are 4 sets of chemically non-equivalent hydrogens in 2-methylbutane, exactly 4 monochloro structural isomers are formed.
Final Answer: 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Melting point difference between dichlorobenzenes

questiontext.text: The melting point of \(p\)-dichlorobenzene is \(323\text{ K}\) and that of \(o\)-dichlorobenzene is \(256\text{ K}\). Calculate the difference in melting points (in \(\text{K}\)) between the \(p\)-isomer and the \(o\)-isomer.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Melting point of \(p\)-dichlorobenzene, \(T_{\mathrm{m}}(p) = 323\text{ K}\).
Melting point of \(o\)-dichlorobenzene, \(T_{\mathrm{m}}(o) = 256\text{ K}\).
Requirement: Calculate the difference \(\Delta T_{\mathrm{m}} = T_{\mathrm{m}}(p) - T_{\mathrm{m}}(o)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The \(p\)-isomer has a significantly higher melting point than the \(o\)- and \(m\)-isomers due to molecular symmetry, which allows tighter packing in the crystal lattice.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The temperature difference is obtained directly by subtraction:
\[\Delta T_{\mathrm{m}} = T_{\mathrm{m}}(p) - T_{\mathrm{m}}(o)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the equation:
\[\Delta T_{\mathrm{m}} = 323\text{ K} - 256\text{ K} = 67\text{ K}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verification: \(256 + 67 = 323\text{ K}\). The magnitude is consistent and physically corresponds to the greater lattice energy of the symmetrical para-isomer.
Final Answer: 67.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Percentage yield of pent-2-ene from 2-bromopentane

questiontext.text: According to Zaitsev's rule, dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopentane with alcoholic potassium hydroxide gives a mixture of pent-2-ene and pent-1-ene. What is the percentage of pent-2-ene in the product mixture?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Substrate: 2-bromopentane.
Reagent: Alcoholic \(\mathrm{KOH}\).
Reaction type: \(\beta\)-elimination (dehydrohalogenation).
Products formed: pent-2-ene and pent-1-ene.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Alexander Zaitsev (Saytzeff) formulated that in dehydrohalogenation reactions, the preferred product is that alkene which has the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms (more substituted, more stable alkene).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Pent-2-ene is a disubstituted alkene having two alkyl substituents (one methyl and one ethyl group), whereas pent-1-ene is a monosubstituted alkene with one propyl group.
Consequently, pent-2-ene is the major product.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Experimentally documented in NCERT chemistry:
- Pent-2-ene is formed as the major alkene in \(81\%\) yield.
- Pent-1-ene is formed as the minor alkene in \(19\%\) yield.
Hence, the percentage of pent-2-ene in the product mixture is \(81\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total percentage sums to \(81\% + 19\% = 100\%\). The major alkene accounts for 81%.
Final Answer: 81.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Number of chlorine atoms in DDT

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of chlorine atoms present in one molecule of \(p,p'\)-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound: \(p,p'\)-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT).
Requirement: Determine the total number of chlorine atoms present per molecule of DDT.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
DDT is an organochlorine polyhalogen compound prepared by the condensation of chlorobenzene and chloral in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid. Its IUPAC name is 2,2-bis(4-chlorophenyl)-1,1,1-trichloroethane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Molecular Structure
Molecular formula: \(\mathrm{C_{14}H_9Cl_5}\).
Structural breakdown:
- Two 4-chlorophenyl rings: Each benzene ring contains 1 chlorine atom at the para position, giving \(2 \times 1 = 2\) aromatic chlorine atoms.
- One trichloromethyl group (\(-\mathrm{CCl_3}\)): Contains 3 chlorine atoms attached to the aliphatic carbon.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Summing the chlorine atoms from both parts of the molecule:
\[N_{\mathrm{Cl}} = 2\text{ (aromatic Cl)} + 3\text{ (aliphatic Cl)} = 5\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Consistent with the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_{14}H_9Cl_5}\), exactly 5 chlorine atoms are present in one molecule of DDT.
Final Answer: 5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Moles of sodium required in Wurtz reaction

questiontext.text: In a Wurtz reaction, ethyl bromide reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether to form \(n\)-butane. How many moles of sodium metal are required for complete reaction with \(0.50\text{ mol}\) of ethyl bromide?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Alkyl halide: Ethyl bromide (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br}\)).
Quantity of ethyl bromide: \(n_{\mathrm{RBr}} = 0.50\text{ mol}\).
Reagent: Metallic sodium in dry ether.
Product: \(n\)-butane (\(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\)).
Requirement: Determine the moles of sodium metal required.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The Wurtz reaction is a stoichiometric coupling reaction where two molecules of an alkyl halide react with two atoms of sodium in dry ether to produce an alkane containing twice the number of carbon atoms along with sodium halide.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Balanced Equation
The balanced chemical equation for the Wurtz reaction is:
\[2\,\mathrm{C_2H_5Br} + 2\,\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C_4H_{10}} + 2\,\mathrm{NaBr}\]The stoichiometric ratio between \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}\) and \(\mathrm{Na}\) is:
\[\frac{n_{\mathrm{Na}}}{n_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}}} = \frac{2}{2} = 1\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Using the 1:1 molar equivalence:
\[n_{\mathrm{Na}} = n_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}} = 0.50\text{ mol}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since 2 moles of alkyl halide require exactly 2 moles of sodium metal, \(0.50\text{ mol}\) of ethyl bromide requires \(0.50\text{ mol}\) of sodium metal.
Final Answer: 0.50.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Mass of butane formed in Wurtz reaction

questiontext.text: A sample containing \(21.8\text{ g}\) of bromoethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br}\)) is treated with excess metallic sodium in dry ether to carry out the Wurtz coupling reaction. Assuming a \(100\%\) yield, calculate the mass of butane (\(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\)) obtained in grams. (Take atomic masses: \(\mathrm{C = 12\text{ g/mol}}\), \(\mathrm{H = 1\text{ g/mol}}\), \(\mathrm{Br = 79.9\text{ g/mol}}\); use molar mass of bromoethane as \(109.0\text{ g/mol}\) and butane as \(58.0\text{ g/mol}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of bromoethane: \(m_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}} = 21.8\text{ g}\).
Molar mass of bromoethane: \(M_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}} = 109.0\text{ g/mol}\).
Molar mass of butane: \(M_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = 58.0\text{ g/mol}\).
Reaction yield: \(100\%\).
Requirement: Mass of butane formed in grams.

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Bromoethane undergoes Wurtz coupling in dry ether in the presence of excess sodium according to the stoichiometric relationship where two moles of bromoethane produce one mole of butane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Balanced Equation
Balanced chemical equation:
\[2\,\mathrm{C_2H_5Br} + 2\,\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C_4H_{10}} + 2\,\mathrm{NaBr}\]Formulas used:
1. Moles of bromoethane: \(n_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}} = \frac{m_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}}}{M_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}}}\)
2. Moles of butane produced: \(n_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = \frac{1}{2}\,n_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}}\)
3. Mass of butane produced: \(m_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = n_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} \times M_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}}\)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Compute the moles of bromoethane:
\[n_{\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}} = \frac{21.8\text{ g}}{109.0\text{ g/mol}} = 0.20\text{ mol}\]
2. Compute the moles of butane produced:
\[n_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = \frac{0.20\text{ mol}}{2} = 0.10\text{ mol}\]
3. Compute the mass of butane formed:
\[m_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = 0.10\text{ mol} \times 58.0\text{ g/mol} = 5.8\text{ g}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units and conservation: \(0.20\text{ mol}\) \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}\) has mass \(21.8\text{ g}\). It reacts with \(0.20\text{ mol}\) \(\mathrm{Na}\) (\(4.6\text{ g}\)), giving total reactant mass \(26.4\text{ g}\). Products are \(5.8\text{ g}\) butane + \(0.20 \times 102.9 = 20.58\text{ g}\) \(\mathrm{NaBr}\), summing to \(26.38\text{ g}\). The mass balance confirms the result.
Final Answer: 5.8.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Difference in carbon-halogen bond length

questiontext.text: In halomethanes, the \(\mathrm{C-F}\) bond length in fluoromethane is \(139\text{ pm}\) and the \(\mathrm{C-I}\) bond length in iodomethane is \(214\text{ pm}\). Determine the difference in bond length (in \(\text{pm}\)) between the \(\mathrm{C-I}\) bond and the \(\mathrm{C-F}\) bond.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Bond length of \(\mathrm{C-F}\) in \(\mathrm{CH_3F}\): \(d_{\mathrm{C-F}} = 139\text{ pm}\).
Bond length of \(\mathrm{C-I}\) in \(\mathrm{CH_3I}\): \(d_{\mathrm{C-I}} = 214\text{ pm}\).
Requirement: Calculate the difference \(\Delta d = d_{\mathrm{C-I}} - d_{\mathrm{C-F}}\) in picometers (\(\text{pm}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Halogen atoms increase in atomic radius going down group 17 from fluorine to iodine. As the size of the halogen atom increases, the overlap of orbitals with the carbon \(sp^3\) hybrid orbital occurs at a greater internuclear distance, resulting in an increasing carbon-halogen bond length from \(\mathrm{C-F}\) to \(\mathrm{C-I}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The difference between the two bond lengths is calculated as:
\[\Delta d = d_{\mathrm{C-I}} - d_{\mathrm{C-F}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given experimental values:
\[\Delta d = 214\text{ pm} - 139\text{ pm} = 75\text{ pm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verification: \(139\text{ pm} + 75\text{ pm} = 214\text{ pm}\). The bond length increases monotonically down the group (\(\mathrm{CH_3F}: 139\text{ pm}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3Cl}: 178\text{ pm}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3Br}: 193\text{ pm}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3I}: 214\text{ pm}\)), confirming the physical validity.
Final Answer: 75.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequence of events during bimolecular nucleophilic substitution

questiontext.text:
Consider the following events occurring during the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (\(\mathrm{S_N2}\)) reaction between chloromethane and hydroxide ion:

(I) Backside approach of the incoming hydroxide nucleophile toward the partially positive carbon atom directly opposite to the departing chlorine atom.
(II) Formation of a pentacoordinate transition state in which all three carbon–hydrogen bonds become coplanar while carbon is simultaneously partially bonded to both incoming and outgoing groups.
(III) Cleavage of the carbon–chlorine bond with departure of the chloride ion as the leaving group, accompanied by inversion of spatial configuration.
(IV) Formation of the final methanol product displaying complete stereochemical inversion.

Which of the following represents the correct sequential order of these stages?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Reaction Overview
The process under evaluation is the concerted \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) displacement reaction between chloromethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3Cl}\)) and hydroxide ion (\(\mathrm{OH^-}\)) to produce methanol (\(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\)) and chloride ion (\(\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).

Step 2: Fundamental Principles of the Bimolecular Mechanism
The \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) reaction proceeds as a concerted, single-step mechanism without any stable intermediate. The incoming electron-rich nucleophile must approach the electrophilic carbon from the direction opposite to the carbon–halogen bond to minimize electrostatic repulsion and allow productive orbital overlap.

Step 3: Logical Order of Mechanistic Events
1. The process begins when the incoming nucleophile approaches the substrate from the backside (opposite the leaving chlorine atom).
2. As the incoming nucleophile approaches and begins forming a bond, the three non-reacting carbon–hydrogen bonds flatten into a single plane, producing an unstable transition state where the central carbon is simultaneously partially bonded to five groups.
3. The carbon–halogen bond weakens further until the chloride ion fully departs as a leaving group, accompanied by the flipping of the three remaining bonds in the manner of an umbrella turning inside out (Walden inversion).
4. The departure completes the formation of the inverted substitution product, methanol.

Step 4: Verification of Sequence
The chronological order proceeds strictly as: backside approach of the nucleophile \(\rightarrow\) transition state assembly \(\rightarrow\) departure of chloride with configurational inversion \(\rightarrow\) formation of the final inverted alcohol molecule. This matches the progression (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct sequential order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequence of steps in Grignard hydrocarbon synthesis

questiontext.text:
Consider the conversion of bromoethane into ethane using magnesium metal followed by reaction with water:

(I) Reaction of bromoethane with magnesium metal suspended in dry diethyl ether.
(II) Insertion of magnesium to yield ethylmagnesium bromide possessing a highly polarized carbon–magnesium bond.
(III) Protonation of the strongly basic carbanionic ethyl group through reaction with water.
(IV) Formation of ethane hydrocarbon along with basic magnesium halide, \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)Br}\).

Arrange these stages in the correct chronological sequence.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Transformations
The pathway outlines the synthesis of an organomagnesium reagent (Grignard reagent) from an alkyl halide and its subsequent protonolysis to generate a hydrocarbon.

Step 2: Governing Chemical Principles
Grignard reagents are synthesized by reacting haloalkanes with magnesium turnings in anhydrous ether. The carbon–magnesium bond is highly polarized with partial negative charge on carbon (\(\mathrm{R^{\delta-}-Mg^{\delta+}X}\)). Because of this pronounced carbanionic character, it reacts readily with any source of acidic protons (such as water) to yield the corresponding alkane.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Reaction Sequence
1. Initially, bromoethane is brought into contact with magnesium in dry ether.
2. Magnesium reacts to form ethylmagnesium bromide (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2MgBr}\)).
3. Subsequently, treatment with water causes the ethyl group to abstract a proton from the \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) molecule.
4. Finally, the proton transfer yields the alkane (ethane, \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\)) and the inorganic byproduct \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)Br}\).

Step 4: Check of Continuity
Reagent formation must precede proton transfer because the carbanion does not exist prior to carbon–magnesium bond formation, and the hydrocarbon product is isolated only following protonolysis. Hence, the logical order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct chronological sequence is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Sequential stages in unimolecular nucleophilic substitution mechanism

questiontext.text:
Consider the hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide) to tert-butyl alcohol under polar protic conditions via the \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism:

(I) Solvation of the leaving halide group by the polar protic solvent, assisting the reversible heterolysis of the carbon–bromine bond.
(II) Slow cleavage of the polarized \(\mathrm{C-Br}\) bond yielding a planar, \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbocation intermediate and a bromide ion.
(III) Rapid nucleophilic attack of the nucleophile on either face of the planar, achiral carbocation intermediate.
(IV) Completion of bond formation yielding 2-methylpropan-2-ol as the substitution product.

What is the correct logical sequence of these mechanistic stages?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Reaction and Mechanism
The reaction is the conversion of \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CBr}\) to \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}\) following unimolecular nucleophilic substitution (\(\mathrm{S_N1}\)).

Step 2: Principles of \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) Kinetics and Mechanism
The \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism is a two-step process occurring through an ionic intermediate. Step I involves slow heterolytic cleavage of the \(\mathrm{C-Br}\) bond facilitated by solvent solvation energy. Step II involves fast combination of the carbocation with the nucleophile.

Step 3: Sequential Breakdown
1. In polar protic solvents, hydrogen bonding and ion-dipole solvation of the departing bromide ion help weaken and polarize the \(\mathrm{C-Br}\) bond.
2. Heterolysis of the polarized bond takes place in the rate-determining step to generate a planar, trigonal \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbocation intermediate and free bromide ion.
3. Once the planar intermediate forms, the nucleophile attacks rapidly from either the top or bottom lobe of the unhybridized \(p\)-orbital.
4. The covalent bond forms, giving the final alcohol product.

Step 4: Consistency Check
A carbocation cannot be attacked before it is formed, and the slow heterolytic cleavage relies on solvent assistance. Therefore, the ordered pathway is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct logical sequence is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q04 - Sequence of reactions in Sandmeyer chlorobenzene synthesis

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following experimental and chemical stages in the synthesis of chlorobenzene starting from aniline via Sandmeyer's reaction in their correct chronological sequence:

(I) Dissolution or suspension of primary aromatic amine (aniline) in cold aqueous mineral acid (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)).
(II) Treatment of the cold acidic amine solution with aqueous sodium nitrite (\(\mathrm{NaNO}_2\)) at 273–278 K.
(III) Formation of a freshly prepared solution containing benzenediazonium chloride.
(IV) Mixing the freshly prepared diazonium salt solution with cuprous chloride (\(\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2}\)) to replace the diazonium group and evolve nitrogen gas.

The correct sequential order of these stages is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Synthesis
The task requires ordering the stages of the Sandmeyer reaction starting from aniline to yield chlorobenzene.

Step 2: Principles of Diazotization and Cuprous Halide Displacement
Primary aromatic amines react with nitrous acid (\(\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HX}\)) at low temperature (273–278 K) to form stable diazonium salts. Because diazonium salts decompose at elevated temperatures, they are prepared in situ and immediately mixed with cuprous chloride to displace the \(\mathrm{-N_2^+}\) group with \(\mathrm{-Cl}\), liberating \(\mathrm{N_2}\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Chemical Progression
1. Aniline is first dissolved or suspended in cold aqueous hydrochloric acid.
2. Sodium nitrite solution is added under ice cooling (273–278 K) to generate nitrous acid in situ.
3. Diazotization occurs to yield a solution of benzenediazonium chloride (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}\)).
4. The diazonium salt solution is combined with cuprous chloride (\(\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2}\)), causing dinitrogen evolution and delivering chlorobenzene.

Step 4: Check of Continuity
The diazotization reaction requires an acidic medium before nitrite addition, and cuprous chloride can only act on the pre-formed diazonium salt. Thus, the order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct sequential order of stages is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q05 - Sequential stages in nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism

questiontext.text:
In the conversion of 4-chloronitrobenzene into 4-nitrophenol by treatment with warm aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by acidification, arrange the following mechanistic stages in their correct logical sequence:

(I) Nucleophilic addition of hydroxide ion to the \(sp^2\) aromatic carbon bearing the chlorine atom.
(II) Formation of a resonance-stabilized carbanionic Meisenheimer intermediate with negative charge delocalized onto the ortho and para positions and into the nitro group.
(III) Rapid expulsion of chloride ion as a leaving group, re-establishing the aromatic sextet.
(IV) Protonation of the phenoxide species upon acidification to produce 4-nitrophenol.

The correct sequential order of these stages is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Reaction and Conditions
The reaction is the nucleophilic aromatic substitution (addition-elimination, \(\mathrm{S_NAr}\)) of 4-chloronitrobenzene with aqueous sodium hydroxide at 443 K followed by acidification.

Step 2: Mechanism of Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution
Aryl halides are generally unreactive toward nucleophilic attack due to resonance stabilization and partial double-bond character of the \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\) bond. However, strong electron-withdrawing groups (such as \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\)) at ortho or para positions stabilize the negative charge developed in the transition state and intermediate through resonance.

Step 3: Detailed Sequence of Events
1. The hydroxide ion attacks the ring carbon bearing the halogen atom in a slow, rate-determining addition step.
2. A resonance-stabilised carbanion intermediate forms where negative charge is accommodated by the ring carbons and directly delocalized into the oxygen atoms of the para-nitro group.
3. In a subsequent fast elimination step, the chloride ion departs, restoring aromaticity to give 4-nitrophenoxide.
4. Acidification (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) protonates the phenoxide oxygen to yield neutral 4-nitrophenol.

Step 4: Check of Continuity
Elimination of chloride cannot occur before the carbanion is created by nucleophilic addition, and acidification is the final workup step. Thus, the order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct sequential order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q06 - Chronological stages of atmospheric ozone depletion by freons

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following sequential atmospheric and chemical processes associated with the release and action of Freon-12 (\(\mathrm{CCl_2F_2}\)) in the correct chronological progression:

(I) Release of volatile Freon-12 into the troposphere from aerosol propellants and refrigeration equipment.
(II) Upward diffusion of unreactive, stable Freon-12 molecules unchanged into the stratosphere.
(III) Photochemical homolysis of carbon–chlorine bonds by intense stratospheric ultraviolet radiation, generating chlorine free radicals.
(IV) Catalytic breakdown of stratospheric ozone into molecular oxygen via chlorine radical chain reactions, disrupting the ozone layer.

Which sequence correctly reflects these sequential environmental events?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Environmental Chemistry Principles
Freons (chlorofluorocarbons) are exceptionally stable and non-reactive in the lower atmosphere (troposphere). Due to their chemical inertness, they do not undergo degradation near the Earth's surface.

Step 2: Atmospheric Transport and Stratospheric Photochemistry
Because of their persistence, chlorofluorocarbons slowly diffuse upward across the troposphere into the stratosphere over prolonged periods. Once in the stratosphere, high-energy solar ultraviolet radiation dissociates the \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\) bond to produce chlorine free radicals (\(\mathrm{Cl^\bullet}\)).

Step 3: Radical Chain Depletion
The liberated chlorine free radicals participate in catalytic chain cycles with ozone molecules (\(\mathrm{O_3}\)), converting them to dioxygen (\(\mathrm{O_2}\)) and regenerating chlorine radicals to continue the destructive cycle.

Step 4: Chronological Ordering
The chain of events follows sequentially: release at ground level \(\rightarrow\) diffusion into the stratosphere \(\rightarrow\) photochemical production of chlorine radicals \(\rightarrow\) catalytic breakdown of ozone. This corresponds to (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct sequence of events is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q07 - Chronological order of historical discoveries in stereochemistry

questiontext.text:
The textbook highlights several foundational historical milestones in the development of organic stereochemistry and organohalogen chemistry:

(I) Louis Pasteur's discovery that crystals of certain compounds exist as non-superimposable mirror images showing opposite optical rotation.
(II) J. Van't Hoff and C. Le Bel's proposal of tetrahedral geometry and asymmetric carbon atoms as the origin of molecular chirality.
(III) Alexander Zaitsev's formulation of the empirical rule governing the regioselectivity of alkene formation in dehydrohalogenation.
(IV) Victor Grignard's discovery of organomagnesium halides (Grignard reagents).
(V) Paul Muller's discovery of the effectiveness of \(\mathrm{p,p^\prime}\)-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT) as an insecticide.

Arrange these historical milestones in chronological order from earliest to latest.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Listing Historical Events with Stated Dates
According to the historical accounts documented in the chapter:
- Louis Pasteur observed enantiomeric crystal morphology and optical rotation in 1848.
- J. Van't Hoff and C. Le Bel independently proposed the tetrahedral carbon model and asymmetric stereocentres in 1874.
- Alexander Zaitsev formulated the rule of preferential formation of the more substituted alkene during \(\beta\)-elimination in 1875.
- Victor Grignard reported the preparation of alkylmagnesium halides in dry ether in 1900.
- Paul Muller discovered the insecticidal properties of DDT in 1939.

Step 2: Comparison of Dates
Arranging the years chronologically:
1848 \(\rightarrow\) 1874 \(\rightarrow\) 1875 \(\rightarrow\) 1900 \(\rightarrow\) 1939.

Step 3: Matching Events with Chronology
- Earliest (1848): Pasteur's optical rotation of enantiomorphic crystals.
- Second (1874): Van't Hoff and Le Bel's tetrahedral carbon concept.
- Third (1875): Zaitsev's dehydrohalogenation rule.
- Fourth (1900): Grignard's discovery of organomagnesium reagents.
- Latest (1939): Muller's discovery of the insecticidal utility of DDT.

Step 4: Check of Continuity
The chronological sequence is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (V).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct chronological order is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (V).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_SEQUENCING_Q08 - Sequence of steps in conversion of isomeric bromopropanes

questiontext.text:
To convert secondary alkyl halide 2-bromopropane into its primary structural isomer 1-bromopropane, arrange the following experimental and chemical stages in their correct logical sequence:

(I) Heating 2-bromopropane with alcoholic potassium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{alc.\ KOH}\)) to carry out dehydrohalogenation.
(II) Isolation of the formed propene alkene gas.
(III) Addition of gaseous hydrogen bromide (\(\mathrm{HBr}\)) to propene in the presence of an organic peroxide.
(IV) Anti-Markovnikov free radical addition yielding 1-bromopropane as the major product.

What is the correct sequential order of steps for this synthetic transformation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Synthetic Goal
The conversion requires transposing the halogen position from \(\mathrm{C-2}\) in 2-bromopropane (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_3}\)) to \(\mathrm{C-1}\) in 1-bromopropane (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Br}\)).

Step 2: Chemical Principles and Pathway Design
Direct nucleophilic displacement of bromide cannot relocate the functional group to an adjacent carbon. The established two-stage pathway involves:
1. Elimination of \(\mathrm{HBr}\) using a strong base (\(\mathrm{alcoholic\ KOH}\)) to generate propene alkene.
2. Regioselective addition of \(\mathrm{HBr}\) across the alkene unsaturation in an anti-Markovnikov manner using organic peroxide (peroxide effect / Kharasch effect).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Sequence
1. 2-Bromopropane is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide, abstracting a \(\beta\)-proton and losing bromide ion (\(\beta\)-elimination).
2. Propene (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2}\)) is collected as the alkene intermediate.
3. Propene is treated with hydrogen bromide in the presence of an organic peroxide.
4. The reaction proceeds via a free-radical chain mechanism, directing the bromine radical to the terminal carbon to give 1-bromopropane as the major product.

Step 4: Check of Continuity
Alkene formation must precede the peroxide-catalyzed addition of \(\mathrm{HBr}\). The logical progression is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

Step 5: Final Answer
The correct sequence of steps is (I) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MCQ_Q01 - Clinical use of chloramphenicol antibiotic

questiontext.text: A chlorine-containing antibiotic produced by microorganisms, which is clinically recognized for its high effectiveness in the treatment of typhoid fever, is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain halogen-containing organic compounds occur in nature and are clinically useful antibiotics synthesized by microorganisms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Compounds
Chloramphenicol is a chlorine-containing broad-spectrum antibiotic produced by soil microbes. In contrast, chloroquine is a synthetic antimalarial, halothane is an inhalation anaesthetic, and thyroxine is an iodine-containing human hormone.

Step 3: Medical Application and Conclusion
Chloramphenicol is specifically indicated and highly effective for the treatment of typhoid fever. Therefore, the chlorine-containing antibiotic used in typhoid treatment is chloramphenicol.

Final Answer:
Chloramphenicol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MCQ_Q02 - Iodine containing hormone and goitre disease

questiontext.text: Which iodine-containing hormone is produced in the human body, the deficiency of which causes the thyroid disease known as goiter?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Biochemical Concept
The human thyroid gland synthesises an iodine-containing hormone essential for regulating cellular metabolic rate.

Step 2: Hormone Identification
The specific iodine-containing hormone produced by the thyroid gland is thyroxine.

Step 3: Deficiency and Disease Check
An inadequate intake of dietary iodine prevents adequate synthesis of thyroxine, resulting in enlargement of the thyroid gland, clinically termed goiter.

Step 4: Conclusion
The hormone whose deficiency causes goiter is thyroxine.

Final Answer:
Thyroxine

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MCQ_Q03 - Synthetic halogen compound used as anaesthetic

questiontext.text: Which synthetic polyhalogenated compound is widely employed as an inhalation anaesthetic during major surgery?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synthetic organic halogen compounds find diverse applications in medicine, including general anaesthesia.

Step 2: Compound Evaluation
Halothane (2-bromo-2-chloro-1,1,1-trifluoroethane) is a volatile, non-flammable liquid halogenated hydrocarbon. Chloroquine is an antimalarial, dichloromethane is an industrial solvent and paint stripper, and Freon-12 is a refrigerant propellant.

Step 3: Clinical Application and Conclusion
Due to its rapid induction and non-explosive properties, halothane is utilized as a surgical inhalation anaesthetic. Thus, the surgical anaesthetic is halothane.

Final Answer:
Halothane

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MCQ_Q04 - Environmental persistence of polyhalogenated organic compounds

questiontext.text: Many halogenated organic compounds persist in the natural environment for exceptionally long periods primarily because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Environmental Principle
The chemical longevity of synthetic chemicals in soil and ecosystems is governed by microbial biodegradability.

Step 2: Evaluation of Carbon-Halogen Stability
The carbon-halogen bonds in polyhalogenated compounds are strong and unfamiliar to enzymatic metabolic pathways of common microorganisms.
