name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Acidity factors and synthetic reactions of carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structure, acidity, and reactions of carboxylic acids:

Statement I: Electron-withdrawing substituents such as \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\) or \(-\mathrm{CF}_3\) stabilize the carboxylate anion through inductive or resonance effects, thereby increasing the acidity of carboxylic acids.

Statement II: Direct attachment of a phenyl group to the carboxylic carbon increases acidity compared to acetic acid because the \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-hybridised aromatic carbon is more electronegative than an \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-hybridised carbon.

Statement III: Treatment of carboxylic acids having an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen with chlorine or bromine in the presence of red phosphorus introduces a halogen exclusively at the \(\alpha\)-position (Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction).

Statement IV: Decarboxylation of sodium salts of carboxylic acids with sodalime (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and \(\mathrm{CaO}\) in a \(3:1\) ratio) yields an alkane having one carbon atom more than the parent carboxylate salt.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों की संरचना, अम्लता और रासायनिक अभिक्रियाओं के संबंध में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\) अथवा \(-\mathrm{CF}_3\) जैसे इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक प्रतिस्थापी प्रेरणिक या अनुनादी प्रभाव द्वारा कार्बोक्सिलेट ऋणायन को स्थायी करते हैं, जिससे कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों की अम्लता बढ़ जाती है।

कथन II: ऐसीटिक अम्ल की तुलना में कार्बोक्सिल कार्बन से सीधे फेनिल समूह का जुड़ना अम्लता को बढ़ाता है क्योंकि \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-संकरित ऐरोमैटिक कार्बन \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-संकरित कार्बन की तुलना में अधिक विद्युत ऋणात्मक होता है।

कथन III: लाल फास्फोरस की उपस्थिति में \(\alpha\)-हाइड्रोजन युक्त कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों की क्लोरीन या ब्रोमीन के साथ अभिक्रिया कराने पर हैलोजन परमाणु केवल \(\alpha\)-स्थिति पर ही प्रवेश करता है (हेल-वोलहार्ड-जेलिंस्की अभिक्रिया)।

कथन IV: सोडालाइम (\(3:1\) अनुपात में \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) और \(\mathrm{CaO}\)) के साथ कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल के सोडियम लवण का विकार्बोक्सिलीकरण कराने पर जनक कार्बोक्सिलेट लवण से एक कार्बन परमाणु अधिक युक्त ऐल्केन प्राप्त होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Effect of Electron-Withdrawing Substituents on Acidity
Acid strength is governed by the relative stability of the conjugate base formed upon deprotonation. In the carboxylate ion, negative charge is distributed over two oxygen atoms. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) such as \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\), \(-\mathrm{CN}\), \(-\mathrm{F}\), and \(-\mathrm{CF}_3\) withdraw electron density through inductive (\(-I\)) and resonance (\(-M\)) effects. This electron withdrawal disperses the negative charge over a larger volume, stabilizing the carboxylate anion and shifting the dissociation equilibrium to the right. Consequently, EWGs significantly decrease \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) and enhance acidity, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Acidity Comparison Between Benzoic Acid and Acetic Acid
In benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOH}\)), the carbonyl carbon is directly bonded to an \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-hybridised carbon of the aromatic ring, whereas in acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}\)), it is attached to an \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-hybridised methyl carbon. Due to \(33.3\%\;\mathrm{s}\)-character compared to \(25\%\;\mathrm{s}\)-character, an \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) carbon has higher electronegativity and exerts an electron-withdrawing inductive effect relative to an \(\mathrm{sp}^3\) carbon. As a result, benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{p}K_a = 4.19\)) is a stronger acid than acetic acid (\(\mathrm{p}K_a = 4.76\)), validating the second proposition.

Step 3: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction Specificity
Carboxylic acids possessing \(\alpha\)-hydrogens react with chlorine or bromine in the presence of a catalytic amount of red phosphorus followed by aqueous workup to yield \(\alpha\)-halocarboxylic acids exclusively. The red phosphorus converts a portion of the acid into acyl halide, which enolizes readily and halogens attack specifically at the \(\alpha\)-carbon. Halogenation does not occur at \(\beta\), \(\gamma\), or other chain positions under these conditions. Hence, the third proposition is chemically accurate.

Step 4: Carbon Count Analysis During Sodalime Decarboxylation
When the dry sodium salt of a carboxylic acid is strongly heated with sodalime (\(\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{CaO}\)), a molecule of carbon dioxide is extruded as sodium carbonate:
\[\mathrm{R-COONa} + \mathrm{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{CaO},\;\Delta} \mathrm{R-H} + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\] The resulting hydrocarbon (\(\mathrm{R-H}\)) contains exactly one carbon atom fewer (descent of the homologous series) than the precursor carboxylate salt, not one carbon atom more. Therefore, the assertion that sodalime decarboxylation yields an alkane with one carbon more is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The principles regarding substituent effects on carboxylate stability, the hybridisation influence in benzoic acid, and the regioselectivity of the HVZ reaction are sound, whereas the description of sodalime decarboxylation incorrectly claims ascending the series instead of descending it.
Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

चरण 1: अम्लता पर इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक प्रतिस्थापियों के प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन
कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल की अम्लता उसके संयुग्मी क्षार (कार्बोक्सिलेट ऋणायन) के स्थायित्व पर निर्भर करती है। \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\) तथा \(-\mathrm{CF}_3\) जैसे प्रबल इलेक्ट्रॉन-अपनयक समूह प्रेरणिक (\(-I\)) और अनुनादी प्रभावों द्वारा ऋणायन के ऋणावेश को विस्थानिकृत करके उसे अत्यधिक स्थायी बनाते हैं। इससे आयनन साम्य दाईं ओर विस्थापित होता है और अम्लता बढ़ती है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: बेन्जोइक अम्ल और ऐसीटिक अम्ल की अम्लता की तुलना
बेन्जोइक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOH}\)) में कार्बोक्सिल समूह बेन्जीन वलय के \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-संकरित कार्बन से जुड़ा होता है, जबकि ऐसीटिक अम्ल में यह \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-संकरित मेथिल कार्बन से जुड़ा होता है। \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) कार्बन में \(s\)-लक्षण अधिक होने के कारण इसकी विद्युत ऋणात्मकता \(\mathrm{sp}^3\) कार्बन से अधिक होती है, जिससे यह इलेक्ट्रॉन आकर्षित करता है। इस कारण बेन्जोइक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{p}K_a = 4.19\)), ऐसीटिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{p}K_a = 4.76\)) से अधिक प्रबल अम्ल होता है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: हेल-वोलहार्ड-जेलिंस्की (HVZ) अभिक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
\(\alpha\)-हाइड्रोजन युक्त कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल लाल फास्फोरस की अल्प मात्रा की उपस्थिति में क्लोरीन या ब्रोमीन के साथ अभिक्रिया करके विशिष्ट रूप से \(\alpha\)-हैलोकार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल बनाते हैं। यह हैलोजनीकरण केवल \(\alpha\)-कार्बन पर ही संपन्न होता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 4: सोडालाइम विकार्बोक्सिलीकरण में कार्बन संख्या का मूल्यांकन
जब कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल के सोडियम लवण को सोडालाइम (\(\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{CaO}\)) के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड सोडियम कार्बोनेट (\(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\)) के रूप में निकल जाती है:
\[\mathrm{R-COONa} + \mathrm{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{CaO},\;\Delta} \mathrm{R-H} + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\] प्राप्त ऐल्केन (\(\mathrm{R-H}\)) में जनक कार्बोक्सिलेट लवण की तुलना में एक कार्बन परमाणु कम होता है (श्रेणी का अवरोहण), न कि एक कार्बन अधिक। अतः चौथा कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
प्रतिस्थापी प्रभाव, संकरण प्रभाव तथा HVZ अभिक्रिया की स्थिति-विशिष्टता से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि सोडालाइम विकार्बोक्सिलीकरण में एक कार्बन बढ़ने का दावा गलत है।
अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect.
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Common names and natural sources of carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Compound)List-II (Natural Source)
A. VanillinI. Meadow sweet
B. SalicylaldehydeII. Vanilla beans
C. CinnamaldehydeIII. Red ants
D. Formic acidIV. Cinnamon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the natural origin of Vanillin
Vanillin is a well-known aromatic aldehyde possessing a pleasant vanilla scent. In nature, it is extracted from vanilla beans. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the natural origin of Salicylaldehyde
Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is naturally occurring and was historically isolated from the meadow sweet plant (Spiraea ulmaria). Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the natural origin of Cinnamaldehyde
Cinnamaldehyde (3-phenylprop-2-enal) is the organic compound that imparts distinctive aroma and flavour to the bark of cinnamon trees. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the natural origin of Formic acid
Formic acid (\(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)), the simplest carboxylic acid, was originally obtained by the destructive distillation of red ants (derived from the Latin word formica meaning ant). Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Common and IUPAC nomenclature of carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Common Name)List-II (IUPAC Name)
A. AcroleinI. Pentanal
B. ValeraldehydeII. Prop-2-enal
C. PhthaldehydeIII. 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one
D. Mesityl oxideIV. Benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Acrolein
Acrolein has the chemical formula \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH\text{-}CHO}\). The principal functional group is an aldehyde located at carbon-1, with an alkene unsaturation at carbon-2 of a three-carbon chain. Therefore, its IUPAC name is Prop-2-enal. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Valeraldehyde
Valeraldehyde is the common name for the unbranched five-carbon saturated aliphatic aldehyde \(\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_3CHO}\). The systematic IUPAC name for this five-carbon aldehyde is Pentanal. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Phthaldehyde
Phthaldehyde comprises a benzene ring bearing two adjacent formyl (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) groups at positions 1 and 2 (\(\mathrm{C_6H_4(CHO)_2}\)). In systematic nomenclature, both aldehyde carbons are treated as substituents on the aromatic ring, giving Benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Mesityl oxide
Mesityl oxide has the structure \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH\text{-}CO\text{-}CH_3}\). Numbering the five-carbon chain to give the ketone carbonyl the lowest locant yields the carbonyl at position 2, a double bond between carbon-3 and carbon-4, and a methyl branch at carbon-4. Thus, its IUPAC name is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Named synthetic reactions and reagents for aldehydes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Named Reaction)List-II (Reagent and Substrate)
A. Rosenmund reductionI. \(\mathrm{SnCl_2 + HCl}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) with nitriles
B. Stephen reactionII. \(\mathrm{H_2 / Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}\) with acyl chlorides
C. Étard reactionIII. \(\mathrm{CO, HCl / \text{Anhyd.} AlCl_3}\) with benzene
D. Gatterman-Koch reactionIV. \(\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2 / CS_2}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) with toluene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Rosenmund reduction
In the Rosenmund reduction, an acyl chloride (acid chloride) is selectively hydrogenated over a poisoned catalyst of palladium supported on barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}\)) to produce the corresponding aldehyde without further reduction to alcohol. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of Stephen reaction
In the Stephen reaction, nitriles are reduced using stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{SnCl_2 + HCl}\)) to give an intermediate iminium salt, which upon subsequent aqueous acid hydrolysis yields an aldehyde. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of Étard reaction
In the Étard reaction, toluene is treated with chromyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}\)) in carbon disulfide or carbon tetrachloride to form a brown chromium complex, which on hydrolysis with water yields benzaldehyde. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of Gatterman-Koch reaction
In the Gatterman-Koch reaction, benzene or an alkylbenzene derivative is formulated directly to benzaldehyde upon treatment with a gaseous mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\)) or cuprous chloride catalyst. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Derivatives of aldehydes and ketones with ammonia derivatives

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagent \(\mathrm{H_2N-Z}\))List-II (Carbonyl Product Class)
A. Hydroxylamine (\(\mathrm{Z = -OH}\))I. Hydrazone
B. Hydrazine (\(\mathrm{Z = -NH_2}\))II. Oxime
C. Semicarbazide (\(\mathrm{Z = -NHCONH_2}\))III. Phenylhydrazone
D. Phenylhydrazine (\(\mathrm{Z = -NHC_6H_5}\))IV. Semicarbazone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the reaction with Hydroxylamine
When aldehydes or ketones react with hydroxylamine (\(\mathrm{NH_2OH}\)), nucleophilic addition followed by elimination of a water molecule yields a condensation product containing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}OH}\) group, termed an oxime. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the reaction with Hydrazine
When aldehydes or ketones react with hydrazine (\(\mathrm{NH_2NH_2}\)), condensation results in elimination of water to form a product bearing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NH_2}\) linkage, known as a hydrazone. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the reaction with Semicarbazide
When aldehydes or ketones condense with semicarbazide (\(\mathrm{NH_2NHCONH_2}\)), only the hydrazine nitrogen (\(-\mathrm{NH_2}\)) acts as the active nucleophile because the amide nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the adjacent carbonyl group. The resulting derivative containing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NHCONH_2}\) moiety is named a semicarbazone. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the reaction with Phenylhydrazine
Reaction of aldehydes or ketones with phenylhydrazine (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NHNH_2}\)) produces crystalline derivatives characterised by the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NHC_6H_5}\) structure, designated as phenylhydrazones. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q05 - Chemical tests and reagents for distinguishing carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagent / Test)List-II (Characteristic Observation)
A. Tollens' reagentI. Red-brown precipitate with aliphatic aldehydes on heating
B. Fehling's reagentII. Shining silver mirror on the clean inner glass wall
C. 2,4-DinitrophenylhydrazineIII. Yellow precipitate with compounds possessing a methyl ketone group
D. Sodium hypoiodite (\(\mathrm{I_2 / NaOH}\))IV. Yellow, orange, or red crystalline precipitate with carbonyl group

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Tollens' test observation
Tollens' reagent is an ammoniacal silver nitrate solution (\([\mathrm{Ag(NH_3)_2}]^+\)). On gentle warming with aldehydes (both aliphatic and aromatic), the aldehyde is oxidised to carboxylate while silver ions are reduced to metallic silver, depositing as a brilliant shining silver mirror on the clean inner wall of the test tube. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Fehling's test observation
Fehling's reagent consists of Fehling solution A (aqueous \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\)) and Fehling solution B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate). On heating with aliphatic aldehydes, cupric ions are reduced to cuprous oxide (\(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\)), depositing as a characteristic red-brown precipitate. Aromatic aldehydes fail to respond to this test. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the 2,4-DNP test observation
2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (Brady's reagent) condenses rapidly with both aldehydes and ketones to produce bright yellow, orange, or red crystalline 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone precipitates. This reaction serves as a universal qualitative test for the presence of the carbonyl functional group. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Sodium hypoiodite test observation
Treatment with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{I_2 + NaOH}\), generating sodium hypoiodite \(\mathrm{NaOI}\)) oxidises compounds containing the \(\mathrm{CH_3\text{-}C=O}\) or \(\mathrm{CH_3\text{-}CH(OH)-}\) unit, precipitating triiodomethane (iodoform, \(\mathrm{CHI_3}\)) as a characteristic yellow crystalline solid. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q06 - Substrates and products of condensation and disproportionation reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reactant System)List-II (Major Product Formed)
A. Ethanal treated with dil. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and heatedI. Benzyl alcohol and Benzoate ion
B. Benzaldehyde treated with conc. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and heatedII. But-2-enal
C. Benzaldehyde + Acetophenone with dil. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at 293 KIII. 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one
D. Propanone treated with \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\) and heatedIV. 1,3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the aldol condensation of Ethanal
Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)) possesses \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. Treatment with dilute sodium hydroxide initiates aldol addition to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol). Subsequent heating causes spontaneous dehydration (loss of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) to yield the conjugated \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde But-2-enal (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CHO}\)). Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Cannizzaro reaction of Benzaldehyde
Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\)) lacks \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. When heated with concentrated alkali (\(50\%\ \mathrm{NaOH}\)), it undergoes self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation via the Cannizzaro reaction). One molecule is reduced to Benzyl alcohol (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}\)) while the other is oxidised to Benzoate ion (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-}\)). Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the cross-aldol condensation between Benzaldehyde and Acetophenone
In this cross-aldol system, acetophenone supplies the enolate nucleophile (as it has \(\alpha\)-hydrogens) which attacks the electrophilic formyl carbonyl of benzaldehyde (which lacks \(\alpha\)-hydrogens). Dehydration of the resulting \(\beta\)-hydroxy ketone produces 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one (commonly known as benzalacetophenone). Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the aldol condensation of Propanone
Propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)) in the presence of barium hydroxide [\(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\)] undergoes aldol addition to give diacetone alcohol (4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one). Subsequent heating eliminates a water molecule to generate the conjugated unsaturated ketone 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (mesityl oxide). Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q07 - Industrial applications of aldehydes ketones and carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Substance)List-II (Industrial / Commercial Use)
A. Formalin (40% aqueous HCHO)I. Industrial manufacture of nylon-6,6 polymer
B. Adipic acid (Hexanedioic acid)II. Preservation of biological specimens
C. Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid)III. Preservative used in packaged food products
D. Sodium benzoateIV. Industrial solvent and table vinegar in food industry

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the application of Formalin
A 40% aqueous solution of methanal (formaldehyde) is known commercially as formalin. It crosslinks cellular proteins and is widely utilised for preserving biological and anatomical specimens, as well as in the manufacture of bakelite. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the application of Adipic acid
Adipic acid (hexanedioic acid, \(\mathrm{HOOC(CH_2)_4COOH}\)) is a straight-chain dicarboxylic acid that undergoes polycondensation with hexamethylenediamine to produce the polyamide fiber nylon-6,6. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the application of Ethanoic acid
Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is produced on a large scale for use as an industrial solvent, in the synthesis of cellulose acetate, and in diluted form (\(5\text{--}8\%\)) as household vinegar in the food processing industry. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the application of Sodium benzoate
Sodium benzoate (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COONa}\)), the sodium salt of benzoic acid, exhibits potent antimicrobial and antifungal action in acidic media and is widely added as a food preservative in beverages, jams, and pickles. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q08 - Acid strength and pKa values of substituted carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Carboxylic Acid)List-II (Approximate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) Value & Rationale)
A. \(\mathrm{CF_3COOH}\)I. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 1.68\); strongly acidic due to powerful \(-I\) effect of nitro group
B. \(\mathrm{NO_2CH_2COOH}\)II. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 0.23\); extremely strong acid due to three electronegative fluorine atoms
C. \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)III. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.76\); weaker acid due to electron-donating \(+I\) effect of methyl group
D. \(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)IV. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 3.75\); intermediate acid lacking an electron-donating alkyl substituent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Trifluoroacetic acid
In trifluoroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{CF_3COOH}\)), three intensely electronegative fluorine atoms exert a potent cumulative electron-withdrawing inductive effect (\(-I\)). This heavily disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate anion, stabilising it to an exceptional degree. Consequently, it is an extremely strong organic acid with a very low \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of approximately 0.23. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nitroacetic acid
In nitroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{NO_2CH_2COOH}\)), the strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group (\(-\mathrm{NO_2}\)) exerts a powerful \(-I\) effect across the single methylene carbon. This significantly enhances carboxylate anion stability relative to unsubstituted acetic acid, giving an approximate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 1.68. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of Acetic acid
In acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)), the methyl group is an electron-releasing substituent through positive inductive effect (\(+I\)). This increases the electron density on the carboxylate group, destabilising the conjugate base and diminishing acidity relative to formic acid, resulting in a higher \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 4.76. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 4: Evaluation of Formic acid
In formic acid (\(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)), only a hydrogen atom is attached directly to the carboxyl group. Because hydrogen does not exert an electron-donating inductive effect like an alkyl group, the formate anion is more stable than the acetate anion, conferring an intermediate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 3.75. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with III, and entry D associates with IV.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q09 - Synthetic routes for the preparation of carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Starting Precursor)List-II (Reagent and Reaction Sequence to Form Acid)
A. Toluene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_3}\))I. Carboxylation using solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) followed by hydronium ion workup
B. Grignard reagent (\(\mathrm{RMgX}\))II. Alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) oxidation under heating followed by acid hydrolysis
C. Primary alcohol (\(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\))III. Stepwise acid or base catalysed hydrolysis via an amide intermediate
D. Nitrile (\(\mathrm{R\text{-}C\equiv N}\))IV. Direct oxidation with Jones reagent (\(\mathrm{CrO_3\text{-}H_2SO_4}\)) in aqueous acetone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the conversion of Toluene to benzoic acid
Primary and secondary alkylbenzenes are vigorously oxidised by heating with alkaline potassium permanganate (\(\mathrm{KMnO_4 / KOH}\)). The entire benzylic aliphatic side chain is cleaved down to potassium benzoate, which upon subsequent acid hydrolysis (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) furnishes benzoic acid. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the conversion of Grignard reagent to carboxylic acid
Grignard reagents (\(\mathrm{RMgX}\)) undergo nucleophilic addition to electrophilic carbon dioxide (solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) or dry ice) in anhydrous ether to form a magnesium halocarboxylate salt. Subsequent protonation with aqueous mineral acid (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) yields a carboxylic acid possessing one more carbon than the alkyl halide. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the oxidation of Primary alcohol to carboxylic acid
Primary aliphatic alcohols (\(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\)) are cleanly oxidised directly to carboxylic acids without isolation of the aldehyde intermediate when treated with Jones reagent (chromium trioxide in dilute aqueous sulphuric acid and acetone, \(\mathrm{CrO_3\text{-}H_2SO_4}\)). Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the hydrolysis of Nitriles to carboxylic acids
Nitriles (\(\mathrm{RCN}\)) contain carbon with a formal oxidation state corresponding to a carboxylic acid derivative. Hydrolysis in the presence of an acid or basic catalyst initially hydrates the triple bond to an intermediate carboxamide (\(\mathrm{RCONH_2}\)), which upon sustained heating with catalyst undergoes complete hydrolysis to produce the carboxylic acid. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q10 - Chemical transformations and reactions of carboxylic acid derivatives

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Reaction)List-II (Reagent Conditions and Distinguishing Feature)
A. Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reactionI. Decarboxylation of alkali metal salt by electrolysis to yield alkane
B. Kolbe electrolytic reactionII. Halogenation at \(\alpha\)-position using \(\mathrm{X_2 / \text{red P}}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)
C. Phthalic acid with excess \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)III. Formation of acyl chloride with escaping gaseous by-products (\(\mathrm{SO_2, HCl}\))
D. Reaction of carboxylic acid with \(\mathrm{SOCl_2}\)IV. Heating gives diamide; strong heating causes cyclisation to phthalimide

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction
Carboxylic acids possessing at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergo selective halogenation exclusively at the \(\alpha\)-position when treated with chlorine or bromine in the presence of catalytic amounts of red phosphorus, followed by aqueous workup. This transformation is known as the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Kolbe electrolytic reaction
When an aqueous solution of a sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid is subjected to electrolysis, anodic oxidation and subsequent decarboxylation produces free alkyl radicals that couple to yield an alkane possessing an even number of carbon atoms. This synthetic process is known as Kolbe electrolysis. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the reaction of Phthalic acid with ammonia
Treating benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid (phthalic acid) with ammonia initially forms ammonium phthalate. Upon mild heating, two moles of water are eliminated to give phthalamide. Sustained strong heating causes intramolecular condensation with elimination of one mole of ammonia gas to yield the cyclic imide, phthalimide. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the reaction with Thionyl chloride
When a carboxylic acid is treated with thionyl chloride (\(\mathrm{SOCl_2}\)), the hydroxyl moiety is substituted by chlorine to yield an acyl chloride. This method is preferred over phosphorus halides because the co-products sulfur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO_2}\)) and hydrogen chloride (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) are both volatile gases that easily escape the reaction vessel, providing the acid chloride in high purity. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q01 - Boiling point order of carbonyls and analogues

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following organic compounds of comparable molecular mass in increasing order of their boiling points:

  1. Butane
  2. Methoxyethane
  3. Propanal
  4. Propan-1-ol

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Compounds and Molecular Masses
The given compounds have comparable molecular masses: Butane (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}\), molar mass \(58\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), Methoxyethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3OCH_2CH_3}\), molar mass \(60\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), Propanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\), molar mass \(58\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), and Propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}\), molar mass \(60\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)).

Step 2: Analysis of Intermolecular Attractive Forces
Boiling point depends directly on the strength of intermolecular forces holding molecules together in the liquid phase: 1. Butane is a non-polar hydrocarbon whose molecules interact only through weak London dispersion (van der Waals) forces. Thus, it has the lowest boiling point (\(\approx 272.5\text{ K}\)).
2. Methoxyethane is an ether with a small net dipole moment, giving rise to weak dipole-dipole attractions. Hence, its boiling point (\(\approx 281\text{ K}\)) is slightly higher than that of butane.
3. Propanal contains a highly polar carbonyl group (\(\mathrm{>C=O}\)) resulting in stronger dipole-dipole interactions than ethers. Consequently, its boiling point (\(\approx 322\text{ K}\)) is noticeably higher than that of methoxyethane.
4. Propan-1-ol possesses a hydroxyl group (\(\mathrm{-OH}\)) capable of forming extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which are significantly stronger than dipole-dipole interactions. Therefore, propan-1-ol has the highest boiling point (\(\approx 370\text{ K}\)).

Step 3: Determination of the Correct Order
Arranging in increasing order of boiling points: Butane < Methoxyethane < Propanal < Propan-1-ol. In Roman numerals, this sequence corresponds to: I < II < III < IV.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct increasing order of boiling points is I < II < III < IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of cyanohydrin formation steps

questiontext.text:
Consider the base-catalyzed addition of hydrogen cyanide (\(\mathrm{HCN}\)) to a carbonyl compound to form a cyanohydrin:

  1. Attack of the cyanide nucleophile (\(\mathrm{CN^-}\)) on the electrophilic carbonyl carbon to form a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate.
  2. Deprotonation of \(\mathrm{HCN}\) by a base to generate the strong nucleophile, cyanide ion (\(\mathrm{CN^-}\)).
  3. Protonation of the tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate by a proton donor to generate the neutral cyanohydrin.

What is the correct chronological sequence of these steps?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of the Reaction and Catalytic Role
Pure hydrogen cyanide is a weak acid and dissociates very slowly to provide cyanide ions. Therefore, the addition of \(\mathrm{HCN}\) to aldehydes and ketones is catalyzed by a base (such as \(\mathrm{OH^-}\)).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Chronological Mechanism
1. In the first step, the added base removes a proton from \(\mathrm{HCN}\) to generate the nucleophilic cyanide ion: \[\mathrm{HCN + OH^- \rightleftharpoons CN^- + H_2O}\] This is statement II.
2. In the second step, the generated cyanide ion (\(\mathrm{CN^-}\)) attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, breaking the carbon-oxygen \(\pi\)-bond and forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate: \[\mathrm{R_2C=O + CN^- \longrightarrow R_2C(CN)-O^-}\] This is statement I.
3. In the third step, the alkoxide intermediate accepts a proton from water (or another molecule of \(\mathrm{HCN}\)) to yield the neutral cyanohydrin and regenerate the base catalyst: \[\mathrm{R_2C(CN)-O^- + H_2O \longrightarrow R_2C(OH)CN + OH^-}\] This is statement III.

Step 3: Synthesis of the Chronological Order
The chronological sequence is statement II followed by statement I and finally statement III: II → I → III.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct chronological sequence of steps is II → I → III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q03 - Reactivity order towards nucleophilic addition reactions

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following carbonyl compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reactions:

  1. Butan-2-one
  2. Propanone
  3. Propanal
  4. Ethanal

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Principles of Nucleophilic Addition Reactivity
The reactivity of aldehydes and ketones towards nucleophilic attack at the carbonyl carbon is governed by two major factors: 1. Electronic factor: Alkyl groups are electron-donating groups due to their inductive (+I) and hyperconjugative effects. They disperse the partial positive charge (\(\delta^+\)) on the carbonyl carbon, thereby decreasing its electrophilicity.
2. Steric factor: Bulky alkyl groups sterically hinder the approach of the incoming nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon, raising the activation energy.

Step 2: Comparison Between Ketones and Aldehydes
Aldehydes have only one alkyl group attached to the carbonyl group, whereas ketones have two. Consequently, aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic additions.

Step 3: Comparing the Individual Compounds
- Between the two ketones, butan-2-one (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_3}\)) has a methyl and an ethyl group, causing greater steric hindrance and a stronger cumulative +I effect than propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)), which has two methyl groups. Thus, butan-2-one is less reactive than propanone.
- Between the two aldehydes, propanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\)) has an ethyl group which is larger and exhibits a stronger +I effect than the methyl group in ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)). Thus, propanal is less reactive than ethanal.

Step 4: Establishment of the Final Increasing Order
Combining these observations gives the increasing reactivity order: Butan-2-one < Propanone < Propanal < Ethanal. In Roman numerals, this sequence corresponds to: I < II < III < IV.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct increasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition is I < II < III < IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q04 - Chronological sequence of aldol condensation elementary steps

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following elementary steps in the correct chronological sequence for the base-catalyzed aldol condensation of ethanal to form but-2-enal:

  1. Nucleophilic attack of the enolate carbanion on the carbonyl carbon of a second ethanal molecule to form an alkoxide intermediate.
  2. Deprotonation of an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen of ethanal by hydroxide ion (\(\mathrm{OH^-}\)) to generate a resonance-stabilized enolate ion.
  3. Elimination of a water molecule upon heating (dehydration) to yield but-2-enal (\(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde).
  4. Protonation of the alkoxide intermediate by water to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol).

What is the correct chronological sequence of these steps?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of Reaction and Substrate
Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)) contains acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. In the presence of dilute base (such as \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)), it undergoes self-aldol condensation followed by dehydration upon heating to yield but-2-enal (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CHO}\)).

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of Elementary Mechanistic Steps
1. Generation of nucleophile: Hydroxide ion abstracts an acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogen from an ethanal molecule to form a resonance-stabilized enolate anion (\(\mathrm{^-CH_2-CHO \leftrightarrow CH_2=CH-O^-}\)). This corresponds to statement II.
2. Nucleophilic addition: The nucleophilic enolate ion attacks the carbonyl carbon of another unreacted ethanal molecule, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide ion. This corresponds to statement I.
3. Proton transfer: The alkoxide intermediate abstracts a proton from water to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol) and regenerates \(\mathrm{OH^-}\). This corresponds to statement IV.
4. Dehydration: Upon heating, 3-hydroxybutanal readily loses a molecule of water via elimination of an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen and \(\beta\)-hydroxyl group to form a conjugated \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde, but-2-enal. This corresponds to statement III.

Step 3: Verification of the Sequence
The chronological order of events is: Deprotonation to form enolate (II) → Nucleophilic addition (I) → Protonation to form aldol (IV) → Dehydration upon heating (III). This sequence corresponds to II → I → IV → III.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct chronological sequence of steps is II → I → IV → III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q05 - Increasing acidity order of haloacetic acids

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following carboxylic acids in increasing order of their acidic strength:

  1. Acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\))
  2. Bromoacetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_2BrCOOH}\))
  3. Chloroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_2ClCOOH}\))
  4. Fluoroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_2FCOOH}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principle of Substituent Effects on Carboxylic Acid Acidity
The strength of a carboxylic acid depends on the stability of its conjugate base, the carboxylate anion (\(\mathrm{RCOO^-}\)). Electron-withdrawing groups (having a \(-I\) inductive effect) disperse the negative charge across the carboxylate moiety, thereby stabilizing the anion and increasing the acidity of the parent carboxylic acid.

Step 2: Comparison of Inductive Effects of Halogen Substituents
In the given haloacetic acids, each halogen is attached to the \(\alpha\)-carbon. The magnitude of the \(-I\) effect depends directly on the electronegativity of the halogen atom: Electronegativity decreases in the order: \[\mathrm{F > Cl > Br > H}\] Consequently, the electron-withdrawing power of the substituents decreases in the same order: \[\mathrm{-F > -Cl > -Br > -H}\]

Step 3: Stabilization of the Carboxylate Anion and Acid Strength
- Acetic acid lacks an electron-withdrawing halogen; the methyl group has a slight electron-donating (+I) effect, making it the weakest acid in the series (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.76\)).
- Bromoacetic acid experiences a moderate \(-I\) effect from bromine, stabilizing the conjugate base (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 2.90\)).
- Chloroacetic acid experiences a stronger \(-I\) effect from chlorine due to higher electronegativity (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 2.87\)).
- Fluoroacetic acid has the most electronegative halogen (fluorine), exerting the strongest \(-I\) effect and resulting in the greatest stabilization of the conjugate base (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 2.59\)).

Step 4: Establishment of the Final Order
Arranging in increasing order of acid strength: Acetic acid < Bromoacetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Fluoroacetic acid. In Roman numerals, this sequence corresponds to: I < II < III < IV.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct increasing order of acidic strength is I < II < III < IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q06 - Chronological synthetic sequence for m-nitrobenzoic acid

questiontext.text:
Consider the synthesis of m-nitrobenzoic acid starting from benzene. Arrange the following synthetic steps in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Nitration using a mixture of concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) and concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).
  2. Friedel-Crafts alkylation with chloromethane in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) to produce toluene.
  3. Oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) followed by acidic workup to convert the methyl group into a carboxyl group.

What is the correct chronological sequence to successfully obtain m-nitrobenzoic acid as the major product?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Synthetic Strategy and Regiochemical Requirements
The target molecule is m-nitrobenzoic acid, where the nitro group (\(\mathrm{-NO_2}\)) and the carboxylic acid group (\(\mathrm{-COOH}\)) are positioned meta to each other on the benzene ring.
The methyl group (\(\mathrm{-CH_3}\)) is an ortho/para-directing activator. If nitration is performed on toluene, the primary products will be o-nitrotoluene and p-nitrotoluene, not the meta-isomer.
In contrast, the carboxyl group (\(\mathrm{-COOH}\)) is a strongly deactivating and meta-directing group. Therefore, the carboxyl group must be established on the ring prior to nitration to direct the incoming nitro group to the meta position.

Step 2: Sequence of Transformations
1. First Step (Statement II): Benzene undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation with \(\mathrm{CH_3Cl}\) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) to yield toluene: \[\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3Cl \xrightarrow{\text{anh. } AlCl_3} C_6H_5CH_3 + HCl}\] 2. Second Step (Statement III): Toluene is oxidized using hot alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) followed by acidification with dilute acid to produce benzoic acid: \[\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_3 \xrightarrow[2.\; H_3O^+]{1.\; KMnO_4 / KOH,\; \Delta} C_6H_5COOH}\] 3. Third Step (Statement I): Benzoic acid contains the meta-directing \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) group. Electrophilic aromatic nitration with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) in the presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) directs the nitro group to the meta position, selectively forming m-nitrobenzoic acid: \[\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } HNO_3 + \text{conc. } H_2SO_4} m\text{-O}_2\text{N-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-COOH}}\]

Step 3: Verification of the Sequence
The correct sequence is Friedel-Crafts alkylation (II), followed by side-chain oxidation (III), and finally electrophilic nitration (I): II → III → I.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct chronological sequence of steps is II → III → I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q07 - Elementary step sequence in acid-catalyzed Fischer esterification

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following elementary steps in the correct chronological sequence for the acid-catalyzed Fischer esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol to form ethyl ethanoate:

  1. Elimination of a water molecule from the protonated tetrahedral intermediate with simultaneous reformation of the carbon-oxygen double bond.
  2. Proton transfer within the tetrahedral intermediate converting a hydroxyl group into a good leaving group (\(\mathrm{-OH_2^+}\)).
  3. Deprotonation of the carbonyl-oxygen-protonated ester species to yield the neutral ester product and regenerate the acid catalyst.
  4. Protonation of the carbonyl oxygen atom of ethanoic acid by an acid catalyst.
  5. Nucleophilic attack of the neutral ethanol molecule on the protonated carbonyl carbon to form a tetrahedral intermediate.

What is the correct chronological sequence of these steps?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of Fischer Esterification
The acid-catalyzed reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol proceeds via a nucleophilic acyl substitution pathway involving a tetrahedral intermediate.

Step 2: Analysis of the Elementary Steps in Chronological Order
1. Activation of the carbonyl group: The acid catalyst protonates the carbonyl oxygen of the carboxylic acid. This resonance-stabilizes the cation and significantly increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. This is statement IV.
2. Nucleophilic attack: The oxygen atom of a neutral alcohol molecule (ethanol) attacks the activated carbonyl carbon, yielding a tetrahedral oxonium intermediate. This is statement V.
3. Proton transfer: An intra- or intermolecular proton shift transfers a proton from the oxonium oxygen to one of the basic hydroxyl oxygen atoms, converting a poor leaving group (\(\mathrm{-OH}\)) into a good leaving group (\(\mathrm{-OH_2^+}\)). This is statement II.
4. Elimination of water: The non-bonded electron pair on the remaining hydroxyl oxygen assists in expelling the water molecule, reforming a resonance-stabilized protonated ester species. This is statement I.
5. Regeneration of catalyst: A base (such as water or another alcohol molecule) abstracts the proton from the carbonyl oxygen of the protonated ester, yielding the neutral ethyl ethanoate and regenerating the \(\mathrm{H^+}\) catalyst. This is statement III.

Step 3: Assembling the Complete Sequence
The full chronological order of mechanistic steps is: Protonation of carbonyl oxygen (IV) → Nucleophilic attack by alcohol (V) → Proton transfer (II) → Elimination of water (I) → Deprotonation to neutral ester (III). This sequence corresponds to: IV → V → II → I → III.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct chronological sequence of steps is IV → V → II → I → III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q08 - Acidity ordering of substituted benzoic acid derivatives

questiontext.text:
Consider the following substituted aromatic carboxylic acids:

  1. 4-Methoxybenzoic acid
  2. Benzoic acid
  3. 4-Nitrobenzoic acid
  4. 3,4-Dinitrobenzoic acid

Arrange these carboxylic acids in increasing order of their acidic strength.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Electronic Principles in Aromatic Acids
The acidic strength of substituted benzoic acids depends on the electronic nature of the substituents attached to the benzene ring: 1. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) such as \(\mathrm{-NO_2}\) (which exert both strong \(-I\) and \(-R\) effects) withdraw electron density from the benzene ring and the carboxylate group, thereby stabilizing the conjugate carboxylate anion (\(\mathrm{ArCOO^-}\)) and increasing acid strength.
2. Electron-donating groups (EDGs) such as \(\mathrm{-OCH_3}\) donate electron density into the aromatic ring by resonance (\(+R\) effect) when positioned at the ortho or para positions. This destabilizes the conjugate carboxylate anion and decreases acid strength compared to unsubstituted benzoic acid.

Step 2: Detailed Evaluation of Each Compound
- 4-Methoxybenzoic acid (I): The methoxy group at the para position donates electron density into the ring through resonance (\(+R > -I\)), destabilizing the carboxylate anion. As a result, its acidity is weaker than that of benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.47\)).
- Benzoic acid (II): Possesses no additional ring substituents and serves as the baseline reference (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.19\)).
- 4-Nitrobenzoic acid (III): The nitro group at the para position exerts both a powerful \(-R\) mesomeric effect and a \(-I\) inductive effect, strongly stabilizing the carboxylate anion and increasing acidity (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 3.44\)).
- 3,4-Dinitrobenzoic acid (IV): Contains two strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups. The para-nitro group exerts both \(-R\) and \(-I\) effects, while the meta-nitro group contributes an additional strong \(-I\) inductive effect. The cumulative electron withdrawal provides the greatest stabilization of the conjugate base, making it the most acidic in the series (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 2.82\)).

Step 3: Establishment of the Relative Acidity Sequence
Arranging from weakest acid to strongest acid gives: 4-Methoxybenzoic acid < Benzoic acid < 4-Nitrobenzoic acid < 3,4-Dinitrobenzoic acid. In Roman numerals, this sequence is: I < II < III < IV.

Final Conceptual Answer: The correct increasing order of acidic strength is I < II < III < IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Hybridisation and geometry of carbonyl carbon

questiontext.text: What are the hybridisation state of the carbonyl carbon atom and the approximate bond angles around it in aldehydes and ketones?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Orbital Analysis
The carbonyl carbon forms three \(\sigma\) bonds and one \(\pi\) bond. Formation of three \(\sigma\) bonds requires three hybrid orbitals, resulting in \(sp^2\) hybridisation.

Step 2: Geometry and Bond Angles
The three \(sp^2\) hybrid orbitals lie in a single plane directed towards the corners of an equilateral triangle. Therefore, the geometry is trigonal coplanar and the bond angles are approximately \(120^\circ\).

Final Answer:
The carbonyl carbon is \(sp^2\)-hybridised with bond angles of approximately \(120^\circ\).

answer.text: \(sp^2\) hybridised with bond angles of approximately \(120^\circ\)
\(sp^3\) hybridised with bond angles of approximately \(109.5^\circ\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Polarity and reactive centres of the carbonyl group

questiontext.text: Which statement accurately describes the electronic nature and polarity of the carbonyl group \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Electronegativity Difference
Oxygen is significantly more electronegative than carbon, which causes the \(\pi\)-electron pair of the \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) bond to be displaced towards oxygen.

Step 2: Charge Distribution and Reactive Centres
This unequal sharing creates a partial positive charge on carbon and a partial negative charge on oxygen. Consequently, the carbonyl carbon acts as an electrophilic centre (Lewis acid) and the carbonyl oxygen acts as a nucleophilic centre (Lewis base).

Final Answer:
The carbonyl carbon is an electrophilic centre while the carbonyl oxygen is a nucleophilic centre due to bond polarisation.

answer.text: Carbon is a nucleophilic centre and oxygen is an electrophilic centre
Carbon is an electrophilic centre and oxygen is a nucleophilic centre
Both carbon and oxygen atoms act exclusively as nucleophilic centres
The bond is completely non-polar because of symmetry in planar arrangement

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - IUPAC nomenclature of propane-1,2,3-tricarbaldehyde

questiontext.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \(\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CHO})-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHO}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of Functional Groups and Rule
The molecule possesses three aldehyde (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) groups attached directly to a three-carbon saturated aliphatic chain.

Step 2: Application of IUPAC Nomenclature Rules
To accord identical treatment to all three aldehydic functional groups, the carbon atoms of the \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) groups are not included in the principal carbon chain. The three-carbon parent chain is propane, and the suffix tricarbaldehyde is used.

Step 3: Position Numbering and Name Assembly
The three \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) groups are located at positions 1, 2, and 3 of the propane chain, giving the systematic IUPAC name Propane-1,2,3-tricarbaldehyde.

Final Answer:
Propane-1,2,3-tricarbaldehyde is the correct IUPAC name.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - IUPAC nomenclature of mesityl oxide

questiontext.text: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the compound commonly known as mesityl oxide, having the structure \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Longest Chain and Principal Functional Group
The principal functional group is the ketone group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)), which receives numbering preference over the carbon-carbon double bond.

Step 2: Numbering the Parent Chain
Numbering starts from the end nearer to the carbonyl carbon: carbon-1 is \(\mathrm{CH}_3\), carbon-2 is the carbonyl group, carbon-3 is \(=\mathrm{CH}-\), carbon-4 is \(=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\), and carbon-5 is the terminal methyl carbon.

Step 3: Substituents and Suffix Assignment
A methyl substituent is located at carbon-4. The double bond begins at carbon-3, and the ketone suffix '-2-one' applies to carbon-2. Combining these yields 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one.

Final Answer:
The systematic IUPAC name of mesityl oxide is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - IUPAC nomenclature of 3-oxopentanal

questiontext.text: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the compound \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHO}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Functional Group Priority
The compound contains both an aldehyde group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) and a keto group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)). In IUPAC nomenclature priority, the aldehyde group takes precedence over the ketone group.

Step 2: Numbering the Chain
The chain is numbered starting with the aldehydic carbon as carbon-1: carbon-1 is \(-\mathrm{CHO}\), carbon-2 is \(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\), carbon-3 is \(-\mathrm{CO}-\), carbon-4 is \(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\), and carbon-5 is \(-\mathrm{CH}_3\).

Step 3: Prefix Assignment and Naming
The parent five-carbon aldehyde is pentanal. The keto oxygen at carbon-3 is designated by the prefix '3-oxo', giving 3-Oxopentanal.

Final Answer:
The IUPAC name of the compound is 3-Oxopentanal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Natural sources of aromatic fragrant aldehydes

questiontext.text: Which aromatic aldehyde is naturally obtained from vanilla beans and imparts a pleasant fragrance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall of Natural Carbonyl Sources
Aldehydes and ketones are widespread in plants and nature where they contribute pleasant flavours and fragrances.

Step 2: Specific Natural Sources
Vanillin is extracted from vanilla beans, salicylaldehyde is obtained from meadow sweet, and cinnamaldehyde is extracted from cinnamon bark.

Final Answer:
Vanillin is the aromatic aldehyde obtained from vanilla beans.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - Catalyst in Rosenmund reduction of acyl chloride

questiontext.text: In the Rosenmund reduction, an acyl chloride is selectively hydrogenated to an aldehyde using which catalytic system?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction Definition
The Rosenmund reduction converts an acid chloride (acyl chloride) into the corresponding aldehyde by catalytic hydrogenation.

Step 2: Reagent Specifics
Hydrogenation is carried out over palladium catalyst supported on barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{Pd}-\mathrm{BaSO}_4\)), where barium sulphate acts as a catalyst poison to prevent further reduction of the aldehyde to an alcohol.

Final Answer:
The catalyst system is palladium supported on barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{Pd}-\mathrm{BaSO}_4\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - Reagents and intermediate in Stephen reaction

questiontext.text: In the Stephen reaction, nitriles are reduced to aldehydes. What reagents and intermediate functional group are involved in this transformation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reduction Step
Nitriles (\(\mathrm{RCN}\)) are treated with stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{SnCl}_2 + \mathrm{HCl}\)).

Step 2: Intermediate Formation
This reduction converts the nitrile group into an aldimine hydrochloride intermediate having the general formula \(\mathrm{RCH}=\mathrm{NH}\cdot\mathrm{HCl}\).

Step 3: Hydrolysis Step
Subsequent hydrolysis of the imine intermediate with water yields the corresponding aldehyde (\(\mathrm{RCHO}\)).

Final Answer:
The reduction uses \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2 + \mathrm{HCl}\) to form an imine intermediate, which on hydrolysis yields the aldehyde.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q09 - Selective reduction of unsaturated nitriles by DIBAL-H

questiontext.text: What is the major product obtained when \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CN}\) is treated with diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H) at low temperature followed by hydrolysis with water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Selectivity of DIBAL-H
Diisobutylaluminium hydride, \(\mathrm{AlH}(i\text{-}\mathrm{Bu})_2\), selectively reduces nitrile groups to imines without attacking unconjugated or conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds.

Step 2: Hydrolysis Step
Hydrolysis of the resulting imine intermediate converts it into an aldehyde functional group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)).

Step 3: Product Determination
The carbon chain and the \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) double bond remain intact: \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHO}\) is formed.

Final Answer:
The product is \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHO}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q10 - Etard reaction chromium complex and product

questiontext.text: In the Etard reaction, oxidation of toluene with chromyl chloride in carbon disulphide yields a brown chromium complex. What is the structure of this complex and the final product after hydrolysis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reagent and Reaction Conditions
Chromyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CrO}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\)) in a non-polar solvent such as \(\mathrm{CS}_2\) or \(\mathrm{CCl}_4\) oxidises the methyl group of toluene.

Step 2: Chromium Complex Intermediate
The oxidation stops at an intermediate brown chromium complex having the formula \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCrOHCl}_2)_2\).

Step 3: Hydrolysis to Benzaldehyde
Subsequent aqueous acid hydrolysis of this complex breaks the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Cr}\) bonds to afford benzaldehyde.

Final Answer:
The intermediate is \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCrOHCl}_2)_2\) which hydrolyses to benzaldehyde.

answer.text: The complex is \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CrO}_2\mathrm{Cl}\) and yields benzoic acid
The complex is \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OCrCl}_3\) and yields benzyl alcohol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q11 - Oxidation of toluene with chromic oxide in acetic anhydride

questiontext.text: When toluene is treated with chromic oxide (\(\mathrm{CrO}_3\)) in acetic anhydride at 273–283 K, an intermediate is isolated that yields benzaldehyde upon acidic hydrolysis. What is the structure of this intermediate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction Purpose
To prevent over-oxidation of toluene directly to benzoic acid, the methyl group is converted into an intermediate that is resistant to further oxidation under the reaction conditions.

Step 2: Formation of the Gem-Diacetate
Chromic oxide in acetic anhydride converts the methyl group of toluene into a gem-diacetate, specifically benzylidene diacetate, \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCOCH}_3)_2\).

Step 3: Subsequent Hydrolysis
Upon heating with aqueous acid, the gem-diacetate readily hydrolyses to release benzaldehyde and two molecules of acetic acid.

Final Answer:
The intermediate is benzylidene diacetate, \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCOCH}_3)_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q12 - Commercial preparation of benzaldehyde by chlorination

questiontext.text: In the commercial preparation of benzaldehyde from toluene, what intermediate is obtained by side-chain chlorination before hydrolysis at 373 K?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Side-Chain Radical Chlorination
Controlled side-chain chlorination of boiling toluene in the presence of light (\(h\nu\)) replaces two benzylic hydrogen atoms by chlorine atoms.

Step 2: Intermediate Formation
This selectively forms benzal chloride (benzylene chloride, \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHCl}_2\)).

Step 3: Hydrolysis Step
Hydrolysis of benzal chloride with water at 373 K replaces the two chlorine atoms with an unstable gem-diol that spontaneously loses water to produce benzaldehyde.

Final Answer:
The intermediate is benzal chloride, \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHCl}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q13 - Gatterman-Koch formylation of benzene

questiontext.text: Which mixture of gases and catalysts is employed in the Gatterman-Koch reaction to convert benzene directly into benzaldehyde?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction Principle
The Gatterman-Koch reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution that introduces a formyl group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) onto an aromatic ring.

Step 2: Reagents Involved
Benzene is treated with carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)) and hydrogen chloride (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\)) or cuprous chloride (\(\mathrm{CuCl}\)) as catalyst.

Step 3: Product Formed
The formylating species generates benzaldehyde as the sole aromatic carbonyl product.

Final Answer:
The reaction utilizes \(\mathrm{CO} + \mathrm{HCl}\) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\) or \(\mathrm{CuCl}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q14 - Preparation of ketones using dialkylcadmium

questiontext.text: Why is dialkylcadmium (\(\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{Cd}\)) preferred over Grignard reagents (\(\mathrm{RMgX}\)) for the preparation of ketones from acyl chlorides?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reactivity of Organometallic Reagents
Grignard reagents are highly reactive nucleophiles. When an acyl chloride reacts with a Grignard reagent, the ketone formed initially is more reactive than the ester or acyl halide towards further nucleophilic addition, resulting in tertiary alcohols as the final product.

Step 2: Moderated Reactivity of Cadmium Reagents
Dialkylcadmium reagents are less nucleophilic and less reactive than Grignard reagents due to lower electropositive character of cadmium. They readily displace the chloride of acyl chlorides but do not add across the carbonyl group of the resulting ketone, allowing the reaction to stop cleanly at the ketone stage.

Final Answer:
Dialkylcadmium is less reactive than Grignard reagents and does not add further to the formed ketone.

answer.text: Dialkylcadmium acts as an oxidising agent rather than a nucleophile
Dialkylcadmium is less nucleophilic and does not add further to the formed ketone
Dialkylcadmium forms an unreactive enolate that precipitates out immediately

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q15 - Reaction of propanenitrile with phenylmagnesium bromide

questiontext.text: What is the final product formed when propanenitrile (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CN}\)) is treated with phenylmagnesium bromide in dry ether, followed by aqueous acid hydrolysis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nucleophilic Attack on Nitrile
The phenyl group from phenylmagnesium bromide (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{MgBr}\)) acts as a carbanion nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of propanenitrile (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{N}\)).

Step 2: Formation of Magnesium Salt Intermediate
The addition produces an imine magnesium halide salt intermediate: \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)=\mathrm{NMgBr}\).

Step 3: Acid Hydrolysis
Upon subsequent aqueous acid hydrolysis (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+\)), the imine linkage is hydrolysed to a carbonyl group, yielding 1-phenylpropan-1-one (propiophenone) along with basic magnesium salt and ammonium ions.

Final Answer:
The product obtained is 1-phenylpropan-1-one (propiophenone).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q16 - Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with propanoyl chloride

questiontext.text: What is the product obtained when benzene is treated with propanoyl chloride (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCl}\)) in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Electrophile Generation
Anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\)) abstracts the chloride ion from propanoyl chloride (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCl}\)) to generate the resonance-stabilised propanoyl cation (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C}^+=\mathrm{O}\)).

Step 2: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
The propanoyl cation attacks the aromatic ring of benzene via electrophilic aromatic substitution, forming an arenium ion intermediate.

Step 3: Aromatisation and Product Formation
Loss of a proton regenerates aromaticity, affording 1-phenylpropan-1-one (propiophenone) as the ketone product.

Final Answer:
The product is 1-phenylpropan-1-one (propiophenone).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q17 - Boiling point trends among compounds of comparable molecular mass

questiontext.text: Consider five compounds with comparable molecular masses (58 to 60 g/mol): \(n\)-butane (58), methoxyethane (60), propanal (58), acetone (58), and propan-1-ol (60). What is the correct order of increasing boiling points?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Hydrocarbon and Ether Intermolecular Forces
\(n\)-Butane is non-polar and held only by weak London dispersion forces, giving it the lowest boiling point (273 K). Methoxyethane possesses a weak dipole moment from the ether linkage, resulting in weak dipole-dipole attractions (281 K).

Step 2: Carbonyl Compounds Dipole-Dipole Association
Propanal (322 K) and acetone (329 K) contain polar carbonyl groups with substantial permanent dipole moments leading to stronger dipole-dipole interactions. Acetone boils slightly higher than propanal due to two electron-releasing methyl groups enhancing polarity.

Step 3: Alcohol Hydrogen Bonding
Propan-1-ol (370 K) contains an \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group capable of forming extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which is much stronger than dipole-dipole forces, giving it the highest boiling point.

Final Answer:
The correct increasing order of boiling points is \(n\)-butane < methoxyethane < propanal < acetone < propan-1-ol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q18 - Solubility of lower aldehydes and ketones in water

questiontext.text: Why are the lowest members of aldehydes and ketones, such as methanal, ethanal, and propanone, miscible with water in all proportions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Interaction with Water Molecules
Water possesses polar \(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds with positively polarised hydrogen atoms. The oxygen atom of the carbonyl group has two lone pairs of electrons and a partial negative charge.

Step 2: Hydrogen Bonding Capacity
These lower carbonyl compounds are capable of forming intermolecular hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen and water molecules. As alkyl chain length increases, the hydrophobic effect of the non-polar hydrocarbon tail predominates, causing solubility to diminish rapidly.

Final Answer:
They form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water molecules through their carbonyl oxygen atoms.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q19 - Geometric and orbital changes during nucleophilic addition

questiontext.text: During the nucleophilic addition reaction to a carbonyl group, what change in hybridisation and geometry occurs at the carbonyl carbon atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Initial State
The unreacted carbonyl carbon is \(sp^2\)-hybridised with a trigonal planar geometry lying in a single plane.

Step 2: Attack by the Nucleophile
The nucleophile approaches the carbonyl carbon from a direction approximately perpendicular to the plane of \(sp^2\) hybridised orbitals.

Step 3: Hybridisation Transition and Intermediate
As the nucleophile forms a new \(\sigma\) bond, the \(\pi\) bond breaks and the electron pair shifts to oxygen. The hybridisation of the carbon changes from \(sp^2\) to \(sp^3\), producing a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate.

Final Answer:
The hybridisation changes from \(sp^2\) to \(sp^3\), and the planar geometry converts into a tetrahedral intermediate.

answer.text: From \(sp^3\) to \(sp^2\), with geometry changing from tetrahedral to planar
From \(sp\) to \(sp^2\), with geometry changing from linear to trigonal planar

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q20 - Order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition

questiontext.text: What is the correct increasing order of reactivity of the following carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition reactions: butanone, propanone, propanal, and ethanal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Steric Factors
Aldehydes have only one alkyl group and a small hydrogen atom attached to the carbonyl carbon, presenting much less steric hindrance to an approaching nucleophile compared to ketones which bear two bulky alkyl groups.

Step 2: Electronic Factors
Alkyl groups are electron-donating via inductive effect (\(+I\)), which reduces the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Two alkyl groups in ketones diminish the positive charge more substantially than a single alkyl group in aldehydes.

Step 3: Comparison within Series
Between ethanal and propanal, the smaller methyl group in ethanal causes less steric hindrance and weaker inductive donation than the ethyl group in propanal. Between propanone and butanone, propanone has two methyl groups whereas butanone has a methyl and an ethyl group, making butanone more hindered and least reactive.

Final Answer:
The reactivity increases in the order: butanone < propanone < propanal < ethanal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q21 - Role of base catalyst in addition of HCN

questiontext.text: Why is the addition of hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to aldehydes and ketones typically catalysed by a base?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Weak Acidity of HCN
Pure hydrogen cyanide is a very weak acid with a low degree of dissociation, meaning the concentration of free cyanide ion (\(\mathrm{CN}^-\)) in pure \(\mathrm{HCN}\) is extremely low.

Step 2: Base-Assisted Generation of Strong Nucleophile
A base deprotonates \(\mathrm{HCN}\) (\(\mathrm{HCN} + \mathrm{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons :\mathrm{CN}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)), generating a high concentration of cyanide ion.

Step 3: Nucleophilic Addition
The generated cyanide ion is a much stronger nucleophile than neutral \(\mathrm{HCN}\) and readily attacks the carbonyl carbon to form cyanohydrin.

Final Answer:
The base deprotonates HCN to generate the strongly nucleophilic cyanide ion (\(:\mathrm{CN}^-\)).

answer.text: The base deprotonates HCN to generate the strongly nucleophilic cyanide ion (\(:\mathrm{CN}^-\))

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q22 - Addition of sodium hydrogensulphite to carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text: Which feature makes the formation of sodium hydrogensulphite (\(\mathrm{NaHSO}_3\)) addition compounds particularly useful in organic chemistry?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formation of Crystalline Addition Compound
Aldehydes and methyl ketones react with saturated aqueous sodium hydrogensulphite to form water-soluble, crystalline bisulphite addition products.

Step 2: Reversibility and Practical Utility
The position of equilibrium lies largely to the right for aldehydes. More importantly, the crystalline adduct can be regenerated back into the pure original carbonyl compound by treatment with dilute mineral acid or aqueous alkali.

Step 3: Application
Because non-carbonyl impurities do not form these adducts, this reversible reaction is widely used for the separation and purification of aldehydes.

Final Answer:
The crystalline adducts are water-soluble and can be converted back into the parent carbonyl compound by treatment with dilute acid or alkali.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q23 - Catalysis and intermediates in acetal formation

questiontext.text: When an aldehyde reacts with two equivalents of a monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride gas, what sequence of products is formed?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Dry HCl Catalyst
Dry hydrogen chloride gas protonates the carbonyl oxygen atom, greatly enhancing the electrophilic character of the carbonyl carbon towards nucleophilic attack by the alcohol.

Step 2: First Equivalent of Alcohol
Addition of one equivalent of alcohol generates an alkoxyalcohol intermediate known as a hemiacetal.

Step 3: Second Equivalent of Alcohol
In the presence of acid, the hemiacetal hydroxyl group undergoes protonation, loss of water, and attack by a second molecule of alcohol to give a gem-dialkoxy compound termed an acetal.

Final Answer:
The aldehyde first forms a hemiacetal intermediate, which reacts further to yield an acetal.
